finding.fix: Set `anchor` to the outermost group's id after the loop (e.g., `let anchor = nested.id;` after the loop) and ensure the insertion operation actually adds the new group as a child of that group, or otherwise construct a scenario where the insertion would exceed MAX_GROUP_DEPTH.

note: Adding a group above the deepest leaf adds one level; MAX_DEPTH + 1 is correctly rejected.

finding.summary: GPU/CPU pixel comparison uses zip, so it silently truncates to the shorter buffer and can pass even if the GPU output length differs from the CPU reference.
finding.evidence: cpu.px.iter().zip(&gpu) only iterates min(cpu.px.len(), gpu.len()) elements. If render_to_vec returns too few or too many pixels, the missing/extra pixels are ignored and the assertion at line 43 may still pass.
finding.fix: Assert cpu.px.len() == gpu.len() before the comparison or use a full-length comparison that fails on length mismatch.

note: Added explicit CPU/GPU pixel-count equality before zip, so an empty/truncated GPU result cannot pass the comparison.

finding.summary: Unchecked indexing into layout.styles by d.style can cause a panic if the decoration style index is invalid.
finding.evidence: Line 184 directly uses layout.styles[d.style as usize] without bounds check, unlike the glyph loop above which uses .get(). A malformed text document or corrupted style index could yield an out-of-range d.style, causing an index-out-of-bounds panic.
finding.fix: Replace with `let style = layout.styles.get(d.style as usize).ok_or_else(|| error("invalid decoration style"))?;` and use `style.color`.

note: Decoration style indices originate in validated internal text layout; external input cannot inject a Layout with arbitrary indices.

finding.summary: preview command serializes every shape path in the entire document into JSON, causing large allocations and UI blocking on each interactive preview.
finding.evidence: The json! macro builds a vector of all shape paths by walking the whole document: `doc.walk().into_iter().filter_map(...)` clones every path. For large documents this is O(total path data) and runs on every preview call.
finding.fix: Return only the edited groups' paths or use a more efficient/compressed representation; avoid serializing unchanged shapes.

note: The automation command returns projected paths by contract; the production UI uses the detached document directly and does not serialize JSON per pointer frame.

finding.summary: set command performs full projection and cache rendering solely for validation, then discards the result, making envelope commit unnecessarily slow.
finding.evidence: `let _prepared = prepare(&source, &c, true)?;` invokes `prepare`, which evaluates geometry, compiles appearances, and renders caches for all edits. The result is unused. This heavy work is duplicated from prior preview calls.
finding.fix: Replace with a lightweight validation that does not render caches, or reuse cached data from a preview if available.

note: Cache preparation validates every target before the single native publication; callers need not have run a prior preview.

finding.summary: preview_document projects and renders all other committed envelopes on every preview call, causing repeated full re-renders of unchanged groups.
finding.evidence: Line 317 calls `project_document(&background)`, which iterates all live envelopes and performs full `prepare` (including cache rendering). These caches are not needed for the final JSON output and the work is repeated each time the preview command is invoked.
finding.fix: Only project the edited groups; for other envelopes, skip cache rendering or reuse cached projections.

note: Other live envelopes must be projected for the detached preview; the shared UI caches warm document projection by source Arc and revision.

finding.summary: Test does not assert that the command returns an error, allowing the test to pass even when the expected error is not produced
finding.evidence: The code only enters the `if let Err(e) = result` block when `result` is `Err`. If `result` is `Ok`, no assertions are executed and the test passes silently, despite the test name indicating that missing schema should be explicitly rejected.
finding.fix: Add an explicit assertion that `result` is an error before the `if let`, e.g., `assert!(result.is_err(), "expected missing schema error");` or restructure to match on `result` and assert the error case unconditionally.

note: Mesh command regression now unconditionally requires native schema success, stored data, undo and no direct-handler journal entry; focused regression passes.

finding.summary: Arc::ptr_eq comparison with a clone of the same Arc is always true and does not verify that the document content was unchanged during preview.
finding.evidence: `let before = s.active().unwrap().doc.clone();` clones the Arc pointer. `Arc::ptr_eq(&s.active().unwrap().doc, &before)` compares the Arc allocation pointer, which is identical for a clone, so the assertion is trivially true even if the underlying document is mutated.
finding.fix: Compare the document contents instead, e.g. `assert_eq!(s.active().unwrap().doc, before);` or `assert_eq!(*s.active().unwrap().doc, *before);`

note: Arc<Document> snapshots are immutable; writes use copy-on-write, so pointer identity detects publication rather than hiding mutation.

finding.summary: The conditional `if evaluator::write_spec(...).is_err()` skips the entire error-handling test block when the spec can be written, allowing the test to pass vacuously.
finding.evidence: All assertions for the fail-closed behavior (Action::Make error, document unchanged, empty journal, no undo) are inside this `if`. If `write_spec` returns `Ok`, the block is skipped and the test passes without verifying the intended error handling.
finding.fix: Unconditionally assert that `write_spec` returns `Err` or restructure the test so the error path is always executed, using a deterministic setup that forces the missing-data condition.

note: Live Paint tests now require available native schema success and separately test an invalid empty graph; focused regression passes.

finding.summary: User-supplied rows/cols in Options are not validated before Mesh::regular; zero or one may cause panic or invalid mesh.
finding.evidence: Options is deserialized with serde, allowing explicit values like rows:0 or cols:1. Gesture::begin_with passes these directly to Mesh::regular without checking. MeshData::validate only checks points.len() > 2601, not row/col bounds. A rows=0 or cols=0 can lead to division by zero, empty mesh, or panic inside Mesh::regular (e.g., interpolation calculations).
finding.fix: Add validation in Gesture::begin_with or Options deserialization to require rows >= 2 and cols >= 2 (or at least >0) before calling Mesh::regular.

note: Mesh::regular rejects zero and out-of-budget dimensions before division; Mesh.validate checks geometry.

finding.summary: write_native converts a fill appearance item to mesh by changing only kind and paint, leaving other fill-specific fields; deserialization may fail.
finding.evidence: When no existing mesh item is found and a visible fill is selected, the code does item["kind"] = json!("mesh"); item["paint"] = json!(mesh) on the existing fill item. Fill items commonly contain additional fields (opacity, blend_mode, gradient, etc.) that are not valid for the mesh variant. The subsequent serde_json::from_value(value) with a strict Appearance schema (likely deny_unknown_fields) will return an error, making mesh creation fail for such fills.
finding.fix: Replace the fill item entirely with a new object containing only the fields required for a mesh (kind, paint, and optionally visible) instead of mutating the existing fill item.

note: Mesh and fill appearance variants retain envelope fields; native mesh command regression compiles and passes.

finding.summary: Expanding fill/stroke without Object/Appearance ignores on-path metadata, producing unprojected path and stale on_path state.
finding.evidence: In shape_expansion, the check at line 111 only rejects live_shape, corners, or source.live, but not layer.vector.on_path. When options.object and appearance are false (e.g., user selects only Fill or Stroke expansion), the on_path handling in expand_layer (lines 202-212) is skipped because it is inside `if options.object || appearance`. The shape path is cloned directly from source (line 114) without applying the on-path transformation, and the output layer retains `vector.on_path` (line 156 only clears it for object/appearance). The result is a layer whose geometry does not follow the path, silently corrupting the expansion.
finding.fix: Add `|| layer.vector.on_path.is_some()` to the condition at line 111 to return an error, or move the on_path conversion outside the `if options.object || appearance` block so it is always applied before shape_expansion.

note: Fill/stroke-only expansion rejects path text unless object expansion is enabled; focused regression passes.

finding.summary: Expanding fill/stroke without Object/Appearance discards live group effects (Blend, Envelope, Repeat) by skipping their expansion.
finding.evidence: In expand_layer, the match on `source.vector.live` (line 182) is inside `if options.object || appearance`. If the user selects only Fill or Stroke expansion (object=false, appearance=false), this block is skipped. The early compatibility check at line 175 rejects Group layers with appearance, live_shape, or corners, but does not reject live groups. Thus a layer with `vector.live = Some(LiveGroup::Blend)` will pass the check, enter the Group branch at line 215, and recursively expand its children without applying the blend/envelope/repeat effect. The live group effect is silently lost, producing an incorrect expanded result.
finding.fix: Include `source.vector.live.is_some()` in the condition at line 175 to return an error when fill/stroke-only expansion is attempted on a live group, or handle live group expansion regardless of the object/appearance flags.

note: Fill/stroke-only expansion rejects live groups before geometry could be discarded; focused regression passes.

finding.summary: Cache byte budget double-counts shapes when selected layers overlap, causing false rejection of valid expansions.
finding.evidence: In prepare, `let mut bytes = 0;` is initialized once and passed by mutable reference to `refresh_tree` for each target layer in the loop (lines 252-255). If a parent and child are both selected, `refresh_tree` on the parent traverses the child's subtree and adds the child's cache bytes to `bytes`. Then `refresh_tree` is called again on the child, adding the same subtree bytes a second time. The old cache from the parent pass is overwritten when the child is reassigned, but the bytes are never subtracted. This leads to an overestimation of total cache usage and may exceed `MAX_CACHE_BYTES`, returning an error even though the actual final cache size would be within limits.
finding.fix: Compute cache bytes after all target layers have been assigned and the document is final, or track per-layer cache sizes and replace old entries when a layer is overwritten.

note: Capture validation rejects overlapping ancestor/descendant targets before aggregate knot preparation.

finding.summary: Command availability check (object.expand.info) performs full document clone, expansion, and rendering, causing UI blocking.
finding.evidence: The `disabled_reason` function (line 165) calls `prepare` on the session. `prepare` clones the entire document (line 237), expands every target layer, and then calls `refresh_tree` (line 254) which compiles appearances and renders raster caches for all shapes in the selected subtrees. The `object.expand.info` command (line 267) invokes this just to report whether the command is enabled. In UI contexts where the info command is called on selection changes or before showing menus, this performs expensive, potentially multi-second work on the UI thread, causing freezes.
finding.fix: Implement a lightweight validation path for availability that does not clone the document or render caches, or cache the result and invalidate only when the selection or document changes.

note: The UI caches exact expand availability per source Arc, revision and selected IDs, avoiding repeated full preparation in an open menu.

finding.summary: Panic when pasting onto a root layer because `path_of` returns an empty path, causing `first.len() - 1` underflow.
finding.evidence: In `paste`, after collecting paths from `r.capture.layers`, if the target is a root layer, `doc.path_of(*id)` returns an empty Vec. The code enters the `if let Some(first) = paths.first()` branch, then evaluates `first[..first.len() - 1]` on line 123, which underflows and panics. This is reachable from user input if the user selects a root layer and triggers paste.
finding.fix: Before accessing `first.len() - 1`, check if `first.is_empty()` and handle root-level targets separately (e.g., compute top-level index by searching `doc.layers` for the layer ID, or return an error). For example, add `if first.is_empty() { return Err(bad("paste target must have a parent")); }` or implement proper top-level insertion.

note: Document.path_of returns the root index for a root layer; valid root paths are not empty.

finding.summary: Flood replacement destroys original layer's opacity, blend mode, effects, and non-fill/non-stroke appearance items.
finding.evidence: In flood(), `group.vector = Default::default();` at line 395 resets vector settings, while `filled()` (line 307) and `stroke_app` (line 375) retain only Fill and Stroke items respectively. Any other appearance items (e.g., inner shadow, gloss) and vector-specific settings on the original layer are dropped. The new group retains only default vector state, losing data.
finding.fix: Preserve the original layer's full vector appearance/settings when constructing the group, or copy all non-fill/non-stroke appearance items to an appropriate child layer.

note: Flood Fill now rejects Mesh paint explicitly without changing the document; focused native mesh regression passes.

finding.summary: In InBetween insertion mode, the new face layer inherits original opacity/effects/blend causing them to be applied twice (once on face and once on group).
finding.evidence: `face` is cloned from `original` at line 383 and not reset for InBetween mode (only reset inside the `Inside` branch at lines 397-400). The sibling face is inserted after the group at line 409. The group itself (line 394) also retains original opacity/effects/blend. This results in duplicate application of layer-level effects and opacity for the new fill.
finding.fix: When insertion is InBetween, reset face.opacity, face.fill_opacity, face.effects, and face.blend to defaults before inserting.

note: InBetween inserts a sibling of the envelope group, not a child; the inherited envelope is applied once. Inside resets child envelope fields.

finding.summary: Indexing `g.sources[0]` can panic if the live paint group has no child sources.
finding.evidence: `let target = ...unwrap_or(&g.sources[0]);` assumes `g.sources` is non-empty. A live paint group with no children can exist (e.g., after deleting its source paths). `preflight` does not reject such a group, and `from_capture` will produce an empty `sources` vector (line 225 only extends if children exist). Then `g.sources[0]` panics.
finding.fix: Before indexing, check `g.sources.is_empty()` and return an error like 'live paint group has no sources'.

note: Graph::new validates the nonempty 1..128 source budget before indexing; empty-graph regression passes.

finding.summary: Code does not compile: `request.operation` is moved out of a shared reference in `if let` (and similar `matches!` later), but `Operation` is not `Copy`.
finding.evidence: `request` is `&Commit`; `if let Operation::Artboard { rect } = request.operation` attempts to move the non-Copy `Operation` value. The enum derives `Clone` but not `Copy`. Later the same occurs at line 414 (`matches!(request.operation, Operation::ContentMove { .. })`) and line 457 (`matches!(request.operation, Operation::Artboard { .. })`).
finding.fix: Match on a reference: `if let Operation::Artboard { rect } = &request.operation` and use `*rect` when calling `integer_rect`; similarly change `matches!(request.operation, ...)` to `matches!(&request.operation, ...)`.

note: Borrowed Copy fields and destructuring are valid Rust; engine unit targets compile.

finding.summary: Code does not compile: `points` array is moved by `for p in points` and then borrowed via `points.iter()`.
finding.evidence: `for p in points` consumes the array (arrays implement `IntoIterator` by value). After the loop, `points.iter()` at line 330 is a use of a moved value.
finding.fix: Iterate by reference: `for p in &points { ... }` or use `points.iter().try_for_each(...)` for the finiteness check.

note: Borrowed Copy fields and destructuring are valid Rust; engine unit targets compile.

finding.summary: Artboard rectangle is transformed twice when a group with an artboard is transformed.
finding.evidence: `transformed_impl` first calls `transform_layer` on `l`, which already applies the affine `a` to the group (including its artboard rect). Then `update_metadata` reads `board.rect` from the already-transformed group and does `integer_rect([p.x, p.y, r[2] * a.m[0], r[3] * a.m[3]])`, applying `a` a second time. This yields incorrect artboard size/position (e.g., a 2x scale becomes 4x).
finding.fix: Use the original artboard rectangle from `original` (e.g., from `source.artboard` under `if let LayerContent::Group(source) = &original.content`) instead of `board.rect` when computing the new artboard rect.

note: transform_layer_map transforms group children but not artboard metadata; the layout path updates artboard bounds once.

finding.summary: MoveOutside validates entire parent group, causing failure if any sibling is locked
finding.evidence: In Action::MoveOutside, after computing parent group id, code calls targets(&doc, &[parent])?. targets calls validate_layer(parent), which recursively checks child.locks for every descendant. A locked sibling that is not selected triggers Err, preventing moving unlocked layers out.
finding.fix: Replace the targets(parent) call with a lock check only on the selected layers (already done by c.check) or validate that the parent group itself is not locked, not its descendants. Use doc.effective_locks(parent) to check parent's own effective locks without recursing into children, and skip the full recursive descendant lock check for this operation.

note: Move Outside validates the parent envelope and inherited locks without recursively rejecting unselected locked siblings; focused regression passes.

finding.summary: Release clip drops vector mask density and feather attributes
finding.evidence: group.vector_mask contains density and feather fields (validated in validate_layer line 115). In release_clip, only mask.path is used to create the released ShapeLayer; density and feather are not transferred, losing mask-specific data if the user later applies paint to the released path.
finding.fix: Preserve mask.density and mask.feather by either applying them to the released shape's opacity/feather or storing them in the layer's appearance if applicable; otherwise document that they are intentionally discarded.

note: Release Clipping rejects nondefault mask density/feather before editing, preserving unsupported mask semantics; atomic failure regression passes.

finding.summary: Test panics on any system without an RTX 5090 GPU, breaking automated test runs and developer machines.
finding.evidence: assert!(info.name.contains("5090"), "{info:?}"); requires the adapter name to contain '5090'. request_adapter may return a different discrete Vulkan GPU; the assertion fails and panics. This is a hard dependency on a specific hardware model, not a condition of the test logic.
finding.fix: Remove hardware-specific assertions or gate the test behind a feature/env var; use a generic discrete Vulkan adapter.

note: The task explicitly mandates RTX 5090 Vulkan validation.

finding.summary: Pixel comparison uses zip without checking lengths, so if GPU output is shorter than CPU output, missing pixels are silently ignored and max diff may be 0, causing false pass.
finding.evidence: cpu.px.iter().zip(&gpu).flat_map(...).fold(0.0, f32::max) will not compare trailing pixels of the longer slice. If render_to_vec returns an empty Vec, max remains 0.0, the assertion max <= 1/255 passes, and the test incorrectly succeeds. The code does not assert cpu.px.len() == gpu.len().
finding.fix: Assert equal lengths before comparing, e.g., assert_eq!(cpu.px.len(), gpu.len()); or use a zip that checks both iterators exhaustively.

note: Added explicit CPU/GPU pixel-count equality before zip, so an empty/truncated GPU result cannot pass the comparison.

finding.summary: Test loop for average axes reuses mutated session without undo, so Axis::Both is applied to already averaged coordinates, not testing requested behaviour.
finding.evidence: The loop at line 60 iterates over [Horizontal, Vertical, Both] but never calls s.undo() or recreates fixture inside the loop. After first iteration, all y are set to 50; after second, x also set to 40; the Both iteration then averages already uniform values and the assertions trivially pass.
finding.fix: Move fixture creation inside the loop or call s.undo() at the end of each iteration to restore the original document before testing the next axis.

note: The fixture is recreated inside each operation loop, so average-axis cases are independent.

finding.summary: Lock enforcement test uses a stale capture from before the document was modified to add the lock, so the command fails due to stale revision, not the lock.
finding.evidence: At line 234-236 the document is cloned and layer ids[1] is locked, then assigned to session without updating the capture. The executable request `base` was created earlier at line 213, so base.capture.revision is outdated. The subsequent s.execute(...) at line 237 fails for stale revision, not because of the lock, so the lock behaviour is never tested.
finding.fix: Create a new Capture using Capture::begin after setting the lock or update the revision on the base capture to match the new document before executing, to ensure the error is due to the lock.

note: Assigning an Arc fixture does not increment session revision; the freshly captured lock preflight still rejects the target.

finding.summary: Compile error: capture of partially moved value `prepared` in move closure
finding.evidence: At line 525, `let ids = prepared.layers;` moves the `layers` field out of `prepared`. Later, at line 527, `s.edit(label, move |doc, active| { *doc = prepared.document; ... })` attempts to capture `prepared` by move, but `prepared` is already partially moved. Rust does not allow moving a partially moved struct into a closure.
finding.fix: Destructure `Prepared` before the closure, e.g., `let Prepared { document, layers, .. } = prepared;` then use `document` inside the closure and `layers` outside, or clone `layers` instead of moving it.

note: Disjoint field partial moves and closures are valid Rust; engine unit targets compile.

finding.summary: PDF import GPU test requires a specific RTX 5090 Vulkan GPU and will fail on any other hardware
finding.evidence: The test asserts `info.name.contains("5090")` at line 106 after requesting an adapter with `.expect("RTX 5090 Vulkan required")` at line 102. On any machine without an RTX 5090, `request_adapter` returns None, causing the expect to panic, or the assertion fails. This makes the test suite non-portable and breaks CI on standard hardware.
finding.fix: Do not require a specific GPU; either mark the test as `#[ignore]` for manual execution, conditionally skip if the target GPU is not present, or remove the hardware-specific assertions and use a software/CPU fallback for GPU parity testing.

note: This integration task requires actual RTX hardware validation, rather than a portable skip.

finding.summary: Glyph undo test only checks layer name, not the path, so it does not verify that undo restored the glyph path
finding.evidence: The test applies `shape.applyPaths` to modify the path, then calls `s.undo()`, but only asserts `s.active().unwrap().doc.layer(id).unwrap().name == "PDF glyph"` at line 91. The path is never compared to the original, so a regression in undo that leaves the transformed path would not be detected.
finding.fix: Capture the original path before the edit and after undo assert that the layer's shape path equals that original, e.g. `let layer = s.active().unwrap().doc.layer(id).unwrap(); assert_eq!(layer.as_shape().unwrap().path, original_path);`

note: PDF glyph undo regression now asserts that the actual glyph path, as well as its name, is restored.

finding.summary: Double journaling: command 'vector.pathEffects.set' is marked journal=true, but its handler calls commit_with_access which uses s.edit, likely recording a second undo entry.
finding.evidence: Line 348: pub fn commit(s: &mut Session, r: &Request) -> Result<()> { s.execute("vector.pathEffects.set", serde_json::to_value(r)?)?; Ok(()) }. The command is registered with journal: true at line 373. The run function set (line 351) calls commit_with_access (line 353), which at line 339 calls s.edit("Edit Path Effects", ...). If s.edit records an undo transaction, the same user action will create two journal entries, making undo require two steps or corrupting history.
finding.fix: Either remove the journal: true flag from the CommandSpec for set, or remove the s.edit call from commit_with_access and have the command directly mutate the document without creating an extra edit transaction, ensuring only one journal entry is recorded.

note: Session.edit owns undo; the execute journal flag records a separate automation journal. These do not create duplicate undo entries.

finding.summary: AreaCache is rebuilt from scratch on every vector.measure.area command invocation, causing full document projection and pathops each time, despite the comment 'Once per revision, not per pointer frame'.
finding.evidence: run_area calls AreaCache::build(&st.doc, st.revision)? immediately before read. If the UI invokes this command on pointer move/hover to update area measurements, this triggers O(N) expensive geometry processing per frame, causing UI stalls. The AreaCache struct and current() method suggest the cache should be reused across calls, but it is discarded immediately.
finding.fix: Cache AreaCache in Session or higher-level state keyed by document revision, and pass it to read; only rebuild when revision changes.

note: The UI uses an AreaCache keyed by source document and revision; the automation command is a standalone query.

finding.summary: Gesture::begin captures every layer in the document (including guides, non-shape layers) and Capture::check rejects if layers.len() > MAX_OBJECTS (4096), making distance measurement impossible on documents with >4096 total layers even if only a few are shapes.
finding.evidence: let ids = doc.walk().iter().map(|(_, _, l)| l.id).collect(); then Capture::new(doc, revision, ids)? is called. Capture::check (line 94) enforces self.layers.len() > MAX_OBJECTS. doc.walk() returns all layers, not just shape/path owners used by the snapping cache. A document with many non-measurable layers (e.g., guides) will fail distance measurement.
finding.fix: Only capture layer IDs that are actually relevant to the snap query (e.g., from cache internals) or count only vector geometry layers against MAX_OBJECTS; alternatively raise the limit or make it configurable.

note: Distance gestures now build their detached snap cache lazily only when snapping is enabled and not bypassed; disabled snapping does not inherit area or snap object budgets.

finding.summary: Scissors loses fill_rule and inverted flags on all split pieces except the first.
finding.evidence: In Action::Scissors, after taking the first piece from split_at, the code sets `first.fill_rule = path.fill_rule; first.inverted = path.inverted;` but the subsequent `for piece in pieces` loop (line 434) adds each remaining piece via `plan.add(i, piece)` without copying these attributes. Pieces created by `ops::split_at` likely have default fill_rule/inverted, so a path with non-default values (e.g. EvenOdd or inverted) will be rendered incorrectly after the cut.
finding.fix: Before `plan.add(i, piece)` in the loop, set `piece.fill_rule = path.fill_rule; piece.inverted = path.inverted;` (or otherwise ensure all output pieces inherit the original path's fill rule and inverted flag).

note: Every scissors piece retains fill rule, inversion and source component operation; focused regression passes.

finding.summary: Erase loses fill_rule and inverted flags for single-subpath shapes.
finding.evidence: In the `erase` function, when the original path has exactly one subpath (`path.subpaths.len() == 1`), the returned `output` vector contains paths built either by `Path::new` (line 674/695) or by `ops::from_geometry` with only `sp.op` set (lines 697-702). Neither path inherits `path.fill_rule` or `path.inverted`. The final return at line 706 returns these pieces directly, so the resulting output layers have default fill/inverted settings, changing rendering for shapes that use non-default fill rules or the inverted flag. The multi-subpath branch avoids this by cloning the original path and retaining its flags.
finding.fix: When `path.subpaths.len() == 1`, after building the output pieces, set `piece.fill_rule = path.fill_rule; piece.inverted = path.inverted;` for each piece before returning, or construct a final path cloned from the original with its subpaths replaced by the cut pieces.

note: Every erase piece retains fill rule and inversion; focused regression passes.

finding.summary: Compile error: cannot move out of borrowed ViewChange in match
finding.evidence: In change_view, request is &ViewChange, and `match request.action` attempts to move the non-Copy ViewAction enum out of the borrowed struct.
finding.fix: Use `match &request.action` and adjust patterns to references, or `match request.action.clone()`.

note: The enum has Copy payloads and the borrowed pattern is valid Rust; engine unit targets compile.

finding.summary: Compile error: invalid dereference of Document field
finding.evidence: `let mut candidate = (*st.doc).clone();` where `st` is `&ActiveState`; `st.doc` is a `Document` value, not a reference. Dereferencing it is invalid.
finding.fix: Replace with `st.doc.clone()` or `(*st).doc.clone()`.

note: DocState.doc is Arc<Document>; dereferencing and cloning the Document is correct.

finding.summary: Potential panic from invalid `above` anchor before validation
finding.evidence: In insert_prepared for target None, `candidate.insert_above(above, layer.clone())` is called before any existence check on `above`. Later at lines 299-301 the code validates `above`, indicating the missing anchor would be an error, but the clone path already invoked `insert_above` with a possibly invalid id.
finding.fix: Move the existence/lock check for `above` before the candidate clone, or avoid calling `insert_above` in the candidate; compute depth manually.

note: insert_above handles an absent ID without panic; captured-target validation prevents publishing a stale result.

finding.summary: Full document clone on every insertion causes UI freeze
finding.evidence: `let mut candidate = (*st.doc).clone();` clones the entire document (all layers, caches, symbol masters) on every call to `insert_prepared`, even for Compound and Symbol targets where `candidate` is not used. This is a hot path for drawing tools and can block the UI thread on large documents.
finding.fix: Remove the full document clone. Instead, compute the new document's max group depth without cloning, or limit the clone to cases where depth cannot be otherwise determined.

note: The bounded detached clone is prepared at insertion/commit, not each pointer frame, and is used for depth validation.

finding.summary: State::navigate does not restrict selection after truncating stack
finding.evidence: `navigate` calls `self.stack.truncate(depth)` but never calls `self.restrict_selection`. After navigating to a shallower scope, selected layers may include layers outside the new scope, violating isolation invariants and potentially causing operations on out-of-scope layers.
finding.fix: Change `navigate` signature to accept `&mut Session` and call `self.restrict_selection(session)` after truncating, or require callers to call `restrict_selection` immediately.

note: Navigating to a parent expands the current scope; the existing scoped selection remains a valid subset.

finding.summary: Code will not compile because `wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::new_without_display_handle()` is not an existing associated function in wgpu.
finding.evidence: `wgpu::InstanceDescriptor` in wgpu has `default()`, `from_env()`, and `from_env_or_default()` constructors, but no `new_without_display_handle()`. The line `..wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::new_without_display_handle()` is a compile error.
finding.fix: Replace with `..wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::default()` or `..wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::from_env()`.

note: The pinned wgpu 30 InstanceDescriptor has new_without_display_handle; engine tests compile.

finding.summary: Test unconditionally requires an RTX 5090 Vulkan discrete GPU and panics on any other hardware, causing the test suite to fail on normal CI machines.
finding.evidence: Line 13: `.expect("RTX 5090 Vulkan required")` will panic if no adapter is found; line 17: `assert!(info.name.contains("5090"), "RTX 5090 required: {info:?}")` will panic if the adapter is not a 5090. The test is not marked `#[ignore]` and has no runtime skip.
finding.fix: Mark the test with `#[ignore]` or add a runtime check that returns early (e.g., if adapter is None or not RTX 5090) instead of panicking.

note: Actual RTX 5090 validation is explicitly required by the task.

finding.summary: Unbounded recursion in translate before group depth check allows stack overflow via malicious PDF with deeply nested layers.
finding.evidence: In preview (line 97), translate is called on the new group containing scene.layers from PDF import. The translate function recursively descends into Group content (line 135) without any depth limit. Only after insertion does preview check doc.max_group_depth() > MAX_GROUP_DEPTH (line 99). If scene.layers has nesting deeper than MAX_GROUP_DEPTH, the recursion can overflow the stack, causing a panic from user-supplied PDF.
finding.fix: Check the maximum nesting depth of scene.layers before calling translate, or add a depth parameter to translate that returns an error when exceeding MAX_GROUP_DEPTH.

note: The PDF scene producer enforces depth budgets before translation consumes the tree.

finding.summary: Serializing PDF bytes as a JSON array of numbers causes massive memory and CPU overhead for large PDFs, potentially freezing the UI.
finding.evidence: The `run` function constructs `json!({"bytes":output.bytes,...})` where `output.bytes` is a `Vec<u8>`. serde_json serializes a `Vec<u8>` as a JSON array of numbers, so a multi-megabyte PDF expands to tens of megabytes of JSON text (e.g., 10 MB -> ~10 million numbers -> >30 MB of JSON). This allocation and serialization happens on the UI thread and can cause visible freezes or out-of-memory conditions.
finding.fix: Base64-encode the PDF bytes before embedding in JSON (e.g., use `base64::encode(&output.bytes)`) or change the command transport to return binary data separately from the JSON response.

note: The production PDF worker uses binary export directly. JSON byte arrays are the existing explicit automation result contract.

finding.summary: Hit-testing a shape layer that is not a valid path text curve (e.g., multi-subpath or inverted) returns an error, aborting the search and preventing selection of any valid curve behind it.
finding.evidence: In curve_at, after nearest distance check, it calls `let sampler = Sampler::new(&shape.path)?;`. Sampler::new returns Err for paths with subpaths.len()!=1 or inverted or <2 knots. Because the `?` operator is used, the entire curve_at returns Err. This means a user clicking near a complex shape will see an error instead of the function skipping that layer and continuing to next layers.
finding.fix: Change the `?` to a match that continues the loop on error, e.g., `let sampler = match Sampler::new(&shape.path) { Ok(s) => s, Err(_) => continue };` or pre-filter the shape with Sampler::new before the nearest call to skip invalid candidates.

note: Path-text hit testing now skips ineligible foreground paths before choosing the nearest eligible curve; focused regression passes.

finding.summary: Stale gesture guard can be bypassed by omitting 'document' and 'revision' fields.
finding.evidence: The loop in `guarded` only checks values that are present: `if let Some(value) = p.get(key) && value.as_u64() != Some(expected)`. If the client omits both keys, no error is returned, allowing a stale node edit to be applied to the current document.
finding.fix: Require both `document` and `revision` to be present and valid, or explicitly define them as mandatory for this command.

note: Optional guards preserve the existing immediate automation API; captured UI gestures provide document and revision guards.

finding.summary: Undo snapshot is recorded before target validation, leaving orphan snapshots on failed commands.
finding.evidence: `snapshot_shapes` is called immediately after collecting shape ids, before the loop that validates path existence, anchors, locks, live shapes, renderer availability, and corner references. If any validation later fails, the undo stack has already been mutated.
finding.fix: Move `snapshot_shapes` after all validation has passed, or make `snapshot_shapes` transactional (only commit on success).

note: snapshot_shapes clones detached shape edits and does not edit Session, history or journal.

finding.summary: Operation::Insert does not validate the parameter `t` before use.
finding.evidence: In `evaluate`, `Operation::Insert { knot, t }` calls `edit::insert(&mut p, *knot, *t)` without checking that `t` is finite or within [0, 1], unlike `Operation::Bend` which checks both. A user can supply a non-finite or out-of-range `t`, leading to undefined insertion behavior or invalid geometry.
finding.fix: Add `finite(&[*t])?` and check `0.0 <= t && t <= 1.0` before calling `edit::insert`.

note: The downstream insert implementation validates the finite parameter range before applying geometry.

finding.summary: `provenance` uses O(n²) scanning of all base knots for each output knot.
finding.evidence: For every output knot, the code builds a `candidates: Vec<_>` by iterating over every subpath and knot in `base` and filtering by anchor equality (lines 269-275). During a join of large vector paths (many thousands of knots), this results in millions of comparisons and allocations, blocking the UI thread.
finding.fix: Use a spatial hash map (e.g., HashMap keyed by anchor coordinates) to look up candidate knots in O(1) average time, or have the join provider return provenance directly.

note: Node provenance now indexes exact anchors once, canonicalizes signed zero, and preserves unchanged coincident-knot priority; focused regression passes.

finding.summary: Potential panic: `edits[0]` may index an empty vector if `snapshot_shapes` returns Ok(empty) for a non-shape or invalid layer.
finding.evidence: `check_target` for `Target::Shape` calls `vector_api::snapshot_shapes(doc, &[*layer])?` and immediately indexes `edits[0]` without checking `edits.len()`. In `apply` (line 206), the same API call is followed by `.into_iter().next().ok_or_else(...)?`, indicating that an empty vector is possible when the layer is not a shape or not found. A malicious or erroneous `layer` id can trigger this panic.
finding.fix: Add `.into_iter().next().ok_or_else(|| error("pen shape not found"))?` before using the element, or propagate an error if empty.

note: snapshot_shapes returns one edit per requested valid shape or an error; a successful singleton request cannot be empty.

finding.summary: Missing lock check for `Target::Shape`: `check_target` does not verify that the target shape layer is unlocked, allowing edits on locked layers.
finding.evidence: In `check_target`, the `Target::Shape` branch only checks `vector.appearance.is_some()`. It does not call `doc.effective_locks(*layer)`. The `Target::VectorMask` branch (line 83) does check locks, and `Target::NewShape` checks container group locks, so the omission for `Shape` is likely unintended. A user can modify a locked shape layer via the pen commit command.
finding.fix: Add a lock check similar to `Target::VectorMask`: `let locks = doc.effective_locks(*layer); if locks.all || locks.vector { return Err(...) }` (depending on lock fields).

note: snapshot_shapes validates inherited locks before returning shape edits.

finding.summary: Erroneous dereference of Document in assert_eq! will fail to compile or compare the wrong type.
finding.evidence: In this file, s.active().unwrap().doc is used directly as a Document value at lines 32 and 57. On line 67, the expression *s.active().unwrap().doc attempts to dereference that Document value. Unless Document implements Deref to a type that is comparable with Document, this is a compile error or a type mismatch. The rest of the file consistently compares Document values without *.
finding.fix: Remove the *: assert_eq!(s.active().unwrap().doc, shown.document);

note: The session document is Arc<Document>, and dereferencing it before Document::clone is correct.

finding.summary: Test contains contradictory assertions: layer ids[4] is asserted to have opacity 0.25, but flatten comparison at offset 138 (which corresponds to that layer) expects identical pixels to layer 1 (opacity 0.5), causing the test to fail.
finding.evidence: Line 39 asserts doc.layer(ids[4]) == &local (opacity 0.25). Line 41 asserts layers 1-3 have opacity 0.5. Loop over offsets [46,92,138] compares pixel values at x and x+offset. If layers are spaced by 46, offset 138 compares layer 1 (opacity 0.5) to layer 4 (opacity 0.25). Pixels will differ.
finding.fix: Either remove offset 138 from the array (leave [46,92]) if only three layers should be compared, or change line 39 to expect opacity 0.5 for ids[4] by not editing it to 0.25, or adjust the manual edit to set ids[4] opacity to 0.5 as well.

note: Offsets 46, 92 and 138 select the three peers; a fourth peer would require offset 184 and is absent as intended.

finding.summary: Compile error: `siblings` is inferred as `&mut [Layer]` but `drain` (and `insert` on line 141) are not methods on slices, so the code cannot build.
finding.evidence: The `if` expression branches have types `&mut Vec<Layer>` (from `&mut doc.layers`) and `&mut [Layer]` (from `Layer::children_mut`). Rust coerces the first branch to `&mut [Layer]`, making `siblings` a slice. `Vec::drain` and `Vec::insert` do not exist on `[Layer]`.
finding.fix: Ensure both branches produce `&mut Vec<Layer>`. For the non-root case, use a method that returns `Option<&mut Vec<Layer>>` (e.g., `children_mut_vec`) or adjust the API; then `drain` and `insert` will be available.

note: children_mut returns a mutable vector; this use compiles.

finding.summary: View tolerance adjustment is discarded or fails to compile because `p` is not mutable.
finding.evidence: `p` is declared as `let p: Params` (immutable) on line 35. On line 41, `p.view.tolerance(p.settings.tolerance_px)?;` is called as if it mutates `p.view`. If `View::tolerance` takes `&mut self`, this code will not compile because `p` is not mutable. If it takes `&self` and returns a new adjusted `View`, the returned view is ignored, so the tolerance adjustment has no effect on the `p.view` later passed to `cache.point` or `cache.rect`.
finding.fix: Make `p` mutable and assign the result if `tolerance` returns a new view: `let mut p: Params = ...; p.view = p.view.tolerance(p.settings.tolerance_px)?;`. If `tolerance` is intended to mutate in place, change `p` to `let mut p` and ensure the method takes `&mut self`.

note: View::tolerance validates and returns a scalar; it does not mutate View. Settings remain separately validated by queries.

finding.summary: Test expects command to error on unknown settings field, but Settings likely ignores unknown fields by default, causing the command to succeed and the test to fail.
finding.evidence: Line 239 passes json!({...,"settings":{"unknown":true}}) and asserts is_err(). The Settings type is deserialized from JSON; line 206 uses serde_json::from_str("{}") and expects default, indicating missing fields are allowed. Unless Settings has #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], serde will ignore the unknown field and deserialization will succeed, leading to a successful query and failing assertion.
finding.fix: Either add #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)] to the Settings struct (if rejecting unknown fields is intended) or change the test to expect success for unknown settings.

note: Settings rejects unknown fields through serde and the engine test target compiles.

finding.summary: prepare_with_projection writes the recolored document back to the session, causing preview commands to mutate the user's document and commit to potentially fail or double-apply.
finding.evidence: In prepare_with_projection, after cloning the document and modifying it, the code executes `(access.write)(&mut p.document, p.book.clone())?;`. `access.write` updates the session's active document and book, so this applies the recoloring immediately. The `preview` command calls `prepare` and thus mutates the session even though it returns `detached:true`. Subsequent `plan.capture.check(s)` calls (e.g., in another preview or commit) will fail because the session no longer matches the captured state, leading to errors or unexpected persisted changes without journaling.
finding.fix: Remove the `(access.write)` call from `prepare_with_projection`. The writing should be done only in `commit` (or by `colours::publish`) after the user explicitly applies the change.

note: Access.write mutates only Prepared.document, a detached clone, before the native session transaction.

finding.summary: Plan::reduce performs O(colors^3) distance calculations in worst case when reducing to many groups, potentially blocking the UI thread.
finding.evidence: The farthest-first seeding loop (`while centres.len() < n`) iterates over all not-selected points and computes distance to all existing centres, giving O(n^2 * pts) operations. Then the k-means loop runs up to 50 iterations, each requiring O(pts * n) distance calculations. When reducing 4096 colors, this can be over 10^10 operations, freezing the UI for seconds. The `reduce` command runs synchronously on the UI thread.
finding.fix: Optimize using a priority queue or limit iterations, or run the computation in a background thread; at minimum, reduce the worst-case by using a more efficient farthest-first sampling (e.g., k-means++ approximation) and fewer iterations.

note: Farthest-first seeding now maintains nearest distances incrementally, reducing its worst case from cubic to quadratic while retaining tie ordering. A 1024-group deterministic regression was added.

finding.summary: Text run and paragraph lengths are inconsistent with the actual text length, leading to invalid style data and potential panics in sampling/style functions.
finding.evidence: The TextLayer is created with text "aβ\nc" (5 bytes in UTF-8). However, the runs vector has two TextRun entries with lengths 1 and 5, summing to 6. Additionally, the single ParagraphRun has length 6. This mismatch can cause out-of-bounds access or incorrect style resolution when functions like sample() or style lookup iterate over runs.
finding.fix: Adjust run lengths to match the text: first run length 1 (covering 'a'), second run length 4 (covering β, \n, c). Set paragraph length to 5 to cover the whole text.

note: Corrected the test run/paragraph byte lengths to cover its five-byte UTF-8 text exactly.

finding.summary: prepare_path clones the entire Document on every preview, causing UI thread jank.
finding.evidence: preview_command calls prepare -> prepare_with -> prepare_path. Line 329 `let mut document = (*st.doc).clone();` deep-clones all layers and image data. The clone is stored in Prepared.document but is never used by preview_command (which only serializes capture and path).
finding.fix: Avoid cloning the full document for preview; use Arc<Document> or clone only the modified layer, or defer the clone until commit.

note: Prepared.document is used by the production pencil detached preview, and raster Surface tiles use copy-on-write. It is not an unused deep copy of pixel data.

finding.summary: Capture::validate allows first == last for Sculpt, but validate_operation_path later rejects it, causing preview to succeed and commit to fail.
finding.evidence: At line 160, condition only rejects `(!s.closed && first > last)`, so first == last passes. However, at line 421 in validate_operation_path, `if first == last ... return Err(fail())`. Thus a user can start a sculpt gesture with first == last, see a preview, but commit fails with 'geometry changed outside the captured interval'.
finding.fix: Add `first == last` to the invalid condition in Capture::validate (line 160) to reject it upfront.

note: Capture now rejects identical Sculpt endpoints up front; a regression was added. The old prepare path also rejected them, so the claimed successful preview was inaccurate.

finding.summary: Redundant snapshot_shapes call in prepare_with for edit operations.
finding.evidence: At line 226, prepare_with already calls snapshot_shapes to get edits. For Continue/Sculpt/SculptRange, it calls snapshot_shapes again at lines 272/276/280 to get the base path. This clones the shape data twice per preview. The first result is discarded.
finding.fix: Reuse the path from the first snapshot (edits[0].shape.path) instead of calling snapshot_shapes again.

note: prepare_with retains and reuses its one captured shape snapshot for Continue/Sculpt/SculptRange.

finding.summary: Test panics on any machine without an RTX 5090 Vulkan discrete GPU, causing the test suite to fail for most developers and CI environments.
finding.evidence: Line 115 calls `.expect("RTX 5090 Vulkan required")` on the adapter request. Lines 117-119 then assert `info.backend == Vulkan`, `info.device_type == DiscreteGpu`, and `info.name.contains("5090")`. On hardware that does not match these exact requirements, the test panics instead of being skipped.
finding.fix: Gate the test so it is skipped when the required hardware is not present: for example, replace the `expect` with an early return (`let Ok(adapter) = ... else { return; };`) and remove the exact device name assertions, or mark the test with `#[ignore = "requires RTX 5090"]` or a feature/env-var gate.

note: The task explicitly requires RTX 5090 hardware validation.

finding.summary: Redundant preflight call after export duplicates scope validation and document cloning work.
finding.evidence: export() calls preflight(s, r)? on line 54, then performs the export, then calls preflight(s, r)? again on line 60. preflight invokes photocraft_svg::export::scoped_document which builds a detached document copy for validation. The document cannot change during the synchronous export because session is immutable, so the second call is unnecessary and can double memory/CPU usage for large documents.
finding.fix: Remove the second preflight call (line 60), or replace it with a lightweight check that does not rebuild the scoped document.

note: Removed the duplicate synchronous post-export scoped-document preflight; the immutable Session cannot change during export.

finding.summary: Selection scope requires 'layers' field but command params string marks it optional.
finding.evidence: The enum variant Selection { layers: Vec<LayerId> } has no #[serde(default)], so deserialization fails if 'layers' is missing. The params string in specs() at line 77 states 'layers?:[id]', implying optional. If the UI sends {"kind":"selection"} based on that spec, export will fail with a deserialization error.
finding.fix: Either add #[serde(default)] to the layers field (treating missing as empty vector) or correct the params string to indicate that layers is required for selection.

note: Corrected command documentation to show separate scope variants and required layers/layer fields.

finding.summary: Exported SVG bytes are serialized as a JSON array of numbers, causing large memory and CPU overhead.
finding.evidence: The json! macro embeds output.bytes directly. If ExportedVector.bytes is Vec<u8> (likely), serde_json serializes it as an array of integers, e.g. [60,115,118,103,...]. For a large SVG (hundreds of KB to MB), this creates a massive JSON structure, blocking the UI thread and consuming memory.
finding.fix: Encode bytes as a base64 string before embedding in the JSON response, or use a binary transport for the command output instead of JSON.

note: The JSON byte-array result is the existing automation contract; the production SVG save worker consumes binary output directly.

finding.summary: Full document clone on every preview call causes major performance degradation during interactive placement (pointer updates).
finding.evidence: In `preview`, `let mut doc = (*s.doc).clone();` clones the entire active document, including all layers and caches, on each invocation. The function is called with different offsets during pointer updates (as implied by the comment 'never on every pointer update'), leading to O(document size) allocation and copy per frame, blocking the UI thread.
finding.fix: Avoid cloning the whole document for each preview. Instead, maintain a single clone of the document (or a lightweight copy) and only apply incremental changes to the inserted group, or use a render-time compositing approach that does not require a full document clone.

note: The detached placement preview needs a candidate document, with shared COW surfaces. Importing/parsing and source preparation happen once rather than per pointer update.

finding.summary: Missing validation of user-supplied DPI in Open command can lead to invalid import parameters and potential division by zero or invalid document dimensions.
finding.evidence: In `open`, `request.dpi` is used directly in `ImportOptions { dpi: request.dpi, ..Default::default() }` without checking for positive finite values. A user can provide 0, negative, NaN, or infinity via command parameters, and `photocraft_svg::import` likely uses DPI as a scaling factor (e.g., points to pixels conversion), causing division by zero, 0-sized documents, or invalid geometry.
finding.fix: Validate `request.dpi` before import: ensure it is finite and > 0, returning an error if invalid.

note: photocraft_svg::import preflight validates finite DPI within 1..9600 before usvg sees it.

finding.summary: Operator precedence makes the alpha channel comparison use raw alpha instead of the difference, causing the assertion to fail for any document with opaque pixels.
finding.evidence: Rust parses `if i == 3 { a[i] } else { a[i] * a[3] } - b[i]` as `if i == 3 { a[i] } else { (a[i] * a[3]) - b[i] }`. For the alpha channel (`i == 3`) the subtraction by `b[i]` is omitted, so the expression becomes just `a[3].abs()`. Any opaque pixel with `a[3] = 1.0` yields a max of at least `1.0`, which is greater than the tolerance `1.0 / 255.0`, triggering the `assert!(max <= 1.0 / 255.0)` panic.
finding.fix: Wrap the whole if expression in parentheses before subtracting b[i]: `((if i == 3 { a[i] } else { a[i] * a[3] }) - b[i]).abs()`, or use a local variable for the CPU-premultiplied value before subtracting.

note: Rust parses subtraction after the entire if expression; the alpha branch subtracts b[i]. Engine GPU test targets compile.

finding.summary: Move tool press at (35,35) is outside the just-placed PDF object bounds, so no object is selected/dragged and the subsequent assert_ne on line 110 fails.
finding.evidence: The PDF is placed by the drag from (20,20) press to (30,25) release (lines 91, 92, 97), creating an object bounded by approximately (20,20)-(30,25). The Move tool drag then starts at (35,35) (line 106), which is outside that rectangle. If the canvas does not maintain the object selection after area click (or switching tools), the drag does not move the imported group, `moved` equals `released`, and `assert_ne!(photocraft_compose::flatten(&released), photocraft_compose::flatten(&moved))` panics.
finding.fix: Start the Move tool drag at a coordinate inside the placed PDF object bounds, for example (25,22.5) or (22,22).

note: Placement translates the imported scene by the pointer delta; it does not resize the artwork to the drag rectangle. The finding assumes incorrect bounds.

finding.summary: Compile error: type mismatch in `p.left /= c.scale;` if `ProfilePoint::left` is `f32` (likely) because `c.scale` is `f64` and Rust does not implicitly convert.
finding.evidence: The adjacent code at line 118 explicitly casts `c.scale` to `f32` for `base.width`, indicating that `base.width` is `f32`. The same type is expected for profile left/right values (e.g., `p.left`), but lines 125-126 omit the cast (`p.left /= c.scale; p.right /= c.scale;`). If `ProfilePoint::left` and `ProfilePoint::right` are `f32`, this is a compile-time error: `cannot apply /= to f32 and f64`. This prevents the entire crate from building.
finding.fix: Add `as f32` casts: `p.left /= c.scale as f32; p.right /= c.scale as f32;` or change `Capture::scale` to `f32` if all consumers expect `f32`.

note: ProfilePoint left/right are f64. The f32 width cast is unrelated; engine tests compile.

finding.summary: Shape caches are rendered using full document bounds, leading to excessive memory usage and potential OOM when document is large or many trace colors.
finding.evidence: let bounds = self.document.bounds(); ... shape.cache = Some(photocraft_vector::render_shape(&shape, self.document.pixel_format(), bounds)); For each trace layer, render_shape creates a bitmap covering the entire document. A 6000x4000 RGBA document yields 96 MB per shape; with many colors this can exhaust memory.
finding.fix: Use a bounds rectangle limited to the trace region (e.g., origin to origin+trace.width/height) instead of the full document bounds.

note: render_shape uses CompiledShape bounds clipping and sparse tile allocation; a document clip is not a full-canvas bitmap allocation.

finding.summary: Test clones Arc<Document> instead of deep-cloning the Document, so assertions that the document is unchanged after prepare/commit failure will pass even if the document is mutated in place.
finding.evidence: Line 29: `let before = session.active().ok_or("no doc")?.doc.clone();` Since `doc` is `Arc<Document>`, `.clone()` returns a new Arc pointing to the same `Document`. Later line 34: `assert_eq!(session.active().ok_or("no doc")?.doc, before);` compares two Arcs that point to the same object, so any in-place mutation by `prepare` is not detected. The same issue occurs at line 54 for the cancellation check at line 61.
finding.fix: Deep-clone the document instead, e.g. `let before = (*session.active().ok_or("no doc")?.doc).clone();` or use an explicit document clone method. Then the assertions compare independent snapshots.

note: Arc<Document> is immutable and edits use COW. The retained Arc remains the old value after publication.

finding.summary: Surface::new(doc.pixel_format()) creates an empty surface; subsequent write_pixel calls will be out-of-bounds
finding.evidence: In render(), result is initialized with Surface::new(doc.pixel_format()) without any width/height. The loop writes to result at absolute coordinates from doc.bounds(). If result has zero dimensions, the first non-zero pixel triggers an out-of-bounds panic in write_pixel.
finding.fix: Create result with dimensions covering doc.bounds() (or clip) before writing, e.g., Surface::new_with_size(pixel_format, doc.bounds().width(), doc.bounds().height()), and adjust coordinates accordingly.

note: Surface is an unbounded sparse tile map; Surface::new correctly starts with no allocated tiles, and writes allocate them.

finding.summary: r.surface.pixel(x, y) uses absolute coordinates but r.surface is a local buffer relative to r.rect
finding.evidence: render::rasterize_warped returns a bounded surface covering only r.rect. The code passes absolute x,y from clip into r.surface.pixel; if the text is positioned away from (0,0), x/y exceed the surface's width/height and panic. Should use x - r.rect.x0 and y - r.rect.y0.
finding.fix: Use r.surface.pixel(x - r.rect.x0, y - r.rect.y0) for reading pixels from the bounded raster.

note: Surface uses absolute document coordinates for sparse tiles, including rasterize_warped results; no local-buffer subtraction is appropriate.

finding.summary: The new test file will not compile because wgpu::InstanceDescriptor has no associated function `new_without_display_handle`.
finding.evidence: The standard wgpu InstanceDescriptor API provides `Default::default()` and `from_env_or_default()`; there is no `new_without_display_handle` method. The struct update syntax `..wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::new_without_display_handle()` therefore fails to compile, breaking the crate's test build.
finding.fix: Replace `..wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::new_without_display_handle()` with `..Default::default()`, or use `wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::from_env_or_default()` if environment-based defaults are desired.

note: The pinned wgpu 30 API contains new_without_display_handle; engine unit targets compile.

finding.summary: The test is not ignored and hard-requires an RTX 5090 Vulkan adapter, so default `cargo test` panics on any other machine or CI.
finding.evidence: `request_adapter(...).expect("RTX 5090 Vulkan required")` panics if no adapter is found, and line 20 also asserts `info.name.contains("5090")`. Without a skip condition or `#[ignore]`, regular developer machines and CI without an RTX 5090 will fail the default test suite.
finding.fix: Mark the test with `#[ignore = "requires RTX 5090"]`, or detect the absence/suitability of the adapter and `eprintln!` + `return` instead of panicking.

note: The task explicitly requires real RTX 5090 Vulkan validation.

finding.summary: NaN coordinates are not rejected and can cause panic in render_shape.
finding.evidence: The condition `.any(|p| p.x.abs() > 1_000_000. || p.y.abs() > 1_000_000.)` only checks for absolute value greater than 1,000,000. In Rust, `NaN.abs()` is NaN and `NaN > 1_000_000` is false, so a NaN coordinate silently passes validation. Later, these coordinates are used in `Affine::translate` and `photocraft_vector::render_shape`, which may panic or produce undefined behavior when encountering NaN.
finding.fix: Add explicit checks for non-finite values, e.g., `|| !p.x.is_finite() || !p.y.is_finite()` to the condition to reject NaN and infinite coordinates.

note: vector_api::validate_path runs before this coordinate budget check and rejects NaN/Inf.

finding.summary: Local variable `cpu` (Buffer) from line 44 shadows the module `cpu`, causing `cpu::legacy_projector` on line 45 to be resolved against a value, leading to a compile error.
finding.evidence: At line 44, `let cpu = cpu::flatten_scaled(...)?.buffer();` binds `cpu` as a `Buffer` value inside the loop body. The subsequent line 45 uses `cpu::legacy_projector`, but `cpu` now refers to the local variable, not the module declared at line 11. Rust does not allow `::` path access on a value, so the code will not compile.
finding.fix: Rename the local Buffer variable to avoid shadowing the module, e.g., `let cpu_buf = cpu::flatten_scaled(...)?.buffer();` and update subsequent uses (`cpu_buf.px`, `cpu_buf.rect`) while leaving `cpu::legacy_projector` unchanged.

note: Rust value and type/module namespaces are separate; the local cpu buffer does not shadow the cpu module in cpu::legacy_projector.

finding.summary: Out-of-bounds pixel access in color_at via surface.rgba
finding.evidence: color_at validates x/y are finite and abs <= 1_000_000, but never checks the coordinates against the surface dimensions (or non-negative). It then calls surface.rgba(x.floor() as i32, y.floor() as i32). If the user passes coordinates outside the rendered surface (e.g., negative or larger than width/height), surface.rgba will index out of bounds and panic.
finding.fix: Before calling surface.rgba, obtain the surface dimensions and check that x/y are within [0, width-1] and [0, height-1]; if not, return an error or return transparent.

note: Sparse Surface::rgba returns transparent for absent/outside tiles; it does not index a finite bitmap.

finding.summary: Cache budget includes unused compiled appearance plans for on-path text without explicit appearance
finding.evidence: In render_caches, for text with on_path and l.vector.appearance.is_none(), the code pushes a shape (from outlines) into 'shapes' and also the layout into 'on_paths'. Later, the loop over shapes skips rendering for indices present in on_paths. However, the budget calculation at line 667 sums cache_bytes for all plans, including those never rasterized. This can falsely trigger the 'exceeds 512 MiB' error and reject a valid operation.
finding.fix: Exclude on_path text with appearance none from the 'shapes' vector or from the plans/budget calculation, since those plans are never rendered.

note: The compiled outline plan budgets the actual on-path raster cache as well as explicit appearance caches; excluding it would undercount allocation.

finding.summary: validate_sample serializes the entire Sample to JSON before checking psd_raw length
finding.evidence: validate_sample calls serde_json::to_value(s) at line 314, which serializes any psd_raw byte vector into a large JSON array of numbers. Only afterward (line 361) does it check if psd_raw length exceeds 1 MiB. A user-provided Sample (e.g., in Operation::Copy) with a large psd_raw can cause huge memory allocation during serialization, leading to OOM before the length check rejects it.
finding.fix: Move the psd_raw length check (currently line 361) before the serde_json::to_value call, and reject any sample with psd_raw exceeding the limit before serializing.

note: Moved the raw FX byte limit before serde serialization; a regression requires that exact budget error for oversized input.

finding.summary: Copied symbol definitions retain original layer IDs, causing duplicate layer ID conflicts when pasting into a document with overlapping IDs.
finding.evidence: The comment on line 390 states 'fresh template LayerIds', but the code duplicates layers with `Layer::duplicate` (line 441) without reassigning IDs. If the source and destination documents have layers with the same numeric IDs (common in unrelated documents), the copied symbol definitions will introduce duplicate layer IDs, violating document invariants and causing validation failures or data corruption when merged.
finding.fix: After duplicating the symbol definition layers, generate fresh LayerIds for each duplicated layer and remap any parent/child references within those layers (e.g., using a mapping of old to new IDs).

note: Layer::duplicate assigns fresh LayerIds recursively, with an existing document regression covering this behavior.

finding.summary: Placing a symbol above a layer with a locked descendant is incorrectly blocked due to recursive lock check in `targets`.
finding.evidence: `targets` calls `target_locks` (line 83) which recursively checks all descendants (line 77). With `position=false`, it still checks `locks.all || locks.pixels` on each descendant. If a group has a locked child, placing a new layer above that group will fail (line 205), even though the child is not being moved or modified. This prevents a valid user operation.
finding.fix: Use a non-recursive lock check for the insertion point layer (e.g., check only the layer's own locks) or modify `target_locks` to optionally skip descendants when `position` is false.

note: Symbol placement now checks only the insertion neighbor and its inherited locks, preserving unmodified locked descendants. A regression was added.

finding.summary: Example writes fixture files to incorrect relative path, causing failure when run from crate root.
finding.evidence: The path `crates/pc-format/tests/fixtures/vector-v1.pcraft` assumes the current working directory is the workspace root. However, when running `cargo run --example vector_arch_fixture` (even with `-p pc-format` from workspace root), Cargo sets the current working directory to the package root (`crates/pc-format`). This resolves to `crates/pc-format/crates/pc-format/tests/fixtures/...`, which likely does not exist, causing `std::fs::write` to return a `NotFound` error and abort the example before producing the fixture files.
finding.fix: Use `tests/fixtures/vector-v1.pcraft` relative to the package root, or construct an absolute path using `concat!(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), "/tests/fixtures/vector-v1.pcraft")` to be independent of the current working directory.

note: Cargo run inherits the invoking shell working directory; it does not change to the package directory as alleged.

finding.summary: All glyphs are assigned to the first cluster in non-warped text conversion, causing multi-style text to lose per-cluster styling and produce incorrect outlines.
finding.evidence: In `ordinary`, when no warp is present, `clusters` is built from `shaped.clusters` with each cluster's style information, but `glyph_clusters` is initialized as `vec![0; shaped.glyphs.len()]`, mapping every glyph to cluster index 0. `on_path::validated_outlines` uses this mapping to determine which cluster each glyph belongs to, so all glyphs are treated as part of the first cluster. Any additional clusters (e.g., different colors, faux bold) are ignored, producing a single style for all glyphs or potentially malformed output. This is reachable by converting any text layer with rich formatting not applied on a path.
finding.fix: Build `glyph_clusters` by assigning each glyph to its actual cluster index, using the existing per-glyph cluster assignment from `shaped` if available (e.g., `shaped.glyph_clusters`) or by iterating clusters and filling the vector according to each cluster's glyph count.

note: Identity cluster transforms intentionally coincide. Each glyph reads its own g.style color, faux-bold and face; glyph styles are not taken from cluster zero.

finding.summary: Mailbox removed immediately after start_preview, so preview result can never be delivered.
finding.evidence: start_preview inserts the sender into MAILBOXES, calls session.start asynchronously, then unconditionally removes it with take_mailbox(id) before the job can consume it. The worker later calling take_mailbox will get None, so it cannot send the Preview; the receiver will see a closed channel.
finding.fix: Remove the unconditional take_mailbox; only remove on session.start error, or have the command handler remove it after sending the result.

note: Session.start invokes the command handler synchronously; the handler takes the mailbox before spawning the latest-key worker. Cleanup removes only an unconsumed validation-failure mailbox.

finding.summary: surface.read_region(bounds) may be called with bounds larger than the layer surface for non-full-canvas raster/smart layers, causing out-of-bounds access.
finding.evidence: source_bounds returns document bounds (or selection bounds) without clipping to the source layer's surface. At line 171-173, the code gets layer.surface() and calls read_region(bounds) immediately. If the layer surface is smaller than the document bounds (e.g., a small pixel layer on a larger canvas), read_region will read past the surface, likely panicking or producing an error. The check at line 80 only validates layer type, not size.
finding.fix: Intersect the source bounds with the layer surface bounds before calling read_region, or use a document-sized composited surface for reading.

note: Sparse Surface::read_region supports arbitrary document rectangles and returns transparent pixels for absent tiles.

finding.summary: Symbol instance group transform does not include the instance transform
finding.evidence: For LayerContent::Symbol, the parent layer's transform is inserted as `inherited` (line 29). The instance transform is only folded into child transforms as `a = inherited.mul(&instance.transform)` (line 33), but the parent layer's transform remains `inherited`. Since the comment says the outer instance's blend/masks/effects stay on this group, those effects use the wrong transform whenever `inherited != a` (e.g., nested symbol instances). Additionally, if the consumer applies group transforms hierarchically, the parent group will transform children that already have absolute transforms, causing double application.
finding.fix: For symbol instances, after computing `a`, update the transform for the symbol instance layer to `a` and project children with relative transforms (or adjust the renderer to not apply the group transform to children).

note: Transforms are absolute and applied once by prepare_expansion. The outer instance envelope is in its containing coordinate space, while master content receives the instance transform.

finding.summary: Unnecessary full clone of Group including its children for every group layer
finding.evidence: `..g.clone()` clones the entire original Group, including the original `children` vector, only to immediately override `children` with the projected result. For large groups this duplicates all child layers (with COW but still allocates and increments refcounts) on every projection, which can be costly on export or cache rebuild.
finding.fix: Replace `..g.clone()` with explicit field updates, e.g., `Group { children: project(...)?, expanded: g.expanded, artboard: g.artboard }` (adjusting for any other Group fields), to avoid cloning the child vector.

note: Replaced Group struct update with explicit expanded/artboard fields, avoiding an unnecessary clone of original children.

finding.summary: command_bindings removes user custom keybinding for a command if its target matches an override target, even when the chord does not conflict, causing loss of user shortcuts for overridden commands.
finding.evidence: In `command_bindings`, the filter condition is `!overrides.iter().any(|b| b.key == key || b.target == id)`. This removes any pixel binding whose command ID equals an override target, regardless of whether the chord is the same. The comment states overrides should affect only chord owners, not all bindings for the target. Input `pixel` includes user overrides; e.g., user assigns 'Shift+Cmd+V' to 'object.pasteBack'; ACCELERATORS contains Cmd+B for same target; the user binding is removed and replaced with Cmd+B.
finding.fix: Change the condition to only remove entries where the chord matches an override key: `!overrides.iter().any(|b| b.key == key)` (and potentially handle duplicate target binding by preferring overrides or warning, but not silently removing different-key bindings).

note: Vector accelerator overrides now replace conflicting chord owners only, preserving custom nonconflicting chords for the same target; a regression was added.

finding.summary: Distort operation ignores Transform Patterns because `a` is None for non-affine maps.
finding.evidence: In `mapping`, `Operation::Distort` returns `Some(map)` but `a` remains `None` in `prepare`. For each shape, `metadata::paint(..., a, c.options.patterns, ...)` is called with `a = None`; the pattern transform is skipped, so patterns do not follow the distortion even if `options.patterns=true`.
finding.fix: Pass the distortion map to `metadata::paint` (or compute a local affine approximation) so patterns are transformed for Distort, or reject Distort with Patterns enabled.

note: metadata::paint explicitly errors when Transform Patterns is enabled for a non-affine Distort map; it does not silently skip the request.

finding.summary: Transform Again for Reshape maps nodes by selection index, so reordering selected targets applies reshape to wrong layers.
finding.evidence: In `again_request`, the old root is found by enumerating `previous.capture.layers` and storing `index`; then `capture.layers[index]` is used as the new root. If the user selects the same target objects in a different order, index points to a different object, and the relative node path is applied to the wrong object, potentially moving incorrect nodes.
finding.fix: Match old and new roots by stable layer identity (e.g., layer UUID or document path excluding position) instead of enumeration index, and verify correspondence before mapping nodes.

note: Reshape replay now matches retained root LayerIds before falling back to positional correspondence for copies/new targets; reordered-selection regression was added.

finding.summary: migrate_with returns the original `found` version instead of the final migrated version. With the new v1->v2 migration step, a v1 manifest is upgraded to `format_version: 2` but `migrate` returns 1, so any caller using the return value will believe the file is still on v1.
finding.evidence: The loop at lines 28-32 sets `v["format_version"] = Value::from(ver + 1)`; after it, line 33 returns `Ok(found)`. Previously `STEPS` was empty so `found == target` in production; now `STEPS` contains `v1_to_v2`, so migrating version 1 to target 2 returns 1 while the JSON has been mutated to 2. The added test at line 86 explicitly asserts the incorrect `migrate(&mut v).unwrap() == 1`.
finding.fix: Return `Ok(target)` or `Ok(ver + 1)` after the loop, and update the test to expect the final version (2).

note: migrate_with returns the original file version as its existing contract and tests require; the manifest is upgraded in place. Production callers discard the return value.

finding.summary: Compile error: `wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::new_without_display_handle` does not exist in wgpu; ignored tests still compile and break the test target.
finding.evidence: The code attempts to construct `wgpu::InstanceDescriptor` with `..wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::new_without_display_handle()`. In wgpu's public API (0.19/0.20) `InstanceDescriptor` has no such associated function; the headless descriptor is created via `Default::default()` or `InstanceDescriptor::from_env_or_default()`. This fails during compilation of the `gpu` test module (`cargo test --no-run`), so CI/build breaks.
finding.fix: Replace `wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::new_without_display_handle()` with `Default::default()` or `wgpu::InstanceDescriptor::default()`.

note: The pinned wgpu 30 API has new_without_display_handle; unit targets compile.

finding.summary: Potential panic from indexing an empty vector in `stroke` if `snapshot_shapes` returns an empty vector for a layer that is not a vector shape.
finding.evidence: The line `let e = &edits[0];` assumes that `vector_api::snapshot_shapes(&st.doc, &[id])?` always returns at least one element. If the requested `LayerId` corresponds to a non-vector layer (e.g., raster or group) and `snapshot_shapes` filters out non-shape layers instead of returning an error, the vector will be empty and this indexing will panic.
finding.fix: Replace direct indexing with a checked access, e.g., `let e = edits.first().ok_or_else(|| error("layer is not a shape"))?;` and propagate a user-friendly error instead of panicking.
