note: snapshot_shapes returns an error for any non-shape target and exactly one edit for a valid singleton; it never filters into an empty success.

finding.summary: The `first` flag is reset for each `PaintedOutline`, so multiple outlines with the same color produce multiple subpaths with `PathOp::Combine` in the same merged `Path`.
finding.evidence: `first` is declared inside `for paint in paints` (line 16) and passed to `finish`, which uses it at line 25: `op: if *first { PathOp::Combine } else { PathOp::Join }`. If two entries in `paints` share a color, the second entry's first subpath is emitted with `PathOp::Combine` even though the shared color path already has subpaths.
finding.fix: Track `first` per unique color, for example store a bool in the `out` tuple or derive the first subpath from `path.subpaths.is_empty()` instead of using a per-paint bool.

note: Separate Combine components intentionally preserve each glyph outline winding/holes before unioning overlapping glyphs; resetting per PaintedOutline is required.

finding.summary: Pen handle dragging is inverted for at_first/closing drags: pointer controls the non-segment control point, so visible curve shapes in the wrong direction.
finding.evidence: In `motion`, for `self.at_first` (lines 277-280) it sets `k.in_ctrl = out; k.out_ctrl = incoming;` but for a path segment the outgoing handle is `out_ctrl`. For closing drags (lines 263-272) it similarly assigns `reflected` to the segment control and `out` to the other. This makes dragging affect the hidden handle while the visible segment uses the reflected point.
finding.fix: Always set the handle that participates in the segment to `out` and the opposite to `reflected`/`incoming`: non-closing uses `k.out_ctrl = out; k.in_ctrl = incoming;` regardless of `at_first`; closing at first uses `k.in_ctrl = out; k.out_ctrl = reflected;`; closing at last uses `k.out_ctrl = out; k.in_ctrl = reflected;`.

note: Extension at the first endpoint traverses the new segment in reverse; closing shapes the arriving handle. Existing endpoint/closing replay tests enforce these directions.

finding.summary: Node budget (`MAX_KNOTS`) is not checked when `begin` creates a new subpath, allowing the path to exceed the limit by one and blocking further edits.
finding.evidence: In `begin`, when no endpoint is found, it always does `path.subpaths.push(Subpath::polyline(&[(at.x, at.y)]))` (line 110) without checking the total knot count against `MAX_KNOTS`. Later `press` (line 200) and `motion` (line 239) enforce the limit, but the initial extra node has already been added, causing total count to exceed `MAX_KNOTS` and later `finish` may fail validation or the user cannot add a second node.
finding.fix: Before pushing the new subpath, check `original.subpaths.iter().map(|s| s.knots.len()).sum::<usize>() >= MAX_KNOTS` and return an error if so.

note: Pen begin now checks the aggregate knot budget before adding a detached subpath; a max-budget regression was added.

finding.summary: `generation` is not incremented when a zero-length line draft is truncated on release, so change tracking misses the path update.
finding.evidence: In `release`, when `sp.knots.len() == 2` and distance < 1e-9, it truncates to 1 knot (line 298) but returns `Preview` without updating `self.generation`. Other path mutations increment `generation`, so UIs relying on it may not re-render the removed segment.
finding.fix: Add `self.generation = self.generation.wrapping_add(1);` after `sp.knots.truncate(1); self.auto.truncate(1);`.

note: Zero-length line release now increments generation after truncating the draft; a generation regression was added.

finding.summary: Compile error: lifetime mismatch in registered.contains(&id.as_str()) because registered is inferred as Vec<&'static str> but id.as_str() returns a shorter-lived &str.
finding.evidence: registered is initialized from crate::toolsets::VECTOR_TOOLS.iter().map(|t| t.id).collect(), where t.id is &'static str, so registered: Vec<&'static str>. In this loop, set.tools is Vec<String>, id is &String, id.as_str() returns &str tied to the local String. Vec<&'static str>::contains expects &&'static str, but &id.as_str() has a shorter lifetime, causing a compile error.
finding.fix: Replace registered.contains(&id.as_str()) with registered.iter().any(|r| r == id.as_str()) or change registered to Vec<String> (e.g., by cloning the static IDs).

note: Vec::contains permits comparing a shorter borrowed str with stored static str values; engine test targets compile.

finding.summary: similarity() returns true for a zero affine matrix, allowing zero-scale transforms to proceed as live similarity transforms.
finding.evidence: When a.m is all zeros, scale = 0.0; both `(x*u + y*v).abs() <= 1e-10 * scale * scale` and `(x.hypot(y) - u.hypot(v)).abs() <= 1e-10 * scale` become `0 <= 0`, so similarity returns true. `live` then computes k=0 and constructs zero-width/height design shapes; `paint` also passes the similarity gate and zeroes the pattern scale before its own validation.
finding.fix: Require a positive scale before testing similarity, e.g. `if scale <= 0.0 { return false; }`.

note: Transform preflight rejects singular/near-zero scale affine maps before metadata::similarity is called.

finding.summary: paint() mutates pattern scale/angle/phase in place before validating the final values, so an error leaves the Fill partially transformed.
finding.evidence: Lines 192-198 assign `*scale`, `*angle`, and `*phase` directly. Line 199 then checks `scale`, `angle`, and `phase` and can return Err. For example, old scale=100 and transform scale=200 gives new scale=20000; line 199 returns Err but `fill.scale` is already 20000, corrupting the pattern even though the operation reported failure.
finding.fix: Compute the new scale, angle, and phase in local variables, validate all of them, and only assign back to `fill` on success.

note: metadata::paint is called only on detached candidate layers; any error discards the candidate before Session publication. No native fill is partially mutated.

finding.summary: effects() mutates effect fields immediately and returns early on bounds errors, leaving some effects scaled and others not.
finding.evidence: `mul` writes `*v *= k` (line 150) and then returns Err if the new value is non-finite or >1e6. The caller uses `?` inside the loop (lines 159-171), so if a later field fails, earlier fields remain changed. `effects.psd_raw` is only cleared on full success, so the layer can contain a mix of scaled and unscaled effect data.
finding.fix: Compute scaled values first, validate each, and only mutate the effect structs after all checks pass, or roll back on error.

note: Effects are scaled on detached candidates, and prepare propagates errors before publication. The original document remains unchanged.

finding.summary: allowed(descend=true) with parent=None permits all layers, bypassing edit_all_layers=false scope at root.
finding.evidence: In Index::allowed, when self.parent is None the closure `self.parent.is_none_or(|id| e.layer.id == id || e.parents.contains(&id))` returns true for every entry. Callers hit (line 598) and Query::Group (line 721) pass descend=true. If scope.edit_all_layers=false and active is a top-level layer (parent None), nested group children become selectable, violating the documented behavior 'At the root this excludes group contents'.
finding.fix: For descend=true and parent=None, restrict to top-level layers, e.g. change the descend branch to `self.parent.map_or_else(|| e.parents.last().is_none(), |id| e.layer.id == id || e.parents.contains(&id))`.

note: Handoff 32 explicitly permits Group Selection to descend sibling scope for leaf hits, including root sibling groups, before selecting an ancestor.

finding.summary: Same::FillColor treats missing fill as equal, selecting unfilled objects when reference has no fill.
finding.evidence: `Same::FillColor => fill(&aa) == fill(&ba)` compares Option<&Fill>. If both references and candidates have no fill, both are None, so the criterion matches. The same pattern affects FillAndStroke (line 466) and StrokeColor (line 465). A user running 'select same fill color' on an unfilled object will select all other unfilled objects.
finding.fix: Require both fills to be present before comparing, e.g. `match (fill(&aa), fill(&ba)) { (Some(a), Some(b)) => a == b, _ => false }`.

note: No fill is a valid appearance attribute shared by unfilled objects; Same Fill/Stroke deliberately compares the topmost optional paints.

finding.summary: Magic Wand fill/stroke color also treats missing fill/stroke as matching.
finding.evidence: `similar(fill(&aa), fill(&ba), w.fill_tolerance)` returns Ok(true) when both Option<&Fill> are None. Consequently, a wand query with fill_color=true on an unfilled reference matches all unfilled layers. The same applies to stroke_color at line 498.
finding.fix: Change `similar` to return false when either fill/stroke is missing, or adjust wand to require both Some before calling similar.

note: Wand compares absent paints as a shared appearance attribute, consistently with Same Fill/Stroke; this is intentional matching semantics.

finding.summary: Query::Artboard filters by the active board from scope instead of the target board, so selecting a non-active artboard can return no results.
finding.evidence: The loop `for e in index.entries.iter().filter(|e| index.allowed(e, false) && paintable(e.layer, readers))` uses Index::allowed, whose board is computed from scope.active (line 313). If scope.edit_all_layers=false and the active layer is not inside the requested artboard, allowed entries are restricted to the active board/siblings and the target artboard's contents are excluded, even though the query explicitly names `board`.
finding.fix: For Artboard queries, derive allowed candidates from the target board's descendants (e.g., by checking `e.parents.contains(&board)` directly) while still enforcing lock/hidden/isolation constraints.

note: Named-artboard queries use geometric overlap within the authoritative current selection/isolation scope; they must not select outside that scope.

finding.summary: User-supplied capture is not validated against the active document, allowing vectorization to target the wrong document.
finding.evidence: In execute(), after parsing `capture` from user input, only `request.layer != id` is checked (line 48). The `Capture` struct also contains a `document` field, which is used later (e.g., line 67 for preview key and possibly in trace_output::publish). Since LayerId values are per-document and not globally unique, a user can supply a capture from another open document with the same layer ID. The command proceeds with the active document (`let doc = s.active()...doc.clone()`), but publish/insertion may use `captured.document`, leading to modifications in the wrong document.
finding.fix: Add a check that `request.document` equals the current active document's ID before accepting the capture, e.g., compare with `s.active().doc.id` and return an error if they differ.

note: trace_output::check validates the captured document, revision and source after deserialization and before publication.

finding.summary: Symbol caches are clipped to the global document bounds in the expansion root coordinate space, causing symbols inside transformed groups to be cut off or disappear.
finding.evidence: render_instance creates a temporary root LayerContent::Symbol and expands it without ancestor transforms. The bounds are then intersected with doc.bounds() (global). refresh_layer_symbols calls render_instance for each symbol without passing parent transforms. If a symbol layer is inside a transformed group, its local coordinates may be outside doc.bounds but become visible after the enclosing group transform is applied by the compositor; the intersection discards those pixels, so the cache is empty or clipped and the symbol does not render correctly.
finding.fix: Do not intersect the expanded layer bounds with doc.bounds() here. Instead use the union of the expanded layer bounds as the cache bounds, or compose the enclosing group transform before clipping to the global document bounds.

note: Native Group has no hierarchical affine field; expansion bakes absolute child transforms once.

finding.summary: Each symbol refresh clones the entire document twice, causing O(N × document size) work when many symbols are refreshed and blocking the UI thread.
finding.evidence: render_instance starts with let mut projected = doc.clone(); and then composite_surface again clones the document (let mut projected = doc.clone(); at line 46). refresh_layer_symbols calls render_instance for every symbol in a subtree, so a document with many symbols performs one full document clone per symbol plus another clone per composite, repeatedly copying all document layers.
finding.fix: Avoid full document clones per symbol: build a working document once and reuse it for batch symbol refreshes, or modify composite_surface to accept pre-projected layers without cloning the entire document.

note: Fixed: removed the redundant full document clone before computing expanded symbol bounds; compositing still owns its necessary detached document.

finding.summary: bounded_cache creates an empty Surface with Surface::new(format) and then writes rows into it, causing a panic or producing an invalid/empty cache.
finding.evidence: Line 307 uses Surface::new(surface.format()) to create an empty surface when clip is empty, confirming that Surface::new(format) creates a zero-sized surface. In the mask baking branch (lines 318-331), cache is reassigned to Surface::new(format) even though clip is non-empty, then write_region is called row-by-row without resizing. This will either panic due to out-of-bounds writes or result in an empty cache, corrupting export for shape layers with vector masks.
finding.fix: Allocate a surface with the correct clip dimensions before writing, for example by using Surface::from_interleaved(format, clip, &[]) or a constructor that accepts width and height, instead of Surface::new(format).

note: Surface is sparse and size-free by design; write_region allocates its tiles without a canvas-sized constructor.

finding.summary: prepare does not verify that the projection preserves layer.vector_mask, allowing a projection to silently drop the user vector mask.
finding.evidence: In the compositing envelope check (lines 207-214), the code compares visible, opacity, fill_opacity, blend, clipped, mask, and effects, but omits vector_mask. The projection trait is required to return a layer with the same ID and cleared live/crop metadata, but it could also clear or alter vector_mask. Since vector_mask is a user-editable mask, its loss would not be detected and the exported PSD would lack the mask, causing data loss.
finding.fix: Add `|| out.vector_mask != layer.vector_mask` to the condition on line 207 so that any change to vector_mask by the projection is treated as an error.

note: Fixed: PSD projection now includes vector_mask in the compositing-envelope equality check; regression rejects a provider that discards it.

finding.summary: No cumulative budget for text run variations leads to unbounded iteration during validation
finding.evidence: Line 108 bounds `t.runs.len()` to MAX_OBJECTS (100_000), but each run's `variations` vector is iterated at line 121 with no total limit. A crafted file with 100,000 runs each containing a large number of variations causes billions of `number()` calls, blocking the UI thread during document validation.
finding.fix: Add a total variations budget before the run loop, e.g., compute `let total_variations: usize = t.runs.iter().map(|r| r.style.variations.len()).sum();` and return an error if it exceeds a configured limit (such as MAX_OBJECTS or a dedicated cap).

note: Fixed: symbol validation charges aggregate text-run variations before scanning them; aggregate-budget regression passed.

finding.summary: Saved paths and work path are omitted from spacing targets; spacing snapping cannot snap to them.
finding.evidence: In Cache::build, the loop over doc.paths (line 305) and the work_path branch (lines 310-313) call only cache.add_path, which adds nodes and curves but does not push an Object to the objects vector. The objects vector is the sole source for spacing pairs built at lines 320-329. Thus spacing_best used by rect will never consider saved paths or work path as spacing objects, despite Source::SavedPath and Source::WorkPath variants existing and being used in node/curve hits.
finding.fix: For each non-excluded saved path and work path, compute a bounding rect (e.g., via geometry.bounds if available or a fallback like crate::snap::layer_rect) and push Object { rect, source } into objects before building the cached spacing pairs.

note: Spacing snap targets are object bounds; work/saved paths are node and curve targets rather than drawable objects.

finding.summary: Point snapping with curves enabled scans every curve and calls geometry.nearest on every pointer move, causing potential UI stalls on documents with many curves.
finding.evidence: Cache::point lines 418-440 iterate over all self.curves and invoke (geometry.nearest)(&curve.path, ...) for each curve. This function is called from the UI hot path during dragging; MAX_OBJECTS permits up to 4096 curves, and no spatial index is used. This results in O(number of curves) nearest calculations per pointer move, which can exceed the per-frame budget on large documents.
finding.fix: Build a spatial index (e.g., bounding-box grid or R-tree) in Cache::build and query only those curves whose bounds are within tolerance of the query point before calling geometry.nearest; or use a per-frame cache if the pointer movement is incremental.

note: Fixed: curve nearest-point queries first cull cached control bounds inflated by tolerance; callback-count regression passed.

finding.summary: Hardcoded FillRule::NonZero in intersects_rect ignores the path's fill rule, so a marquee entirely inside a hole of an EvenOdd shape is incorrectly treated as intersecting.
finding.evidence: The file's own evenodd_hole test constructs a two-rectangle path and asserts fill_contains with NonZero returns true at the hole center (5,5). In intersects_rect, the fallback uses FillRule::NonZero, so a Rect fully inside the hole of such a shape would select it, even though EvenOdd filling excludes that area.
finding.fix: Use the path's fill rule (e.g. path.fill_rule()) instead of FillRule::NonZero, or pass the actual fill rule into fill_contains.

note: geom::PathData has no fill-rule field; this primitive intentionally uses NonZero. Production selection uses the native rule-aware hit provider.

finding.summary: path.to_bezpath() allocates a new BezPath on every call, on the marquee-selection hot path.
finding.evidence: intersects_rect is documented as 'Used for marquee selection' and will be called for each path on pointer move. Line 49 unconditionally calls path.to_bezpath(), converting the entire path and allocating a new BezPath each time, which can degrade performance with many or complex paths.
finding.fix: Cache the BezPath in PathData or convert once and reuse, or iterate PathData segments directly without building a BezPath.

note: The helper is not the production selection hot path, which caches geometry and bounds. No demonstrated performance regression from this small detached primitive.

finding.summary: Unbounded recursion in has_instances can cause stack overflow on a deeply nested manifest
finding.evidence: validate_symbols_manifest calls has_instances(&doc.layers) when doc.symbols.is_empty(). has_instances recurses into ContentM::Group children with no depth parameter or limit (line 647). A malicious file with a deeply nested group chain (even empty groups) and no symbols will trigger unbounded recursion before the depth-limited collect function is called, leading to a stack overflow crash.
finding.fix: Add a depth parameter to has_instances and enforce the same MAX_GROUP_DEPTH limit as collect, e.g. has_instances(layers, depth) with if depth > MAX_GROUP_DEPTH { return false } or return an error.

note: Fixed: has_instances now iteratively validates every branch against MAX_GROUP_DEPTH instead of recursing or returning early on one symbol.

finding.summary: fit_single_from can panic with an index out of bounds when u is longer than pts, including empty pts via fit_single.
finding.evidence: fit_single(&[]) calls chord_params(&[]), which returns vec![0.0]. fit_single_from then enters the reparameterization loop: for (i, ui) in u.iter_mut().enumerate() { *ui = newton(&best, pts[i], *ui); }. With i=0, pts[0] panics because pts is empty. Similarly, any caller passing u longer than pts triggers this.
finding.fix: Add a guard at the start of fit_single_from: if pts.len() != u.len() || pts.is_empty() { return a zero cubic with error 0; } or use pts.get(i) to avoid panics. Ensure chord_params returns an empty Vec for empty input.

note: fit_single_from is private; all callers provide nonempty matched sample/parameter vectors, including the fixed-size removal fitter.

finding.summary: sample produces NaN points when n=0 and include_start is true.
finding.evidence: For n=0 the loop executes i=0 and computes i as f64 / n as f64 = 0.0/0.0 = NaN. c.eval(NaN) returns a NaN point, which can propagate invalid geometry. The function is pub(crate) and has no n>0 precondition.
finding.fix: Handle n==0 explicitly: if include_start, push c.eval(0.0); else return without pushing. Or document and enforce n>0.

note: Private sample callers use positive constants 12, 16 and 40; zero is not an external input.

finding.summary: arc() ignores the slope parameter because it is multiplied by 0.0, so changing slope via UI has no effect on the generated path.
finding.evidence: The expression `KAPPA * (1.0 + slope.clamp(-1.0, 1.0) * 0.0)` always evaluates to KAPPA for finite slope. Handles h1 and h2 therefore depend only on a and b, not on slope.
finding.fix: Use slope in the formula, e.g. `let k = KAPPA * (1.0 + slope.clamp(-1.0, 1.0));` or the intended nonzero factor.

note: The legacy unused geometry arc helper is not the live Arc implementation; design_shapes generates and validates actual start/end/sweep parameters.

finding.summary: polar_grid() emits one radial line even when radial is 0, because the iteration count uses radial.max(1).
finding.evidence: `for i in 0..radial.max(1)` yields `0..1` when radial is 0. The loop then pushes `line(c, ...)` for that iteration, so requesting zero radial dividers produces an unwanted line.
finding.fix: Handle `radial == 0` by returning only ellipses, or loop `for i in 0..radial` while using `radial.max(1)` only as the divisor in the angle calculation.

note: The public polar-grid helper emits no spokes for zero radial count. Added zero-spoke regression.

finding.summary: rectangular_grid() can panic on overflow when h_dividers is u32::MAX via `h_dividers + 1`; a similar overflow exists for v_dividers and for concentric in polar_grid().
finding.evidence: In debug builds, `h_dividers + 1` panics on overflow. In release it wraps to 0, causing `i as f64 / 0.0` to produce inf/NaN and pushing a line with invalid coordinates. No validation rejects u32::MAX.
finding.fix: Cast divider counts to a wider type before adding 1 or use saturating arithmetic, and cap the number of dividers to a practical maximum.

note: Production shape generation uses bounded validated design-shape counts rather than these legacy low-level generators.

finding.summary: subpaths() can return an element range that does not start with MoveTo after a ClosePath followed by a drawing command, causing those path segments to be silently dropped by segments().
finding.evidence: For a BezPath built as move_to((0,0)), line_to((10,0)), close_path(), line_to((20,0)): subpaths() sets start to the index after ClosePath (line 29), then line 35 pushes (start..len, false) where the first element is PathEl::LineTo. segments() delegates to kurbo::segments() with no MoveTo, and kurbo::segments has no current point so it ends immediately; the LineTo after the close is lost even though it is a valid new subpath in the represented path.
finding.fix: Ensure every subpath range starts with an explicit PathEl::MoveTo, e.g. normalize the BezPath by inserting a MoveTo to the closed subpath's start point after any ClosePath that is followed by a non-MoveTo command, or change segments() to accept an initial point for such ranges.

note: segments requires normalized MoveTo-based subpaths; native/SVG normalization injects MoveTo after ClosePath before further segments.

finding.summary: Vector mask with density != 1 produces an incorrect transparency mask: outside the path becomes partially opaque instead of transparent, and inside is fully opaque instead of the specified density.
finding.evidence: The code draws a full white rectangle with opacity `1.0 - m.density` and then draws the vector mask path with white at opacity 1.0. On a transparent background, this results in alpha = 1 - density outside the path and alpha = 1 inside, which is the inverse of the expected mask (0 outside, density inside). This corrupts layer transparency during PDF export.
finding.fix: Draw only the vector mask path with solid white at opacity `m.density` and leave the outside fully transparent, or build the mask by clearing to transparent and filling the path with alpha=density.

note: Mask density relaxes masked-out pixels toward visibility; it is not a uniform multiplication of every mask sample.

finding.summary: Fill opacity is applied globally to both fill and stroke, causing strokes to become more transparent than intended when fill_opacity < 1.
finding.evidence: `s.push_opacity(norm(l.fill_opacity))` is pushed before drawing the layer content. In `shape()` both `path_fill` and `path_stroke` are called, so the stroke's effective opacity becomes `fill_opacity * stroke_opacity`, but `fill_opacity` should only affect fills, not strokes.
finding.fix: Remove the global push of fill_opacity and instead pass `fill_opacity` into `path_fill` as a multiplier for fill paint opacity, leaving stroke opacity unaffected.

note: Layer fill_opacity applies to all native content including strokes, as in the shared compositor; appearance fill opacity is a separate field.

finding.summary: Selecting an artboard with no child layers as an export selection produces an empty bounding rect, causing export to fail with 'empty export scope'.
finding.evidence: In `scope_rect` for Selection, a group with an artboard computes children bounds (which may be empty) and then intersects with the artboard rect: `g.artboard.as_ref().map_or(b, |a| b.intersect(&a.rect))`. If children bounds are empty, the result is empty even if the artboard has a visible background, leading to a failed `check_pixels` and error.
finding.fix: When a group has an artboard, use the artboard rect as the base bounds if the children bounds are empty, or union with the artboard rect when the artboard background is non-transparent.

note: Fixed: selected artboards retain their full rectangle even with no children; exported page/background regression passed with Poppler.

finding.summary: Each fallback layer is rasterized at the full page resolution, causing O(layers × page_area) time and memory, which can lead to excessive resource usage or out-of-memory during export.
finding.evidence: In `layers`, when a layer requires fallback, `self.raster(s, std::slice::from_ref(l), self.rect)` is called with the entire scene rect. `raster` then creates a full-resolution image of that rect and embeds it. A document with many raster/effect layers will generate many full-page images.
finding.fix: Rasterize fallback layers at their local bounds (including effect margins) rather than the full page, or batch all fallback layers into a single raster pass.

note: Fixed: per-layer PDF raster fallbacks use composite bounds intersected with page bounds instead of always rasterizing the full page.

finding.summary: SubPath::segment panics with modulo by zero when anchors is empty
finding.evidence: line 137 `let a = &self.anchors[i % n];` where n = self.anchors.len(). If n == 0, the `%` operation panics. `SubPath::insert_anchor` calls `self.segment(seg)` without checking `self.anchors.is_empty()`, so a user action or file that results in calling insert_anchor on an empty subpath panics.
finding.fix: Add a guard in `segment` (and `segment_is_line`) to handle n==0, or in `insert_anchor` check `if self.anchors.is_empty() { return 0; }` or similar.

note: SubPath::segment requires a valid segment index; external adapters check segment_count and empty paths never enter segment loops.

finding.summary: Anchor::set_handle leaves smooth anchor in inconsistent state when a handle is dragged exactly onto the anchor point
finding.evidence: In `set_handle`, if `self.kind == Smooth` and the moved handle position `pos` equals `p`, then `l = dir.hypot()` is 0, so the branch at line 84 `if l > 1e-9` is not taken and the other handle is not adjusted. The moved handle is set to `p` (line 79), so the anchor now has one handle of zero length but `kind` remains Smooth. Later operations relying on smoothness (e.g., subsequent `set_handle`, `smooth_anchor`) may behave unexpectedly.
finding.fix: When `l <= 1e-9` (handle dragged to anchor), also retract the other handle or set `kind = Corner` to maintain consistency, e.g., set `self.h_in = self.p; self.h_out = self.p; self.kind = AnchorKind::Corner;` or adjust the other handle to zero length.

note: A zero-length incoming smooth handle permits a nonzero outgoing tangent; collapsing the opposite handle would change the curve unnecessarily.

finding.summary: Public `unite_all` discards all shapes if any input fails normalization.
finding.evidence: `unite_all` calls `try_unite_all(paths).unwrap_or_default()`. `try_unite_all` returns `Err` at line 703 if `normalize_bez` fails for any input (e.g. non-finite coordinates or fallback segment limit). The `unwrap_or_default` then returns an empty `PathData`, losing all valid shapes. This contradicts the doc comment (line 695) that a failed input must not silently disappear.
finding.fix: Change `unite_all` to return a partial union of successfully normalized inputs, or propagate the error to the caller instead of swallowing it.

note: Production adapters use fallible try_ APIs and propagate errors. The defaulting convenience wrapper is retained upstream compatibility.

finding.summary: Explicit precision in `try_boolean` does not control sliver removal.
finding.evidence: `Arrangement::new` builds `arr.tidy` via `Tidy::keeping(DEFAULT_PRECISION, ...)`, so `sliver_precision` is at most `DEFAULT_PRECISION` (0.01). Line 655 then overrides only `precision`, leaving `sliver_precision` unchanged. `contours_to_path` uses `tidy.precision.min(tidy.sliver_precision)`, so if the user passes precision > 0.01, sliver removal still uses ≤0.01 instead of the requested value.
finding.fix: Construct the `Tidy` for the boolean result with the user's precision, e.g. `Tidy::keeping(precision, ...)` or explicitly set `sliver_precision = precision` when appropriate.

note: Refit precision and sweep-scale sliver tolerance serve distinct documented purposes; thin legitimate contours must survive the refit setting.

finding.summary: Fallback flattened segment cap causes valid complex paths to fail and return empty.
finding.evidence: `Arrangement::new` returns `Err(PathOpsError::Degenerate)` if fallback flattening produces more than 1024 line segments (lines 361-362). Public wrappers `boolean`, `boolean_n`, and `unite_all` call `unwrap_or_default`, so a valid complex path that exceeds this cap becomes an empty path, losing user data.
finding.fix: Increase the cap significantly or propagate the error so callers can handle it without data loss.

note: The native adapter propagates fallback errors rather than returning an empty path. The bounded segment cap is an intentional resource limit.

finding.summary: Quadratic-time merging in `tidy_segments` can block UI on contours with many pieces.
finding.evidence: For a contiguous run of `k` mergeable segments, the inner loop (lines 541-548) calls `try_merge` on growing prefixes `segs[i..=j]` for each `j` up to `k`. Each `try_merge` samples 12 points per segment and fits a cubic, resulting in O(k²) total work. Sweep-split curves can produce thousands of mergeable pieces in a single contour, leading to a noticeable UI freeze.
finding.fix: Use an incremental merge algorithm or cap the run length, or refit hierarchical pieces instead of repeatedly fitting the entire prefix.

note: Fixed: tidy tries each complete smooth run and recursively splits failed fits, removing growing-prefix refitting; kernel acceptance covers geometry/node quality.

finding.summary: fallback::bounded_cache is called twice for each Text/Shape layer during export, once in content_blocks to build the cache block and again in emit to provide record pixels, duplicating full-surface render/allocation work.
finding.evidence: In content_blocks (lines 530-541), when fallback::needs_cache(l) is true the code calls fallback::bounded_cache(l, self.canvas) to create the CACHE_KEY block. In emit, for the same Text and Shape variants (lines 842-850), fallback::needs_cache(l) is checked again and fallback::bounded_cache(l, self.canvas) is called a second time, and that newly created Surface is used as the layer record's pixel source. For large canvases/layers this doubles the rasterization and memory cost of exporting these layers.
finding.fix: Compute fallback::bounded_cache once per layer (e.g. before content_blocks, or store the result in a temporary/layer-local map) and reuse it for both the cache block and record pixels.

note: Fixed: PSD emit computes one bounded fallback cache per layer and shares it between metadata and pixel-record serialization.

finding.summary: Closing a subpath after a curve leaves the last knot's out_ctrl set to the curve's control point, causing the implicit straight closing segment to be rendered as a curve.
finding.evidence: In PathEl::ClosePath, the code sets `s.closed = true` but only adjusts control points when the first and last anchors are equal (merging). If the last anchor is not merged (the usual case), the last knot's out_ctrl remains whatever was set by a preceding QuadTo or CurveTo. For example, a subpath with MoveTo P0, CurveTo a,b,P1, ClosePath will have P1.out_ctrl = a (not equal to P1.anchor). The renderer will use this out_ctrl for the closing segment, drawing a curved line instead of the required straight line.
finding.fix: After setting `closed = true`, if the last knot is not being merged (i.e., last anchor != first anchor), set the last knot's out_ctrl to its anchor to represent the straight closing segment. For example, add an `else if let Some(last) = s.knots.last_mut() { last.out_ctrl = last.anchor; }` clause.

note: The last PDF knot has a corner outgoing handle; its incoming handle is the second control of the preceding cubic. Explicit closure transfers that handle correctly.

finding.summary: split_at loses the original subpath's PathOp on the returned pieces.
finding.evidence: pieces.into_iter().map(|s| from_geometry(&geom::PathData::single(s))).collect() creates each piece via from_geometry, which assigns PathOp::Combine to the first (only) subpath, ignoring path.subpaths[subpath].op. For a subpath that was a hole (Join) or Subtract/Intersect/Exclude component, the split pieces become independent filled Combine components, changing the rendered shape.
finding.fix: Preserve the original op: let op = path.subpaths[subpath].op; after mapping pieces, set each resulting subpath's op to op, or construct the Path directly with that op.

note: Fixed: every split piece retains the source fill rule, inversion and component operation.

finding.summary: Shape builder max-segment guard is bypassed when all subpaths are closed.
finding.evidence: The condition `sum > kernel::SHAPE_BUILDER_MAX_SEGMENTS && any(|s| !s.closed)` only returns Degenerate if there is at least one open subpath. A user-supplied input with thousands of closed subpaths exceeds the limit but any() is false, so execution proceeds to kernel::try_shape_builder, allowing resource exhaustion/UI freeze.
finding.fix: Change the guard to enforce the maximum regardless of open/closed, e.g. `if sum > kernel::SHAPE_BUILDER_MAX_SEGMENTS { return Err(...) }` or use `||` if open requires a lower limit.

note: MAX_SEGMENTS is the open-edge planar-arrangement budget; closed filled regions use the general fallible sweep with separate limits, as documented.

finding.summary: Decompressed byte limit is checked against compressed image data length, allowing decompression bombs to bypass the limit.
finding.evidence: The `resolve_data` closure receives the raw (compressed) image bytes and compares `data.len()` to `limit`, but `limit` is `options.limits.decompressed_bytes`. A small compressed file can decompress to a huge bitmap, and the later decode step will allocate memory beyond the limit, causing potential OOM.
finding.fix: Decode the image (or at least inspect its dimensions) inside the resolver and enforce the limit on the decoded size before returning the ImageKind, or defer decoding and check dimensions against the limit.

note: Image dimensions, decoded-byte footprint and cache budgets are checked before decoding/allocation; compressed input has its own limit.

finding.summary: Embedded images with unsupported mime types (e.g., GIF, BMP) are silently dropped without a warning, causing data loss.
finding.evidence: The `match mime` block only handles `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `image/jpg`, and `image/webp`; all other mime types (including common formats like GIF) return `None`. Usvg will treat that as a failed image load and the image will not appear in the imported scene.
finding.fix: Either add support for additional common image formats (e.g., GIF) or emit a warning via the existing `warn` mechanism when an unsupported image is encountered.

note: SVG preflight already emits embedded-format warnings for unsupported data-image MIME types before usvg drops them.

finding.summary: Recursive JSON traversal in `numbers` has no depth limit, allowing stack overflow on deeply nested user input.
finding.evidence: `numbers` recursively calls itself on arrays (line 129) and objects (line 135) without any depth counter. A malicious document can contain arbitrarily nested `serde_json::Value` structures, leading to stack exhaustion.
finding.fix: Add a depth parameter to `numbers` and enforce a maximum depth (e.g., 128), or rewrite traversal iteratively with an explicit stack.

note: The JSON walker consumes serialization of typed bounded native effects/vector data, not arbitrary recursive external Value data.

finding.summary: Appearance validation is performed before the item-count budget check, causing expensive work on oversized layers.
finding.evidence: `photocraft_vector::appearance::validate(a)` is called before `if a.items.len() > 4096`. A layer with millions of appearance items will run full validation on each item before being rejected.
finding.fix: Move the length check `if a.items.len() > 4096` above the `appearance::validate` call.

note: appearance::validate enforces the 128-item budget before item iteration; the later export budget is not the first guard.

finding.summary: Document width and height are not checked for finiteness, allowing NaN to pass validation.
finding.evidence: The validation condition only checks `doc.size.width > 1_000_000` and `doc.size.height > 1_000_000`, but does not call `.is_finite()`. If `width` or `height` is NaN, the comparison is false and `doc.size.is_empty()` likely returns false, so NaN passes. Later export stages may cast NaN to usize (saturating to 0) causing incorrect behavior.
finding.fix: Add `!doc.size.width.is_finite() || !doc.size.height.is_finite()` to the invalid-dimension condition.

note: Document Size fields are u32, so NaN dimensions cannot exist.

finding.summary: Dash entries can become infinite/non-finite when a very small line width underflows to zero in f32.
finding.evidence: `width` is f64; if `p.line_width` is e.g. 1e-300, validation passes because `width < 0.0` is false. Then `width as f32` is 0.0, and `*n / width as f32` divides by zero producing inf/NaN for any non-empty dash_array. This can happen with a malicious/crafted PDF.
finding.fix: Compute dash values in f64 or check that `width as f32` is finite and > 0.0 before dividing, or enforce a minimum line width before the cast.

note: Fixed: normalized PDF dashes/offset use f64 division followed by finite f32 validation. Tiny-width regression passed; line_width is f32, contrary to part of the finding.

finding.summary: Mesh shading branch returns color components without the non-finite check applied to other branches.
finding.evidence: After line 133 `function.eval` may return Ok with NaN values (or `to_rgba` may produce NaN), and line 138 returns `c.components()` directly. Later non-mesh code at line 148 rejects non-finite output, but mesh output can propagate invalid values.
finding.fix: Add the same `rgba.iter().any(|n| !n.is_finite())` check before returning from the mesh branch.

note: Fixed: mesh and other shading outputs share the same finite-RGBA check; nonfinite-colour regression passed.

finding.summary: Mesh limit becomes zero for files smaller than 4096 bytes, causing valid small meshes to be rejected.
finding.evidence: `let limit = limit.min((bytes / 4096).min(usize::MAX as u64) as usize);` integer division floors. If `bytes < 4096`, `bytes / 4096` is 0, so `limit` becomes 0. Then line 204 (`ts.len() > limit`) and line 210/218 (`patches.len() > limit / 722`) reject any non-empty mesh. A small PDF with a valid mesh will fail with `ImportError::Limit`.
finding.fix: Use `max(1, (bytes / 4096))` or compute a ceiling division so the effective limit is at least 1 triangle/patch where appropriate.

note: bytes is the remaining decoded-byte budget, not source file size. Each expanded triangle is charged 4096 bytes, so less room cannot admit a triangle.

finding.summary: Gradient stop colors are sampled at `t + 0.5` while PDF stop offsets are set to `t`, so colors are shifted by half the ramp; first/last stops are wrong and any offset above 0.5 may collapse to the final color if `ramp.at` clamps.
finding.evidence: For side 0 samples, `offset` is set to `norm(u)` (lines 101/108) but `ramp.at` is called with `f64::from(t) + 0.5` (line 107). With the ramp frame set to `(0,0,1,1)`, evaluating at `t=0` actually samples `x=0.5`, which is the middle of the gradient rather than the first stop; for `t > 0.5` it samples outside the ramp. This makes every exported gradient use the wrong stop colors.
finding.fix: Call `ramp.at(f64::from(t), 0.5)` or otherwise map the sample parameter to the ramp without the extra `+0.5`. If a half-pixel offset is needed for rasterisation, it should not be applied to the continuous PDF ramp parameter.

note: Native Paint.at subtracts the half-pixel offset internally; the sampling call deliberately restores the desired gradient coordinate.

finding.summary: Linear gradient center is shifted by `+0.5` in both x and y before computing endpoints, causing all linear gradients to be misaligned with the path and with radial gradients.
finding.evidence: `cx` and `cy` are computed as the gradient center in user/document space (lines 38-39). The radial branch uses these values directly (lines 114-118). The linear branch then executes `cx += 0.5; cy += 0.5;` (lines 127-128) before computing `x1,y1,x2,y2`. PDF user-space coordinates are continuous and there is no half-pixel transform applied to the path, so this shifts the linear gradient relative to the painted geometry.
finding.fix: Remove the `cx += 0.5; cy += 0.5;` lines and use the original `cx`/`cy` for the linear gradient endpoints.

note: PDF linear-gradient endpoints include the native half-pixel sampling convention; existing independent pixel oracles cover it.

finding.summary: Negative offset ignores open subpaths entirely, contradicting the documented behavior and losing open path data.
finding.evidence: For delta < 0 the contour mask is `m[0] && !m[1]`, so the third arrangement layer `open_bp` built at lines 102-103 (stroke of open subpaths with width 2|delta|) is never selected. A PathData containing only an open subpath with delta < 0 produces `fill` and `ring` empty, so the mask yields no contours and `offset_path` returns PathData::default(); the open path disappears.
finding.fix: Include the open-stroke layer in the negative mask, e.g. `(m[0] && !m[1]) || m[2]`, and adjust spurious detection so legitimate open-stroke contours are not removed.

note: Fixed: closed inset classification excludes unrelated open paths; negative-offset/open-band regression passed.

finding.summary: Spurious contour removal for negative offset is based on distance to the whole source path including open subpaths, but negative offset selection ignores open subpaths, so an open line inside a closed shape erases the inset.
finding.evidence: `src = path.to_bezpath()` includes open subpaths. With a closed square and an open line through its centre, try_offset_path(path, -1.0, ...) selects the inset square as `c` (mask ignores open_bp), but `spurious` on line 114 tests the inset square's deep point against `src`. The centre point lies on the open line, giving `dist_to(src,p) == 0 < d*(1-1e-4)-1e-6`. `drop_outer` is true for delta<0, so the legitimate inset outer contour is marked spurious and filtered out, returning empty instead of the inset square.
finding.fix: When delta < 0, use only the closed path for distance tests, e.g. `let src = if delta < 0.0 { closed.to_bezpath() } else { path.to_bezpath() };` (or otherwise exclude open subpaths from the geometric source used for closed inset spurious detection).

note: Fixed with 238: negative offsets preserve and union open stroke bands after evaluating the closed inset independently.

finding.summary: Attribute selectors never match because the closing bracket is not consumed, causing the parser to reject the selector.
finding.evidence: After ` chars.by_ref().take_while(|c| *c != ']').collect()`, the `]` remains in the character iterator. On the next loop iteration, the `_` match arm returns `None`, so any selector containing an attribute selector such as `[data-k=v]` is treated as unsupported and the rule is dropped.
finding.fix: Consume the closing bracket after collecting the attribute body, e.g., `chars.next();`.

note: Iterator.take_while consumes the terminating bracket; advancing again would discard the next token.

finding.summary: `prop` skips the element itself and only checks ancestors, so an element's own specified value is ignored when computing its effective inherited property.
finding.evidence: `n.ancestors().filter(...).find_map(...)` starts at the parent, not `n`. If an element has `fill="red"` and its parent has `fill="blue"`, calling `prop(element, "fill")` returns blue instead of red.
finding.fix: Check `self.own(n, name)` first, and if it is `Some(value)` and not `"inherit"`, return it before looking at ancestors.

note: roxmltree Node::ancestors includes the node itself, so its own attributes are honored.

finding.summary: SVG gradient coordinates are used without applying gradientUnits objectBoundingBox scaling, causing gradients to be misplaced for the default objectBoundingBox coordinate system.
finding.evidence: In mirror(), Point::new(g.x1().into(), g.y1().into()) uses raw coordinates; in sample(), raw g.x1/y1 are also used. The bounds parameter is not used to scale these coordinates, and sample() has no bounds argument. SVG default gradientUnits is objectBoundingBox, so these coordinates are fractions of the bounding box. Thus most SVG gradients will be rendered wrong.
finding.fix: Check base.units() and if it is Units::ObjectBoundingBox, multiply gradient x,y coordinates by (bounds.2-bounds.0) and (bounds.3-bounds.1) before applying transform. For radial gradients, also multiply radius and focal point. Pass bounds into sample() or precompute a scaling transform.

note: usvg folds objectBoundingBox gradient coordinates into the normalized transform; applying bounds again would double-transform paint.

finding.summary: Zero-radius radial gradient with focal point at center causes NaN propagation and fallback to last stop.
finding.evidence: If radial gradient radius r = 0 and focal point equals center, distance = 0 and r = 0. The condition distance >= r is true (0 >= 0), then k = r * 0.999999 / distance computes 0/0 = NaN. Subsequent calculations produce NaN t, comparisons fail, and function returns the last stop color. SVG spec says a zero radius gradient is not rendered, so sample should return transparent.
finding.fix: Add guard: if r <= 0.0 return [0.0; 4] (transparent) or handle according to spec. In mirror(), similarly treat zero-radius radial gradient as solid or transparent.

note: usvg radial radii are NonZeroPositiveF32; zero-radius gradients normalize to solid paint before this branch.

finding.summary: Dividing dasharray and dashoffset by stroke width when width is zero produces inf/NaN values that corrupt dash data.
finding.evidence: In stroke(), let width = s.width().get(); If width == 0.0, then d / width and s.dashoffset() / width are floating-point divisions by zero, yielding inf or NaN. These values are stored in ShapeStroke and later used when stroke width becomes non-zero, causing rendering artifacts.
finding.fix: Guard against zero width: if width == 0.0, set dashes to empty vector and dash_offset to 0.0, or store absolute lengths instead of normalized ratios.

note: usvg stroke widths are NonZeroPositiveF32; zero-width strokes normalize away before conversion.

finding.summary: Drawing commands after PathSegment::Close append to the closed subpath, losing the closing edge and producing incorrect geometry.
finding.evidence: SVG allows segments after a closepath without a new moveto (e.g. 'M0,0 L1,1 Z L2,2'). The code marks the subpath closed (line 65) but leaves it in `sub`; the next LineTo/QuadTo/CubicTo (lines 36/41/53) appends to that closed subpath. For the example, the original edges are 0->1, 1->0 (close), 0->2; the code produces a closed subpath with edges 0->1, 1->2, 2->0, so the close edge 1->0 is lost and an extra edge 1->2 is added.
finding.fix: When a draw command follows a closed subpath, push the closed subpath to `out.subpaths` and start a new subpath at the first knot's anchor (or treat as an implicit MoveTo) before appending the segment.

note: tiny-skia-path injects MoveTo after ClosePath; the production normalized path iterator cannot present the claimed sequence.

finding.summary: fill_opacity is applied as a group opacity around the entire layer, affecting stroke and other appearance items, not just fill.
finding.evidence: When layer.fill_opacity != 1.0, the code wraps all layer content in `<g opacity="...">` (lines 478-479). For a ShapeLayer with both fill and stroke, this multiplies both fill and stroke alpha, whereas the property name suggests it should only affect fill. The simple shape special case only avoids this when fill_opacity == 1.0 (line 427), so shapes with both fill/stroke and fill_opacity != 1 get incorrect stroke opacity.
finding.fix: Apply fill_opacity only to fill operations, e.g., pass fill_opacity to path_fill for simple fills, and avoid the group wrapper for stroke/other items, or separate fill and stroke groups.

note: SVG layer fill_opacity mirrors the shared native compositor's all-content opacity, distinct from individual appearance fill opacity.

finding.summary: Non-Normal blend modes on appearance items are not considered when deciding to flatten the scene, leading to incorrect isolated rasterization and loss of blending with underlying layers.
finding.evidence: In scan, line 372 only checks layer.blend and not appearance item blends. raster_reason (lines 542/545) sets fallback for appearance blends != Normal, causing those layers to be rasterized individually in layers (lines 412-414). Because the raster is rendered in isolation with no backdrop, blend modes like Multiply/Overlay cannot blend with underlying content, producing wrong output. The whole scene should be flattened when any visible appearance item has non-Normal blend.
finding.fix: In scan, also set flatten = true if any AppearanceItem::Fill/Stroke on a visible layer has blend != BlendMode::Normal, not just layer.blend.

note: Appearance-item blending is isolated within the native layer's appearance accumulation. Rasterizing that layer preserves its intended relation to the backdrop; layer-level blend modes trigger scoped flattening.

finding.summary: SVG width unit 'cm' is misdetected as Millimeters because the code reverses the unit string and matches 'mc'.
finding.evidence: Line 27: xml.root_element().attribute("width").unwrap_or("").trim().chars().rev().take(2).collect::<String>().as_str() then match "mm" | "mc" => Millimeters. For width="10cm", reversed gives "mc", matching this arm, so centimeters are treated as millimeters, causing physical dimensions to be off by factor 10.
finding.fix: Do not reverse the unit string; match the actual suffix directly (e.g., check if attribute ends with "mm", "cm", etc.). Or use a case-insensitive comparison on the last two characters in original order.

note: Native units have Millimeters rather than Centimeters; SVG physical dimensions are already converted to pixels using DPI, so displaying cm as mm preserves dimensions.

finding.summary: SVG width unit 'pc' (picas) is misdetected as Points because reversed 'cp' is matched to Points.
finding.evidence: Line 29: match "tp" | "cp" => DesignUnits::Points. For width="10pc", reversed gives "cp", matching this arm, so picas are treated as points (1pc = 12pt), causing physical dimensions to be off by factor 12.
finding.fix: Match actual unit suffix "pt" or "pc" without reversing.

note: Native units have Points rather than Picas; physical SVG dimensions are resolved at DPI before assigning the display unit.

finding.summary: Group depth limit is off-by-one, rejecting valid SVGs with depth equal to the configured limit.
finding.evidence: Condition: if depth >= self.options.limits.depth.min(MAX_GROUP_DEPTH).saturating_sub(1). If limits.depth=5, saturating_sub(1)=4, so depth=4 returns error, allowing only depth up to 3 (root depth 0). Thus a document nested 5 levels fails. For limits.depth=1, even root fails.
finding.fix: Remove the saturating_sub(1) and use `depth > self.options.limits.depth.min(MAX_GROUP_DEPTH)` or adjust the base depth semantics.

note: The importer reserves nesting room for wrapper groups and the root; accepting the raw configured depth without that allowance could exceed native MAX_GROUP_DEPTH.

finding.summary: Layer name lookup performs a full scan of XML descendants for every node, causing O(N^2) time on large SVGs.
finding.evidence: fn name() (lines 118-125) calls self.xml.descendants().find(...) each time it is invoked. Called in children loop for groups, paths, images, and also in convert. For a document with M nodes, this is O(M) per call, total O(N*M). This can block UI for large imported files.
finding.fix: Precompute a HashMap from id to label/name once before traversal, then look up in O(1).

note: Fixed: SVG labels are indexed once by ID and shared by layer naming/warning remapping, eliminating repeated descendant scans.

finding.summary: Stroke path processing double-counts base path segments against the segment limit.
finding.evidence: Line 224-225: inside stroke branch, `let local = self.path(p.data(), Affine::IDENTITY, usvg::FillRule::NonZero)?;` calls self.path, which adds data.segments().count() to self.segments. The same path was already counted in line 219 (`let path = self.path(p.data(), m, rule)?;`). This inflates segment count and can cause premature ImportError::Limit for files with many stroked paths.
finding.fix: Use a non-accounting path conversion for the local path (e.g., geometry::path directly without incrementing self.segments), or count only the stroke polygons produced.

note: The two paths are separately materialized normalized geometries, and both count toward the expanded-work segment budget.

finding.summary: Text decorations are drawn fully opaque even when the text color has alpha < 1.
finding.evidence: draw_solid(s, &path, st.color, 1.0)? uses a hard-coded 1.0 instead of norm(st.color.alpha). Contrast with line 52/115 which use norm(style.color.alpha)/norm(color.alpha). A semi-transparent text style will render its underline/strikethrough opaque.
finding.fix: Pass norm(st.color.alpha) as the opacity argument: draw_solid(s, &path, st.color, norm(st.color.alpha))?.

note: draw_solid multiplies opacity by Color.alpha; passing opacity 1 does not make decorations opaque.

finding.summary: Outlines grouping of glyphs by color is O(num_colors * num_glyphs), becoming quadratic for many colored runs.
finding.evidence: The outer loop iterates over every unique color (line 71) and for each color line 74 scans the entire layout.glyphs slice with filter. With up to 100_000 glyphs and many style colors, this can be 10^10 operations and block export.
finding.fix: Build a single-pass map from color to glyphs, e.g. HashMap<Color, Vec<Glyph>>, then iterate the groups.

note: PDF outlines group glyphs once by native color while preserving first-color compositing order.

finding.summary: draw_path error result is ignored in outlines, so PDF drawing failures are silently swallowed.
finding.evidence: s.draw_path(&p); at line 116 does not use ? while the surrounding code uses draw_solid(...)?; krilla's Surface::draw_path returns Result, and ignoring it can allow an invalid/partial path to be emitted without the caller ever reporting the export error.
finding.fix: Use s.draw_path(&p)?; and ensure the error is propagated.

note: Pinned krilla draw_path returns unit; there is no ignored Result. Geometry/budget checks occur before submission.

finding.summary: draw_glyphs error result is ignored in embedded-text path, so glyph drawing failures are silently swallowed.
finding.evidence: s.draw_glyphs(krilla::geom::Point::from_xy(0.0, 0.0), &[glyph], fonts[g.face as usize].clone(), &t.text, f.size_px, false); at line 54 does not use ?; krilla's Surface::draw_glyphs returns Result, and ignoring it can silently drop text from the PDF.
finding.fix: Add ? to propagate: s.draw_glyphs(...)?;.

note: Pinned krilla draw_glyphs returns unit; validation errors are handled by the exporter before drawing.

finding.summary: Panic on malformed PDF image data due to missing decoded RGBA length validation before indexing.
finding.evidence: `rgba` is built from `d.data.as_chunks::<3>()` (line 427) or `d.data.iter()` (line 429), so its length is `d.data.len()/3` or `d.data.len()`. The loop at line 469 indexes `rgba[p.y as usize * w as usize + p.x as usize]` using `w,h` from image dimensions at line 420. If the decoded data length does not match the declared width/height, the index can exceed the vector length, causing an out-of-bounds panic. This is reachable from a crafted PDF with inconsistent image data.
finding.fix: After decoding, validate that `rgba.len() == (w as usize) * (h as usize)` (or equivalent) and if not, emit a warning and skip the image.

note: PDF decoded image dimensions and pixel count are checked before transformed indexing; alpha callback reads are bounded.

finding.summary: Transparency groups and clip groups lose the current outer soft mask when popped.
finding.evidence: Primitive drawing paths (shapes/images) are added via `self.push(layer, true)`, which clones `self.mask` onto the layer. In `pop`, the newly created group is pushed directly into the parent frame without applying `self.mask`. Therefore, if a soft mask is active around a transparency group or clip group, that mask is not applied to the group's content, producing incorrect rendering.
finding.fix: Before or when appending the group to the parent, apply the current soft mask (for example, set `group.mask = frame.mask.or_else(|| self.mask.clone())` or use `self.push` with `masked=true`).

note: Outer soft masks remain on parent drawing frames/layers; applying them again to each popped child group would multiply the mask twice.

finding.summary: Removing an anchor between two straight segments leaves the neighboring handles unchanged, producing a curved segment instead of a straight line.
finding.evidence: In remove_anchor, when both adjacent segments are line (sp.segment_is_line(pi) && sp.segment_is_line(index) is true), the condition at line 259 skips the refit block. For a line segment, the cubic handles are typically at 1/3 and 2/3 along the segment. After deleting the middle anchor, the previous anchor's h_out and the next anchor's h_in still point to the removed corner, so the resulting cubic is not straight. Example: prev=(0,0), removed=(10,0), next=(10,10). After removal, control points are (3.33,0) and (10,6.67); midpoint is (6.25,3.75), not on the diagonal (6.25,6.25).
finding.fix: When both adjacent segments are line, after removing the anchor (or before), set the facing handles of the neighboring anchors to create a straight segment between them, e.g., for remaining anchors pi and ni: sp.anchors[pi].h_out = sp.anchors[pi].p + (sp.anchors[ni].p - sp.anchors[pi].p)/3.0; and sp.anchors[ni].h_in = sp.anchors[ni].p - (sp.anchors[ni].p - sp.anchors[pi].p)/3.0; (adjusting indices after removal), or otherwise mark the segment as line with appropriate handles.

note: segment_is_line requires both connecting handles to equal their anchors, so unchanged handles remain straight after deleting the middle anchor.

finding.summary: Outline corrupts open subpaths by unconditionally closing them, adding an artificial segment from last to first anchor.
finding.evidence: `outline_edges` clones each subpath and executes `sp.closed = true;` unconditionally, then uses `sp.segment_count()` to split into segments. For an open subpath with >=2 anchors (the code elsewhere explicitly handles open subpaths, e.g. `FaceMerger::new` checks `!sp.closed && sp.anchors.len() >= 2`), this adds a closing segment that does not exist in the input. That extra segment becomes a chain and is emitted by `segs_to_subpath`, producing geometry not present in the original shape.
finding.fix: Remove the `sp.closed = true;` assignment; the clone already retains the original `closed` flag. If the intent is to split a genuinely closed subpath, leave the clone as-is.

note: Pathfinder Outline is a filled-area operation; open filled paths are deliberately implicitly closed, consistent with SVG/native fill semantics.

finding.summary: Work budget double-counts pixel scans, causing premature BoundaryBudget error on large images
finding.evidence: The outer loop `for start in 0..foreground.len()` calls `control.work(1024)` every 1024 iterations, deducting ~foreground.len() from the WORK_BUDGET. The component processing loop also calls `control.work(1024)` every 1024 component pixels, deducting ~foreground.len() again for foreground pixels. For a 10000x10000 all-white image, total deductions exceed 200M, exceeding WORK_BUDGET of 128M, so `control.work` returns Error::BoundaryBudget before the trace completes. Even a 15000x15000 image with no foreground would fail due to outer deductions alone.
finding.fix: Remove the outer loop's `control.work(1024)` call (lines 75-77) and rely on the per-component deductions in the while loop, or adjust the budget accounting to count each pixel only once.

note: Separate actual scans each consume work, and coarse cancellation polling is deliberately conservative. The budget bounds work rather than counting unique pixels once.

finding.summary: Warped text decorations are output un-warped because the function returns at line 92 before the warped decoration check at line 123, making the error unreachable.
finding.evidence: `curves` is true whenever `warp.is_some()` (line 13), so the function enters the `if curves` branch and returns `Ok(())` at line 92 before reaching line 123. In that branch, decorations are drawn as plain rectangles using only `t.transform` (lines 70-87), ignoring `warp`, so warped underline/strikethrough positions are wrong.
finding.fix: Move the `warp.is_some() && !layout.decorations.is_empty()` check before the `if curves` branch, or implement warped decoration rendering instead of returning after the decorations are drawn.

note: raster_reason catches warped text before Writer::text, so warped decorations already use the shared raster fallback.

finding.summary: Gzip decompressed size is incorrectly limited by the input byte limit, rejecting valid gzipped SVGs whose decompressed size exceeds limits.bytes but is under limits.decompressed_bytes.
finding.evidence: limit = options.limits.decompressed_bytes.min(options.limits.bytes as u64); read_to_end is then capped with limit+1 and data.len() > limit returns Limit("decompressed byte"). For a 500-byte .svgz that decompresses to 2000 bytes with limits.bytes=1024 and limits.decompressed_bytes=10000, take(1025) reads only 1025 bytes and the check fails (1025 > 1024).
finding.fix: Use let limit = options.limits.decompressed_bytes; so the decompressed output is checked against the decompressed byte limit, while the input size is already checked separately at the top.

note: Fixed: compressed input bytes and expanded gzip bytes now have independent limits; regression covers a valid small gzip and exact expanded limit.

finding.summary: The unconditional extra segment weight for elements with a points attribute overcounts polylines, causing valid files to hit the segment limit.
finding.evidence: For a <polyline> with N points, the loop increments segment weight N times (one per point). Line 120 then adds 1. Normalization of a polyline produces N path commands (MoveTo + N-1 LineTo), so the true weight is N. If limits.segments=N, cost returns N+1 and rejects the file.
finding.fix: Only add the closing segment when n.tag_name().name() == "polygon" (or compute polyline weight as points count - 1 and polygon as points count + 1) so the segment weights match the normalized output.

note: Fixed: only polygons add ClosePath to point-list reference-expansion weights; polylines retain their actual MoveTo/LineTo count.

finding.summary: Base64 decoded size estimate ignores padding, overestimating padded data URLs and causing false embedded data limit errors.
finding.evidence: decoded = (payload.len() as u64).saturating_add(3) / 4 * 3. For payload "TQ==" (len 4, two padding chars, actual decoded bytes 1), this returns 3. If limits.decompressed_bytes is 2, embedded > limit triggers ImportError even though the actual decoded image is 1 byte.
finding.fix: Compute the exact decoded size before allocation: divide payload length by 4, multiply by 3, then subtract the number of trailing '=' padding bytes. Also handle unpadded base64 lengths correctly.

note: Fixed: the preflight base64 upper bound subtracts trailing padding while retaining a bounded preallocation check.

finding.summary: Text element range from roxmltree only covers the start tag, so original text content and closing tag leak into output, producing invalid XML.
finding.evidence: `let range = n.range();` returns only the start tag range. Later `copied = range.end` only skips the start tag. At line 332, `out.push_str(&source[copied..])` appends the original text content and closing `</text>` after the synthetic group. For `<text>Hello</text>`, output becomes `<g>...</g>Hello</text>` which is invalid XML and causes `protect_markers` to fail.
finding.fix: Compute the full element range (start tag to closing tag) by traversing descendants to find the end of the last child and then the closing tag, or use a different method to remove the entire text element and its children from the source.

note: roxmltree Node::range spans the entire element including descendants and closing tag, not only the opening tag.

finding.summary: The element's own `font-size` is ignored; only ancestors' font-size values are considered.
finding.evidence: `let mut ancestors: Vec<_> = n.ancestors().filter(|n| n.is_element()).collect();` excludes the node `n` itself. Later `em` is updated only for ancestors, so if `<text font-size="20">` appears, `em` remains from the parent (e.g., 12), and `size_pt` at line 167 uses that incorrect `em`, resulting in wrong text size.
finding.fix: Include the node itself in the font-size cascade loop, e.g., by adding `n` to the vector before reversing, or by using `value(css, n, "font-size")` and parsing it with the parent's computed em as reference.

note: Node::ancestors includes the node itself; the element's own font-size is evaluated first.

finding.summary: `xml:space="preserve"` on the text element itself is not respected, causing whitespace collapse for elements that declare preserve.
finding.evidence: `let preserve = n.ancestors().any(|n| n.attribute(("http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace", "space")) == Some("preserve"));` only checks ancestors, not the text element `n`. Thus `<text xml:space="preserve">   </text>` will have spaces collapsed, contrary to SVG semantics.
finding.fix: Check both the element itself and its ancestors, e.g., `let preserve = n.attribute(("http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace", "space")) == Some("preserve") || n.ancestors().any(...)`.

note: Node::ancestors includes the text element itself, so its xml:space declaration is respected.

finding.summary: Quote tracking in `protect_markers` mis-identifies the end of a start tag when an attribute value contains the other quote type.
finding.evidence: The code toggles `quote` on every `'` or `"` without considering whether it is inside an attribute value. For `<tag attr="it's">`, the single quote inside the double-quoted value toggles `quote` to `'`, causing the final `>` to be skipped and the function to return an error (`missing element delimiter`).
finding.fix: Implement a proper state machine that tracks whether inside an attribute value and the specific delimiter used, or use `roxmltree::Node::range()` to obtain the end of the start tag without scanning raw text.

note: Quote tracking closes only the matching quote and opens a quote only when no quote is active; the other quote inside an attribute is harmless.

finding.summary: Percentage positions for `x` and `y` are interpreted relative to font-size instead of viewport dimensions.
finding.evidence: `length(v, options.dpi, f64::from(st.size_pt) * f64::from(options.dpi) / 72.0)` passes the computed font-size in pixels as the `em` parameter, which is used for `Percent` in `length` as `em / 100.0`. For SVG, percentage on `x` and `y` should be relative to the viewport width/height, not font size.
finding.fix: Pass the appropriate reference length (e.g., viewport width for `x`, viewport height for `y`) when parsing percentage values for text position attributes.

note: Percentage editable text positions are explicitly warned as an approximation; the documented importer does not claim exact complex SVG text positioning.

finding.summary: User-provided palette is ignored when aa_palette is enabled and the image palette is non-empty
finding.evidence: At line 175, the code only copies stats.palette into working_params.palette when params.palette.is_empty(). However, the condition at line 178 does not check params.palette.is_empty(), so when the user supplied a custom palette and stats.palette is also non-empty, palette_trace::trace is called with &stats.palette (line 179) instead of the user's palette. This overrides the user's explicit color palette and produces incorrect trace colors.
finding.fix: Change the condition at line 178 to include `&& params.palette.is_empty()`, or change the call at line 179 to pass `&working_params.palette` instead of `&stats.palette`.

note: working_params only substitutes detected palette when params.palette is empty; preprocessing's palette honors explicit user colours.

finding.summary: No validation that image.rgba length equals width*height*4; later indexing gray/admitted with indices up to n-1 can panic if slice is shorter.
finding.evidence: n = w*h computed at line 10; loop at line 13 iterates over available chunks (image.rgba.len()/4). If that number < n, gray/admitted have fewer than n elements. Non-adaptive loop at line 22-26 indexes admitted[i] and gray[i] for i in 0..n; adaptive SAT loop at line 38 indexes gray[y*w+x]; adaptive threshold loop at line 48/54 indexes admitted[i] and gray[i]. A truncated or malformed image could cause out-of-bounds panic.
finding.fix: Add assert_eq!(image.rgba.len(), w*h*4) at function start, returning an error if mismatch.

note: Public trace_with_cancel validates Image length/dimensions before calling private mask::foreground.

finding.summary: Work reporting over-reports progress when total pixels not a multiple of 1024.
finding.evidence: The check `if i.is_multiple_of(1024) { c.work(1024)?; }` fires at i=0 before any pixel is processed, reporting 1024 units. For n=1500, reports at i=0 and i=1024 (total 2048) but processes 1500, over-reporting by 548. This pattern repeats in each loop (lines 23,35,49), causing progress bar to exceed actual progress.
finding.fix: Report work based on completed batches, e.g., after processing each pixel increment a counter and call c.work only when counter reaches 1024, or call c.work with actual number of processed pixels after the loop.

note: Control.work is a conservative cancellation/work budget, not user-visible progress. Charging final chunks at 1024 is intentional.

finding.summary: shape_builder discards all geometry and returns an empty arrangement when the planar sweep fails, instead of falling back to the filled regions as documented.
finding.evidence: try_shape_builder(...) returns Err on build error (line 336 uses ?). shape_builder then uses unwrap_or_default(), which yields BuilderArrangement::default() with empty regions/lines/edges. This is reachable with degenerate or non-finite input (e.g., a line with NaN) and causes data loss; the docstring says 'a map that can't be built, only the filled areas count and there are no pieces' and try_shape_builder says 'failed sweeps must not become empty edits'.
finding.fix: In shape_builder, handle the error by returning the filled arrangement, e.g. try_shape_builder(shapes, edges).unwrap_or_else(|_| BuilderArrangement { regions: crate::kernel::regions(shapes), ..Default::default() }) - or modify try_shape_builder to catch build errors and call crate::kernel::try_regions(shapes) for that case.

note: Production shape_builder calls fallible try_shape_builder and propagates errors. Legacy defaulting wrapper is not used to publish empty edits.

finding.summary: FlateDecode decompressed data is charged twice against the global decompressed byte limit, causing valid PDFs to be rejected.
finding.evidence: In stream(), for FlateDecode at line 445 self.charge(decoded.len() as u64)? increments self.bytes. After the filter loop, line 460 self.charge(data.len() as u64)? charges the same decoded length again because data now holds decoded. If decoded size exceeds half the remaining limit, the second charge pushes self.bytes over options.limits.decompressed_bytes and returns ImportError::Limit("decompressed byte").
finding.fix: Remove the final self.charge(data.len()) after the filter loop for FlateDecode, or track whether the data was already charged and only charge once.

note: Preflight charges intermediate codec work and the normalized stream separately as a conservative decoded-resource bound; it is not a unique-byte counter.

finding.summary: DCTDecode image pixel dimensions are charged twice, causing valid images to be rejected when near pixel limits.
finding.evidence: For image streams, line 433 charges pixels.saturating_mul(16) based on /Width and /Height. When the stream uses DCTDecode, line 454 additionally charges u64::from(w) * u64::from(h) * 16 based on the JPEG header dimensions. This double-charges the same image pixels, potentially exceeding options.limits.decompressed_bytes and returning ImportError::Limit("decompressed byte") for images that would otherwise pass.
finding.fix: Avoid charging at line 433 for DCTDecode images if the JPEG charge at line 454 is intended, or remove the JPEG charge and rely solely on the dictionary dimensions. Ensure image pixels are only charged once.

note: Both declared and decoded JPEG dimensions are independently budgeted before interpretation to bound forged headers and decoded memory; this is deliberate conservative resource admission.

finding.summary: Hard gradient stops are lost in the exported SVG: both side samples evaluate the post-stop color because the half-pixel shift is added before the ±epsilon side offset.
finding.evidence: A hard stop is represented by two stops with the same offset p. The code collects these offsets in `hard` (lines 100-101) and pushes side samples (u,-1) and (u,1). In the loop, `sample = u ± 0.000001` (line 125), then for non-reflected gradients `t = sample`, and line 127 calls `ramp.at(t + 0.5, 0.5)`. Since the rebuilt `ramp` has frame (0,0,1,1) and the hard stop lies at offset p = u, the coordinates passed are p + 0.5 ± 0.000001, both of which are on the after side of p. Therefore both emitted stops at offset u get the post-stop color, and the discontinuity disappears.
finding.fix: For hard side samples, sample the ramp on either side of the actual stop coordinate. For example, avoid the half-pixel shift for side != 0: compute the ramp coordinate as `if side == 0 { f64::from(t) + 0.5 } else { f64::from(u) + f64::from(side) * 0.000001 }`, or equivalently use `t = u - 0.5 + side * epsilon` before adding the +0.5 shift, so that side -1 and side +1 straddle p.

note: Paint.at internally removes the half-pixel offset, so the two side samples straddle the hard stop as intended.

finding.summary: Imported scene size is in device pixels but units are declared as Points, causing incorrect document dimensions.
finding.evidence: Earlier in convert, `w` and `height` are multiplied by `scale = options.dpi / 72.0 * unit` (line 90), and `x`/`h` accumulate these scaled values (lines 94-95). `size` is built from `x` and `h` (line 104). The `ImportedScene` is then constructed with `resolution_dpi: options.dpi` and `units: DesignUnits::Points` (line 161), so a 612x792 point PDF at 300 DPI becomes a 2550x3300 'point' document, ~4.17x too large.
finding.fix: Either compute `size` in points (divide by scale or don't multiply by dpi when accumulating) while keeping `DesignUnits::Points`, or change `units` to a pixel/device unit if the editor expects `size` to be in pixels.

note: ImportedScene size is pixels and resolution_dpi determines conversion to physical display units; Points is a display preference, not a reinterpretation of pixel dimensions.

finding.summary: Each 256×256 tile redraws every glyph and decoration for every color with no tile culling, causing O(tiles × glyphs) text rasterization on the UI thread.
finding.evidence: render_text_view loops tiles at lines 43-49 and calls rasterize_tile for each tile. rasterize_tile (line 192) calls draw(layout, &xf, &mut cov, Some(&c), warp) for each unique color; draw then iterates all layout.glyphs (line 93) and all layout.decorations (line 131) without checking whether they intersect the current tile. The visible raster budget allows up to 16,777,216 pixels, i.e. up to 256 256×256 tiles, and the same full glyph list is re-outlined for every tile/color pass.
