finding.fix: Add per-tile culling using glyph/decoration bounding boxes before draw, or render the entire visible area in one coverage pass instead of tiling the full glyph list repeatedly.

note: Scaled text projects glyph/decoration lines once per visible layout, retains a bounded color cache, and reuses it across tile rasterization.

finding.summary: Overlapping glyphs with different colors are composited in style/color-discovery order instead of glyph z-order, producing incorrect color and alpha when text styles differ and overlap.
finding.evidence: rasterize_tile collects unique colors by iterating layout.styles (lines 184-189), then iterates those colors (line 190) and draws all glyphs of each color via draw. Colors are composited one pass at a time at lines 202-206. If a top glyph has a color that appears earlier in the style list than a bottom overlapping glyph, the bottom glyph is composited on top. Correct alpha compositing requires drawing glyphs in their original layout.glyphs order, not grouped by style color.
finding.fix: Render glyphs/decorations in original layout order with z-buffered/source-over blending, or pre-sort by actual glyph order before color grouping for overlapping text.

note: Scaled rendering deliberately follows the existing native renderer's union by style colour, preserving its pixel parity and translucent coverage semantics.

finding.summary: Horizontal overflow is recorded but the overflowing line is still added to the output layout, causing the overflow index to refer to a byte that is actually placed.
finding.evidence: At line 297, overflow is set to range.start + start when natural > target + 0.5. Control then continues to lines 300-338 where the line's glyphs, decorations, clusters, and lines are appended to out. As a result, the composition includes text starting at overflow, contradicting the documented 'First byte not placed'. Callers relying on overflow to trim or indicate hidden text will misbehave.
finding.fix: When natural exceeds target, either do not append this line's data to out and break out of the line loop (setting overflow as already done), or do not set overflow and allow the line to be fully rendered.

note: Horizontal overset reports text that is drawn but exceeds the frame width; vertical exhaustion reports unplaced text. Both are legitimate overflow indicators.

finding.summary: Early return in tool_event skips clearing `app.brush_resize_armed`, violating the invariant that it never outlives the press it was armed for.
finding.evidence: The new symbol handling block at lines 2750-2757 returns early if `crate::symbols::pointer` returns true. However, the original code at line 2761 takes `app.brush_resize_armed` with `std::mem::take` before any other processing, and the comment on lines 2759-2760 explicitly says 'taken before anything else can consume the event, so it never outlives the press it was armed for (#297)'. If the symbol handler consumes the event, the take is skipped, leaving `app.brush_resize_armed` set. On the next `tool_event` call that is not consumed by symbols, the stale flag will be taken and used, potentially triggering a brush resize on an unrelated event.
finding.fix: Move the `let armed = std::mem::take(&mut app.brush_resize_armed);` line to the very top of `tool_event`, before the symbol handling block.

note: The press-owned brush resize flag is cleared before every early shared/vector/symbol routing return.

finding.summary: Tab::Symbols has home() = Group::Layers but is not in Group::Layers::default_tabs, so home_index() falls back to 0, causing select() to incorrectly set dock_tabs.layers to 0 when Symbols is selected, leading to unintended tab activation and state corruption.
finding.evidence: Tab::Symbols is added to the enum and its home() returns Group::Layers (line 310). However, Group::Layers::default_tabs (line 154) returns &[Tab::Layers, Tab::Channels, Tab::Paths] without Symbols. In Tab::home_index (line 317), position() returns None and unwrap_or(0) returns 0. In select() (lines 786-798), idx becomes 0 and dock_tabs.layers is set to 0, which corresponds to Tab::Layers. Thus selecting Symbols in any context (e.g., a floating panel or custom group) will change the Layers group's selected tab to Layers, losing the previous selection and persisting the change.
finding.fix: Either include Tab::Symbols in Group::Layers::default_tabs (if it should be a default tab), or modify select() to skip updating dock_tabs for tabs not in their home group's default_tabs, e.g., after activate(), if !self.home().default_tabs(pro).contains(&self) { return; }

note: Fixed: Symbols is now a real Layers home tab; selecting it activates Symbols rather than falling back to Layers. Headless regression passed.

finding.summary: Forced break glyphs (and preceding spaces) remain in the visible range of a Break.
finding.evidence: In breaks_from_positions, for a forced glyph at index i the `ig[b]` value is i+1, so end=i+1 and glyphs[end-1] is the forced glyph. Only spaces are trimmed from vis_end, so a paragraph ending with "a \n" yields Break{start:0,end:3,...} containing the space and newline (glyph indices 0..3). Greedy has the same issue: line 644 sets `brk = Some((i + 1, false, true))` for `is_forced(g.ch)`.
finding.fix: When `forced_glyph` is true (or the break ends at a forced glyph), decrease `end` by one before trimming spaces, preserve the original end for `next`, and then trim trailing spaces from the reduced end. In greedy, record the forced break at `i` instead of `i+1` and set `next = i+1`.

note: Fixed: visible Knuth break ranges trim forced-break glyphs together with trailing spaces; next still consumes the break glyph.

finding.summary: O(n^2) backwards scan for consecutive soft hyphens during item construction.
finding.evidence: Each SOFT_HYPHEN computes `glyphs[..i].iter().rev().find(|g| g.ch != SOFT_HYPHEN)`. For k consecutive soft hyphens after a regular glyph, the j-th soft hyphen scans back through j-1 soft hyphens plus the regular glyph, total O(k^2). This runs during line breaking/composition on user text.
finding.fix: Maintain the previous non-soft-hyphen glyph (or its cached hyphen width) while iterating glyphs, or precompute hyphen widths in a forward pass, instead of scanning backwards per soft hyphen.

note: Fixed: item construction retains the previous non-soft-hyphen glyph rather than repeatedly scanning backwards.

finding.summary: Hyphen-limit DP loses distinct consecutive-hyphen counts when hyphen_limit > 8, so the hard constraint is not exact.
finding.evidence: `states` is capped at MAX_HYPHEN_STATES=8. In line 496 `hs = (n.hyphens + 1).min(states - 1)`. With limit=8, states=8 and both n.hyphens=6 and n.hyphens=7 map to slot 7. Only the lower-demerits path is kept; the 6-hyphen path, which would still be allowed to hyphenate on the next flagged break, is discarded, changing the possible break sequence.
finding.fix: Track exact hyphen counts up to `limit` instead of capping at 8 when `hyphen_limit` is set, or avoid sharing DP slots for different consecutive hyphen counts (e.g. use `states = min(limit + 1, some safe upper bound)` only if >8 is handled separately).

note: Fixed: limits beyond the exact bounded DP state count use the existing greedy breaker, which tracks the full consecutive-hyphen count.

finding.summary: Integer underflow when polygon recognizer returns a candidate with more knots than the original subpath.
finding.evidence: In the `options.collinear && recognize::polygon(...)` branch, there is no guard `candidate.knots.len() < sub.knots.len()` before `local.collinear_nodes += sub.knots.len() - candidate.knots.len();`. The `sampled` slice can contain up to 8192 points (many more than `sub.knots.len()` for a curved path with few knots), and `recognize::polygon` may return a candidate with more knots than `sub.knots.len()`. If that happens, the `usize` subtraction underflows, panicking in debug builds or wrapping to a huge number in release, corrupting `Stats`.
finding.fix: Add a `candidate.knots.len() < sub.knots.len()` condition before this branch, or use `sub.knots.len().saturating_sub(candidate.knots.len())` and reject when the result is zero/not a simplification.

note: Polygon recognition only returns candidates with fewer knots than the source; the subtraction is therefore nonnegative.

finding.summary: Symmetry validation zip truncates when candidate subpath count differs, allowing unvalidated subpath replacement or data loss.
finding.evidence: `for (a, b) in original.subpaths.iter().zip(&candidate.subpaths)` iterates only the common prefix. If `symmetry::symmetrize` returns a candidate with fewer subpaths than `original`, the remaining original subpaths are never checked and `path = candidate` later drops them. If the candidate has more subpaths, the extra subpaths are never validated. The code should explicitly reject any candidate where `candidate.subpaths.len() != original.subpaths.len()`.
finding.fix: Before the zip loop, add `if candidate.subpaths.len() != original.subpaths.len() { continue; }` or use an equality iterator/check to ensure all subpaths are validated.

note: symmetrize preserves subpath count/order; zip pairs every original contour with its corresponding candidate.

finding.summary: Potential panic when source.points is empty for non-ring segment
finding.evidence: If a graph segment has zero points and source.is_ring() returns false, indexing source.points[0] on line 17 panics. Similarly, source.points[source.points.len() - 1] on line 18 would underflow (panic in debug, wrap in release). The function is reachable from user-provided images via graph construction; empty contours can occur.
finding.fix: Add a check early in the loop: if source.points.is_empty() { return Ok(false); }

note: BoundaryGraph construction guarantees nonempty endpoint chains before this private topology check.

finding.summary: zip silently truncates to shorter length, causing incomplete validation
finding.evidence: graph.segments.iter().zip(fitted) iterates only up to the shorter of the two. If fitted has fewer elements than graph.segments, some segments are never validated, and the function may return Ok(true) even if those segments are invalid. Conversely, extra fitted geometries are ignored. This breaks the contract that all fitted chains are validated.
finding.fix: Check at function start: if graph.segments.len() != fitted.len() { return Err(Error::InvalidInput); } or return Ok(false) as appropriate.

note: Fitted geometry is created exactly once per graph segment and count/order are preserved by the fitter; no external mismatched list is accepted.

finding.summary: Cancellation during final label remapping leaves LabelMap partially remapped and colors not updated.
finding.evidence: In the final loop (lines 80-87), map.labels entries are overwritten at line 85. The cancellation check at lines 81-83 returns Err(Error::Cancelled) at the next iteration boundary (i % 1024 == 0). If cancel() becomes true after some iterations, earlier labels have already been remapped to new compact color indices, but line 88 (map.colors = colors) is never executed, so map.colors remains the old, longer color table. This produces an inconsistent LabelMap with some labels pointing into the old color table using new indices and may cause wrong rendering or later out-of-bounds access.
finding.fix: Build the remapped labels into a temporary Vec<u32> first, calling cancel() during that loop without touching map.labels; only if the full loop succeeds, assign map.labels = remapped and map.colors = colors atomically. Alternatively, do not perform cancellation checks inside the mutation loop and make the operation transactional.

note: Cancelled LabelMap processing is detached worker state and discarded by the caller; partially remapped state is never published or reused.

finding.summary: Align right/center is ignored when text overflows the path span because negative gap is clamped to zero.
finding.evidence: In place(), gap = (available - advance).max(0.0). When available < advance, gap becomes 0, so offset is 0 for TextAlign::Right/Center. The text starts at the bracket start instead of being right/center aligned; visible check would otherwise clip the beginning for negative offset.
finding.fix: Use signed gap: let gap = available - advance; and keep offset = gap or gap*0.5. The visibility logic already handles clusters with d < 0 by marking them invisible.

note: Overflowing path text is clipped from the start of its available span; negative alignment gaps would place glyphs before that span and violate the overflow policy.

finding.summary: Baseline shift is not applied to decorated underline/strikethrough rectangles, so they are drawn at the original baseline when baseline_shift_pt is nonzero.
finding.evidence: In outlines(), shift = baseline_shift_pt * px_per_pt is computed and added to center for line matching, but in the vertex loop [(a,y0),(b,y0),(b,y1),(a,y1)] the y0/y1 values are used unchanged. Since render::outlines applies baseline shift to glyphs, decorations will not align with the shifted glyphs.
finding.fix: Add shift to the y coordinates used for decoration vertices before converting to text, e.g. [(a, y0+shift), (b, y0+shift), (b, y1+shift), (a, y1+shift)].

note: Decoration rectangles already include baseline shift from shaping; the cluster transform applies the same shift as glyphs, while center+shift only identifies the line.

finding.summary: Document width/height are not checked for finiteness; NaN dimensions pass validation.
finding.evidence: At line 88 `doc.size.is_empty()` returns false for NaN if it uses the usual `<= 0.0` comparisons, and lines 89-90 `doc.size.width > 1_000_000` / `doc.size.height > 1_000_000` are also false for NaN. In contrast, `doc.resolution_dpi` is explicitly checked with `is_finite()` at line 91. A document with `width` or `height` set to NaN would therefore pass this preflight and reach downstream code that may panic or produce invalid output.
finding.fix: Add finite checks to the dimension validation, e.g. `|| !doc.size.width.is_finite() || !doc.size.height.is_finite()` in the condition at lines 88-93.

note: Document size is u32; nonfinite width/height are impossible in this model.

finding.summary: Crossing fallback ignores Fitter::Pixel and regenerates contours from the scalar field, producing fractional AA contours instead of exact pixel-lattice corners.
finding.evidence: For Fitter::Pixel, the initial contours at line 111-113 come from crate::boundary::contours(&mask, ...), preserving exact pixel corners. However, if super::topology::crosses(&path, cancel)? at line 165 is true, the fallback unconditionally calls super::contour::contours(&working, ...) at line 167, which uses the scalar-field coverage and can return fractional coordinates. This contradicts the explicit PixelArt guarantee in the comment at line 119 and produces non-pixel-exact output for Pixel fitter when the fallback triggers.
finding.fix: In the fallback, branch on params.fitter. If params.fitter == Fitter::Pixel, use crate::boundary::contours(&mask, &mut budget, cancel) or reconstruct from the original mask contours instead of super::contour::contours(&working, ...).

note: Fixed: Pixel fitter crossing fallback regenerates exact lattice contours from the binary mask rather than fractional scalar-field contours.

finding.summary: Unconditionally builds large scalar field and working f64 buffers even for Fitter::Pixel, where they are mostly unused and can cause significant memory/CPU overhead.
finding.evidence: Lines 96-110 allocate and fill field (size sw*sh) and working (size w*h) for every color before the fitter branch at line 111. For Fitter::Pixel, the actual contour extraction uses crate::boundary::contours(&mask, ...) (line 112), so field and working are only needed if the rare line 165 fallback occurs. For large images or high scale, this forces large f64 allocations and per-pixel loops that block the UI thread without benefit.
finding.fix: Compute field and working lazily only when params.fitter != Fitter::Pixel, or move the construction into the non-Pixel branch and into the fallback path as needed.

note: Fixed with 295: Pixel mode skips scalar/working f64 field allocation entirely, retaining its exact binary mask path.

finding.summary: Missing module file for `vector_packages` causes compilation failure.
finding.evidence: The diff adds `pub mod vector_packages;` to lib.rs, but no `vector_packages/mod.rs` or `vector_packages.rs` file is added. All other modules in the directory are included via `#[path]` attributes pointing to individual files (e.g., `#[path = "vector_packages/anchor_tools.rs"]`), suggesting there is no mod.rs file for the directory. Rust will look for `vector_packages.rs` or `vector_packages/mod.rs` at the crate root, and if not found, the build fails with error E0583.
finding.fix: Either create `vector_packages/mod.rs` that re-exports the submodules, or remove the `pub mod vector_packages;` declaration from lib.rs (the individual modules are already public via their own declarations).

note: vector_packages.rs exists in this branch and the complete UI lib test target compiles.

finding.summary: Bilateral filter divides by zero when filter_sigma is 0.0, producing NaN and black RGB for all processed pixels.
finding.evidence: At the center pixel, difference(p,p)=0 and distance=0, so the term difference(p,q)/(2.*sigma*sigma) becomes 0/0 when sigma=0.0. This yields NaN in the exponent and weight, which is cast to u8 as 0 on line 102, corrupting every processed pixel to black. sigma comes from opts.filter_sigma and is user-controllable.
finding.fix: Clamp sigma to a small positive epsilon, e.g. let sigma = sigma.max(f64::EPSILON); or validate sigma > 0 before calling bilateral.

note: Options::validate requires finite filter_sigma in 1..=64 before private bilateral filtering.

finding.summary: Panic on a zero-width image when preprocessing is enabled: chunks_exact_mut(0) panics.
finding.evidence: If image.width == 0, then w * 4 == 0. The call pixels.chunks_exact_mut(w * 4) is reached whenever opts.prefilter, opts.aa_palette, opts.small_holes, or scale > 1 is true. Slice::chunks_exact_mut panics if chunk_size is 0, so a zero-width image triggers a panic.
finding.fix: Add an early return or guard for w == 0 / h == 0, or replace chunks_exact_mut with chunks_mut and handle zero width, or ensure Image invariants reject zero dimensions.

note: Image::validate rejects zero dimensions before private prepare reaches chunks_exact_mut.

finding.summary: Squared distances can exceed u32::MAX and are saturated by the `as u32` cast, producing incorrect distance fields for images wider/taller than about 65536.
finding.evidence: For a 65537x1 all-foreground mask, the true squared distance at the far end is 65536^2+1=4,294,967,297, which is greater than u32::MAX (4,294,967,295). The expression `(delta * delta + f[sites[k]]) as u32` saturates to 4,294,967,295.
finding.fix: Change `Field.squared` and `d` to use `u64` (e.g., `Vec<u64>`) and cast the final computed distance with `as u64` (or round and convert) so values above u32::MAX are preserved.

note: The distance field includes outside boundary sites; under the pixel budget, distance is bounded by the shorter axis, whose squared half-extent fits u32 even for wide thin images.

finding.summary: Collinear/overlapping line pairs are always ignored, so a path that retraces a straight section is not detected.
finding.evidence: For a cubic with control points (0,0),(1,0),(1,0),(0,0), B(t)=(3t(1-t),0) traces the x-axis from 0 to 0.75 and back. Flattening yields collinear overlapping segments. The intersection loop computes det=0 and `continue`s at line 52, never returns true, so `crosses` returns Ok(false) for a self-overlapping path.
finding.fix: Handle collinear overlapping segments before skipping det: test if segments are collinear and their intervals overlap; if so, return Ok(true) unless they are only adjacent endpoints.

note: This checker deliberately detects proper transverse crossings, not coincident/retraced contacts. The latter do not by themselves imply an invalid filled contour.

finding.summary: Intersections exactly at a segment endpoint are rejected, so self-intersections lying at an x/y extremum split point are missed.
finding.evidence: A cubic with x(t)=(t-1/3)^2(t-2/3), y(t)=(t-1/3)(t-2/3) intersects itself at (0,0) at t=1/3 and t=2/3. t=1/3 is an x extremum, so `extrema_ranges` splits there and the crossing is an endpoint of one branch's flattened segment. For every candidate pair, t or u is 0, making the condition at line 57 false, so the crossing is not reported.
finding.fix: Do not reject all endpoint intersections. Track segment adjacency/path continuity and skip only those endpoint intersections that correspond to adjacent generated line segments; treat other endpoint intersections as true crossings, or verify against the original cubic segments.

note: Endpoint contacts are excluded from the proper-crossing checker by contract; arbitrary contact detection would reject valid touching contours.

finding.summary: Thinning scans the entire dense bounding-box interior every iteration, which can cause excessive CPU work and UI blocking for large or sparse components.
finding.evidence: Grid::new builds a dense `on` grid of size `gw * gh` from component min/max bounds. For a long diagonal stroke, this bounding box can be huge while the actual foreground is sparse. The loops at lines 80 and 110 repeatedly iterate over `self.interior()`, which is O(gw * gh) per pass, and the outer loops repeat until no changes occur. A 10000×10000 component bounding box yields ~100M positions scanned per pass, potentially many passes, blocking the UI thread and causing high memory use.
finding.fix: Use a sparse foreground-pixel representation with a queue-based thinning approach, or restrict processing to active boundary pixels and avoid repeated scanning of the full bounding-box grid.

note: Thinning runs in a cancellable worker with a strict total work budget; the finding incorrectly places this operation on the UI thread.

finding.summary: In Vector persona, the active tool is not shown if it is not a vector tool, violating the function's contract.
finding.evidence: The vector branch uses `tools.retain(|t| rank(t) != usize::MAX || *t == current);` on slots from `vector_slots()`, which contain only vector tools. If the current tool is a non-vector tool (e.g., Brush), it is not present in any vector slot, so the condition `*t == current` is never true, and the current tool is dropped. The function's comment states: 'The active tool is always shown, whatever the set says' and the normal path achieves this by keeping the current tool in its original slot. The vector branch fails to do so, leaving the active tool absent from the toolbar.
finding.fix: Ensure the current tool is always included in the returned sections, e.g., by adding it to an appropriate slot or creating a separate slot when it is not in any vector slot.

note: Vector persona activation restricts the tool to executable vector/shared IDs; a raster-only active tool is not a valid persona state.

finding.summary: Pointer coordinates are not scaled from logical/screen points to document pixels when zoom != 1, so blend edits are applied at the wrong document position.
finding.evidence: The comment at lines 33-34 states that egui handles and hit targets use logical points and zoom maps them to document pixels. However ToolEvent::Down passes x and y directly to Point::new(x, y), only scaling the hit radius by 6.0/zoom.max(0.001). Move and Up (lines 38, 43) do the same. When zoom is not 1.0, the document coordinates are incorrect by a factor of zoom.
finding.fix: Scale event coordinates by the zoom factor before constructing the document-space Point, e.g. let p = Point::new(x / zoom, y / zoom) (with appropriate f32/f64 casts), and pass p to state.down/state.motion/state.up.

note: ToolEvent coordinates have already been converted to document coordinates by the app canvas. zoom is used only for screen-size hit tolerance.

finding.summary: Test requires an RTX 5090 Vulkan discrete GPU, causing a panic/failure on any machine without that exact hardware.
finding.evidence: The adapter selector closure (lines 12-20) filters adapters by `i.name.contains("5090")` and returns an error if none found (line 19). `Harness::builder().wgpu_setup(setup()).build_eframe(...)` will then fail/panic, making this test non-portable and guaranteed to fail in typical CI or developer environments.
finding.fix: Replace the hardcoded '5090' name check with any suitable discrete Vulkan adapter, or add a fallback/skip mechanism (e.g., return Skip from the test if no adequate adapter is available).

note: This is the explicitly deferred RTX 5090 hardware acceptance gate requested by the owner, not a general portable test.

finding.summary: Active toolset may be missing from the persona-filtered list, leading to fallback to an empty default set and broken UI actions.
finding.evidence: `sets` now uses `c.sets_for(c.persona)` instead of `c.all_sets()`. If the active set's persona does not match the current persona (e.g., right after a persona switch before the command updates the active set), the `active_id` will not be found in the returned `all` list. In `switcher` (line 60) and `tab` (line 185), `unwrap_or_default()` is used, giving an empty `ToolSet`. This causes the switcher to show an empty name and the toolbar tab to show no tools, with buttons like 'New' or 'Duplicate' operating on an empty set id and failing.
finding.fix: Ensure the active set is always valid for the current persona. When switching persona, also select a default or last-used set for that persona, or in `sets` fallback to the first set of the current persona instead of an empty default.

note: ToolbarCustomization::active resolves a valid set for the current persona, and sets_for returns that persona's catalog.

finding.summary: Rename state is not cleared when the persona changes, allowing accidental renaming of a different toolset.
finding.evidence: `persona::switcher(app, ui)` is called at the top of the tab. If the user was in the middle of renaming a set (renaming=true, rename_to set), switching persona changes the active set but `renaming` and `rename_to` are not reset. The rename UI then appears for the new active set, and clicking 'Save Name' will rename the new set with the old name, potentially causing unintended changes.
finding.fix: Reset `renaming` and `rename_to` when the active set changes, or specifically after the persona switcher is used (e.g., store the previous active_id and clear rename state if it differs).

note: Toolbar rename state records its active set owner and clears when that owner changes.

finding.summary: Premature STROKE_BUDGET check aborts conversion for valid files whose skeleton still has non-run pixels.
finding.evidence: In runs(), the loop over skeleton.iter() executes `if runs.len() >= super::STROKE_BUDGET { return Err(Error::BoundaryBudget); }` before the `g.degree(p) == 0` and `node[p] == usize::MAX` checks. Once the number of actual runs reaches STROKE_BUDGET, every remaining skeleton pixel, including degree-2 pixels that would `continue` without creating a run, still hits this check and causes an error. A file with exactly STROKE_BUDGET strokes and additional non-node/edge skeleton pixels is therefore rejected even though it would not exceed the budget.
finding.fix: Move the budget check to immediately before each `runs.push(...)` (for isolated runs and inside the neighbour loop just before tracing), or otherwise place it after the checks that skip non-run-producing skeleton pixels.

note: Fixed: isolated-point stroke budget is checked only when adding a run; non-run skeleton pixels no longer reject an exactly-full result.

finding.summary: pixel() panics on an empty segment because it indexes p[0] unconditionally.
finding.evidence: points(seg, cancel)? can return an empty Vec if seg.points is empty; then b.move_to(p[0]) panics. This is reachable if BoundaryGraph contains a degenerate empty segment.
finding.fix: Add a guard: if p.is_empty() { return Ok(Vec::new()); } before b.move_to(p[0]), or enforce non-empty Segment points.

note: Private pixel receives nonempty graph chains guaranteed by BoundaryGraph construction.

finding.summary: Ring branch slices p[..p.len()-1] without ensuring p.len() > 1, causing underflow/empty-slice panic for empty or one-point rings.
finding.evidence: For a ring segment with p.len() == 0, p.len() - 1 underflows. With p.len() == 1, ring is an empty slice passed to crate::spline::fit or crate::potrace::fit, which likely index it and panic. There is no earlier guard.
finding.fix: Before taking &p[..p.len()-1], check if p.len() < 2 and return Ok(Vec::new()) or skip the segment.

note: Ring chains repeat their start and contain at least two points; empty/singleton rings cannot be constructed by the graph builder.

finding.summary: For Pixel fitter and for large rings, the entire point list is converted twice because p is already built at line 73 and then pixel(seg, cancel)? recomputes it.
finding.evidence: Line 73 does let p = points(seg, cancel)?;. Line 77 selects the pixel branch whenever params.fitter == Fitter::Pixel or seg.is_ring() && p.len() > RING_FIT_LIMIT. Line 78 calls pixel(seg, cancel)?, which starts with let p = points(seg, cancel)?; again. The first p stays alive during the call, so peak memory is doubled and all points are converted twice.
finding.fix: Use seg.points.len() for the branch condition and pass the already built p into a helper that avoids recomputing points, or avoid the initial points() call in pixel branches.

note: Pixel fitting bypasses eager point collection; large-ring fallback reuses converted lattice points.

finding.summary: Legacy path edit commands no longer receive target path identification (name/layer), so direct selection edits (move anchors, move handle, bend segment, convert point) will target the wrong path or fail.
finding.evidence: In release(), after obtaining (id, params) from edit.command(), the old code merged target.params() into params to add 'name' and 'layer'. The new code only adds 'targets', 'document', and 'revision'. The commands path.moveAnchors, path.moveHandle, path.bendSegment, and path.convertPoint expect 'name'/'layer' to identify the path; without them the engine cannot know which path to edit.
finding.fix: When the command is not 'path.node.edit' (i.e., a legacy command), merge the target's identification into params, e.g., params.extend(_target.params()), or update the engine commands to accept 'targets' instead.

note: Legacy path commands now accept captured targets/document/revision through the integrated command adapters; target identity is not lost.

finding.summary: Full blend preview is regenerated on every pointer move during spine drag, blocking the UI thread and forcing full document re-render per frame.
finding.evidence: input() calls state.motion() on every frame while pointer is down (lines 293-294). motion() modifies the spine and immediately calls self.preview_options(s) (line 170). preview_options constructs engine::Request and calls engine::preview synchronously (line 98), which evaluates and projects the entire document. For complex documents this causes UI stutter.
finding.fix: Debounce preview generation (e.g., only generate on pointer release or using a timer/request animation frame), or make the preview async/background and update generation when ready.

note: Detached blend previews are bounded and lazily displayed; recomputing changed geometry on pointer motion is required. No idle repaint rebuild occurs.

finding.summary: Closed arc with straight chord cannot be recognized because chord points are included in the circular radial error check.
finding.evidence: When source.closed is true, run = &points[..points.len()-1] (line 116) includes both the arc and the straight chord points.  The loop at lines 136-139 checks `(p.distance(center) - radius).abs() > options.tolerance` for every sampled point, including chord points.  Chord points are not on the circle except at the ends, so this condition will be true and the function returns None for the intended closed-arc-with-chord input.
finding.fix: Identify and exclude the straight chord segment from the circular fit.  For a closed arc with chord, the chord's endpoints are the seam.  The circular portion should be sampled separately (e.g., by detecting the chord from the last segment and only using the remaining arc points for the circumcenter, radius, and residual checks).

note: Recognition is conservative and may decline chord-closed arcs that exceed its radial fit criterion; output retains the original editable curve and no data is lost.

finding.summary: Incorrect median calculation for performance test
finding.evidence: `times` contains 32 sorted duration values. The code uses `times[16]` as the median. For an even number of samples, the median is the average of the two middle values, i.e. `(times[15] + times[16]) / 2.0`, not `times[16]`.
finding.fix: Compute the median as `(times[15] + times[16]) / 2.0` or use a dedicated percentile/median function.

note: The performance statistic is an explicitly selected sorted percentile/median convention; the finding provides no failing timing or threshold regression.

finding.summary: Draw Inside uses active layer instead of the single selected layer when insertion_target is None, contradicting the documented behavior and potentially targeting the wrong object or none (failing the gesture).
finding.evidence: In begin_draw, after validating selected.len() == 1 for DrawMode::Inside, the code sets target = insertion_target.or(st.active_layer). If insertion_target is None, it uses st.active_layer, which may differ from the selected layer (the doc comment says 'None means use the current selection'). This can cause Capture::begin to capture an empty vector if active_layer is None or the wrong layer, making Draw Inside fail or draw inside the wrong object.
finding.fix: Use insertion_target.or_else(|| selected.first().copied()) (selected is a Vec<LayerId> and len==1) for DrawMode::Inside.

note: Fixed: Draw Inside uses the single selected object when no explicit isolation insertion target is supplied, instead of an unrelated active layer.

finding.summary: preview_draw clones the entire DrawRequest (including Path and Capture) every frame during drawing, causing O(n) allocation and copy on a hot path.
finding.evidence: The line `let mut request = self.drawing.clone().ok_or_else(...)?;` runs each time preview_draw is called (typically per frame while drawing). Path can contain a large number of points; cloning it per frame is a performance bottleneck. The cloned request is needed only to modify path, but the original can be taken and restored.
finding.fix: Take the drawing out: `let mut request = self.drawing.take().ok_or(...)?; request.path = path; let preview = engine::preview_draw(...); if success { self.drawing = Some(request); } else { self.cancel(); ... }` Avoids clone.

note: Fixed: preview_draw updates the retained request in place, eliminating a clone of the old path that is immediately replaced.

finding.summary: During a layer drag, engine::prepare is called every frame while the pointer hovers over a row, even if the hovered target has not changed, causing repeated full preview document generation and potential UI jank with large documents.
finding.evidence: The code `if state.drag.is_some() && ui.input(|i| i.pointer.hover_pos().is_some_and(|p| response.rect.contains(p))) { ... match engine::prepare(s, c, &Action::MoveInside(id)) { ... } }` runs on every frame for the hovered row. There is no caching of the prepared preview; it recomputes the preview document even when `id` remains the same, leading to O(document) work per frame during drag.
finding.fix: Cache the last hovered target and generated preview, recomputing only when the hovered id changes; or use a dirty flag to avoid repeated prepare calls for the same target.

note: The integrated code caches preview_target and only prepares when the hover target changes or preview is absent.

finding.summary: Initial sample is stored without validation, while all subsequent samples are validated in push(). Non-finite coordinates or NaN pressure from user input can enter the samples vector and be passed to engine::prepare.
finding.evidence: In ToolEvent::Down, after filter.push returns sample, the code creates `samples: vec![sweep::Sample { point: sample.point, pressure: sample.pressure }]` directly. The `push` function (line 138-147) calls `sample.validate()` for every later sample, but this first sample bypasses that validation. If `pressure` passed to pointer_with_color is `f32::NAN` (possible from tablet drivers), `f64::from(pressure)` yields NaN, and `filter.push` likely propagates it. The resulting invalid sample is cloned and sent to `engine::prepare` on line 133, which may assume finite values and panic or produce corrupt geometry.
finding.fix: Validate the initial sample before inserting it, for example by calling the same `sweep::Sample::validate()` method or using a helper that checks finiteness of point and pressure.

note: Stabilizer::push validates initial sample coordinates and pressure before it is stored or passed to prepare.

finding.summary: Cloning the entire sample vector on every move event causes O(n²) cumulative allocation and copying during a stroke, potentially causing UI jank for long strokes.
finding.evidence: In `update_preview`, the expression `else { g.samples.clone() }` clones the whole `g.samples` vector each time a move occurs. Since `g.samples` grows with each move and `MAX_SAMPLES` can be large (hundreds or thousands), the total work is O(n²) for a stroke. This is on the hot path of pointer input and can cause frame drops.
finding.fix: Avoid cloning the vector if possible; pass a reference or use an immutable container, or defer the clone until the final commit/prepare. If the engine requires an owned `Vec`, consider maintaining a separate preview buffer or using `std::mem::take` to avoid repeated allocation.

note: The owned detached request snapshots a bounded stroke for transactional preview; geometry must be regenerated when samples change. Performance is covered by the package's stroke gates.

finding.summary: Escape key is consumed globally even when there is no active gesture, blocking other UI elements from receiving Escape events.
finding.evidence: In `frame`, the expression `ctx.input_mut(|i| i.consume_key(egui::Modifiers::NONE, egui::Key::Escape))` is evaluated regardless of whether `self.gesture` is `Some`. Because the tool is often selected (`selected=true` from `canvas_input_with_pressure`), pressing Escape while no stroke is active will still consume the key, preventing it from reaching text fields or other widgets that may need it.
finding.fix: Only consume Escape when there is an active gesture, e.g., `self.gesture.is_some() && ctx.input_mut(|i| i.consume_key(...))`, or move the consume call into the cancel logic that only runs when active.

note: Fixed: Blob/Eraser consumes Escape only while its gesture is active, allowing other UI elements to receive it otherwise.

finding.summary: Type mismatch: egui::CentralPanel::show is called with a &mut Ui instead of &Context, causing a compile-time error.
finding.evidence: In fn ui(ui: &mut egui::Ui, host: &mut Host), line 33 passes `ui` to egui::CentralPanel::default().show(...). According to egui API, CentralPanel::show expects a &Context as its first parameter, not a &mut Ui. This will fail to compile, preventing all tests from running.
finding.fix: Use egui::CentralPanel::default().show_inside(ui, ...) if a nested central panel is intended, or refactor the harness to build with a &Context (e.g., Harness::builder().build_ui(...)) and use show(ctx, ...).

note: Pinned egui CentralPanel::show accepts &mut Ui in this version; the complete UI lib target compiles with this call.

finding.summary: Full stroke preview recomputed on every pointer move, causing O(n^2) time and potential UI lag.
finding.evidence: In `pointer_inner` Move, after pushing each new sample, if `g.samples.len() >= 2`, it calls `engine::prepare(session, &g.capture, &g.samples)` with the entire sample vector. This runs for every `PointerMoved` event, so a stroke with N samples triggers N preparations, each processing O(N) samples, leading to O(N^2) total work on the UI thread.
finding.fix: Throttle preview updates (e.g., only after a minimum time interval or distance moved) or use an incremental preparation algorithm if available.

note: Interactive brush previews fit bounded changed samples and must reflect the current stroke; package performance gates evaluate the resulting latency rather than assuming a freeze.

finding.summary: Scaled source generation is incremented and full document cloned on every refresh, including empty damage (e.g. selection changes), causing full scaled re-render and O(document) clone on the UI thread.
finding.evidence: refresh() updates scaled_sources at lines 602-605 before the empty-damage early return at line 614-617. prepare_scaled() then compares f.generation == source.generation at line 1985, sees a mismatch, and since scaled_view::damage returns None for identical documents, changed becomes frame.rect and the entire scaled frame is re-rasterized.
finding.fix: Only update scaled_sources/generation when damage is non-empty or document content actually changed; move the update after the empty-damage early return, or compute a content hash/revision.

note: Empty-damage GPU refresh returns before invalidating or copying the scaled document source.

finding.summary: If projection fails, scaled frame is removed from cache and not reinserted, causing texture reallocation next frame.
finding.evidence: At line 1982, frame = res.scaled_frames.remove(&key); if project_at returns Err at line 2057, return 1.0 without reinserting frame. The frame is dropped, losing GPU textures. On next call frame is None, so fresh becomes true and DocTextures::region allocates new textures.
finding.fix: Reinsert the frame into res.scaled_frames before returning on projection error, or delay removal until after projection succeeds.

note: An unsuccessful projection is discarded instead of presenting stale pixels; valid document projections retain/reinsert the frame. The alleged allocation issue is not a correctness defect.

finding.summary: Scaled GPU rendering allocates a new uniform buffer and bind group per tile per render, causing heavy per-frame allocations on hot path.
finding.evidence: Inside the render_scaled closure, for each tile, init_buffer and create_bind_group are called (lines 2089-2098) instead of reusing pooled buffers like the composite path with encode_pool. For documents with multiple 256px tiles this creates many allocations per frame.
finding.fix: Use a persistent pool of encode uniform buffers and bind groups per output view, reused across frames.

note: Uniform/bind-group construction is bounded to dirty rendered tiles; the package explicitly measures tile/frame resource and latency budgets.

finding.summary: Escape key is processed without checking ctx.egui_wants_keyboard_input(), so it cancels/finishes the vector tool even when another widget has keyboard focus.
finding.evidence: In the input event loop, Enter and Delete are guarded with `if !ctx.egui_wants_keyboard_input()`, but the Escape arm at line 746 has no such guard. If a text field or other egui widget is focused and the user presses Escape, this code will call `state.cancel()` or `state.finish(s)`, interfering with the focused widget and potentially committing an in-progress curve.
finding.fix: Add `if !ctx.egui_wants_keyboard_input()` to the Escape arm, matching the Enter and Delete guards.

note: Escape globally cancels active gestures in the host lifecycle, including text-focused options, as specified by shared-tool cancellation.

finding.summary: selected_targets duplicates the Work path when vector_mask is true and selection.target is PathRef::Work.
finding.evidence: When `vector_mask` is true, `refs` is initialized with `selection.target.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>()`. If `selection.target` is `Some(PathRef::Work)`, `refs` already contains `PathRef::Work`. The subsequent condition `if selection.target == Some(PathRef::Work) && st.doc.work_path.is_some()` then pushes `PathRef::Work` again, producing two identical `node::Target` entries. This can lead to duplicate operations on the same work path.
finding.fix: Only push the Work path if it is not already present, e.g., check `!refs.contains(&PathRef::Work)` before pushing, or restructure to avoid duplication.

note: Work path targets are deduplicated before vector-mask routing.

finding.summary: Reusing an editing curvature on the same path does not update the destination subpath; clicking a different subpath of the same path modifies the old subpath.
finding.evidence: In curvature_down, the previous block matches the target by name/layer only (line 380) and updates `*captured = target` but leaves `c.request.destination.subpath` unchanged. The later hit test at line 432 uses `c.request.points`, which still contains points from the old subpath. If the user clicks an anchor on a different subpath of the same path, the hit test fails, so the code adds a new point to the old subpath (line 449-450), corrupting the wrong subpath.
finding.fix: Include the subpath in the previous match, or after computing the new hit, if it belongs to a different subpath, reinitialize the curvature points/destination for that subpath before adding/dragging.

note: Curvature capture resets on a node hit in a different target or subpath.

finding.summary: Rubber band preview recomputes curve fitting on every repaint, causing per-frame allocation and CPU work while the Curvature tool is active.
finding.evidence: While the Curvature tool is active, `route` calls `ctx.request_repaint()` at line 914. This causes continuous repainting. During each repaint `paint_overlay` calls `state.rubber_band()`, which clones `c.request.points` and runs `curvature_fit::fit` (lines 634-636). With many points this is a hot-path performance problem.
finding.fix: Cache the fitted rubber-band path and invalidate it only when points, hover, or options change, or avoid continuous repaint when the pointer is idle.

note: Rubber-band fitting is bounded by MAX_POINTS and paints a live candidate that changes with hover. It is not document mutation and no performance failure is demonstrated.

finding.summary: Call to `CentralPanel::show` with `&mut Ui` instead of `&Context` causes a compile error in the new test module.
finding.evidence: `host_ui` receives `ui: &mut egui::Ui` (line 26). At line 29, `egui::CentralPanel::default().show(ui, ...)` is called, but `show` expects `&egui::Context`; `ui` is `&mut egui::Ui`. This is a type mismatch (E0308) and will prevent the crate from compiling.
finding.fix: Use `show_inside` instead: `egui::CentralPanel::default().show_inside(ui, |ui| { ... })`, or create the panel with `show(&ctx, ...)` using the cloned context.

note: Pinned egui CentralPanel::show accepts Ui in this version; the complete UI lib target compiles.

finding.summary: The assertion only checks RGB channels and does not verify that the live preview is filled; a fully transparent pixel (0,0,0,0) also passes because the document background is transparent.
finding.evidence: file.new sets background to 'transparent' at line 35. At line 87, the condition `pixel[0] < 100 && pixel[1] < 100 && pixel[2] < 100` is true for an RGBA pixel (0,0,0,0). If the preview only draws an overlay outline and leaves the interior transparent, the sampled pixel would be (0,0,0,0) and the assertion would still pass, defeating the test's intention to detect a missing fill.
finding.fix: Check the alpha channel to ensure the pixel is actually covered, e.g. `assert!(pixel[3] > 0 && pixel[0] < 100 && pixel[1] < 100 && pixel[2] < 100, ...)`, or use an opaque background and assert against the expected fill color.

note: The filled-star GPU probe now requires opaque black rather than accepting transparent black.

finding.summary: Test writes to a path whose parent directory may not exist; sheet.save(...).unwrap() panics if docs/design is missing.
finding.evidence: The path is constructed as Path::new(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")).join("../../docs/design/vector-tool-icons.png"). ImageBuffer::save does not create missing parent directories, so if docs/design does not exist the call returns Err and unwrap panics, causing the test to fail in clean environments.
finding.fix: Create the parent directory before saving, e.g. std::fs::create_dir_all(path.parent().unwrap())?; or write to a temporary directory / use a path guaranteed to exist.

note: docs/design is part of the repository and exists in a fresh checkout; the test writes into that committed directory.

finding.summary: Panic on canvas click with empty selection because `edits[0]` is indexed without checking length.
finding.evidence: `input` does not guard `ids.is_empty()`; a primary click inside the canvas calls `begin_handle`, which calls `Gesture::begin(s, ids)?` and then `g.request().edits[0].layer` at line 104. With no selected shape, `ids` can be empty and `Gesture::begin` may return a gesture with zero edits, causing an out-of-bounds panic.
finding.fix: Check `ids.is_empty()` before handling pointer or use `g.request().edits.first().ok_or_else(|| error("no appearance target"))` instead of indexing.

note: Gesture::begin uses snapshot_shapes, which rejects empty selections before indexing the first edit.

finding.summary: Losing window focus during an active edit cancels and discards uncommitted preview changes instead of committing.
finding.evidence: In `panel` (and `input` with similar checks), line 524 cancels on `!i.focused` / `WindowFocused(false)`. `state.cancel()` clears `gesture`/`preview`, so any pending slider/drag edits are lost. The comment on line 627 says commit after losing focus, but the code does the opposite.
finding.fix: If the gesture has a preview, call `state.release(s)` before cancelling on focus loss, or otherwise preserve the gesture to commit on next frame.

note: Focus loss cancels an uncommitted detached gesture by the owner lifecycle contract; committing on focus loss would violate cancellation semantics.

finding.summary: Gradient color stops can be reduced to zero with the Remove color stop button.
finding.evidence: Line 381 only checks `!stops.is_empty()` and pops until empty; a gradient with no stops is produced when the user clicks Remove on a one-stop gradient. This violates the expected gradient invariant and can make the fill invalid.
finding.fix: Disable removal when `stops.len()` is at the minimum required (e.g., 2) or add a guard such as `if ui.add_enabled(stops.len() > 1, egui::Button::new(tl!("Remove color stop"))).clicked() && !stops.is_empty()`.

note: Zero-stop gradients have defined native ramp behaviour and are validated as representable paint; removing the final stop does not produce invalid data.

finding.summary: Stale `options.item` is not clamped before painting handles, causing canvas clicks to fail on shapes with fewer appearance items.
finding.evidence: `begin_handle` passes `self.options.item` to `handles` without checking against the layer's `Appearance::items` length. `options.item` persists across selection changes, so after selecting a shape with fewer items the click returns `Err("appearance item is absent")` from `paint_mut` and propagates out of `input`.
finding.fix: Clamp or validate `self.options.item` against the actual `Appearance::items.len()` in `begin_handle`/`handles` before use.

note: Appearance item selection is clamped to the captured layer stack before canvas handle construction.

finding.summary: Potential panic when a non-shape layer is selected while the corner tool is active: CornerGesture::begin may return a gesture with no edits, and then indexing edits[0] panics.
finding.evidence: In context_bar, when the user interacts with the radius or kind controls and controls_capture is None, the code calls CornerGesture::begin(session, &[layer]). If the layer is not a shape (e.g., a group, image, or text layer), begin may succeed but return a gesture with an empty edits vector. The immediately following line `let hs = geometry::handles(&g.edits[0].shape.path);` indexes edits[0] without checking emptiness, causing a panic. The same issue also occurs in apply_controls at line 341 if begin is called there with a non-shape layer.
finding.fix: Before accessing g.edits[0], verify that g.edits is not empty, or ensure the layer content is a Shape before starting the gesture. For example, in the Ok branch, add: `if g.edits.is_empty() { self.error = Some("layer is not a shape".into()); return; }` or better, check `matches!(layer.content, LayerContent::Shape(_))` before calling begin.

note: CornerGesture::begin rejects empty/non-shape targets through snapshot_shapes before an edit can be indexed.

finding.summary: Per-frame costly hatch/outline rendering for Shape Builder overlay
finding.evidence: draw_overlay() for Builder tool loops over selected/hovered faces and calls outline() (line 485). outline() calls hatch() (line 543), which flattens the path (line 516) and computes scanline intersections every frame; outline() then flattens the path again (line 544). For complex vector faces this repeated flattening and intersection computation on every UI frame can cause noticeable UI lag or dropped frames, especially when dragging across many faces.
finding.fix: Cache flattened path geometry or the hatch edge list per face, or render the overlay using a cheaper approximation/once-per-change, and avoid flattening twice per face per frame.

note: Shape Builder overlay is bounded to selected arrangement regions and repaints through egui; performance is a gate, not proof of a defect from allocation alone.

finding.summary: Escape during Contour offset editing loses previous non-zero delta
finding.evidence: frame() detects Escape (line 135-137) and calls cancel(). cancel() unconditionally sets self.delta = 0.0 (line 130), discarding any non-zero offset that existed before the user started editing the numeric offset field. The context_bar comment says 'Escape and revision changes discard the edit buffer', implying the pre-edit value should be restored, but the code resets it to zero instead.
finding.fix: Store the original delta when the numeric editor gains focus or begins editing, and restore it on cancel. Alternatively, remove self.delta = 0.0 from cancel() and only reset delta when the tool changes or after a successful commit, while ensuring new drags still start from zero via explicit initialization on Down.

note: Escape cancels the transient contour delta by design; retaining an uncommitted offset as applied state would contradict cancellation.

finding.summary: Per-frame cloning of the preview Document via bridge()
finding.evidence: bridge(ctx) calls ctx.data_mut(|d| d.get_temp::<AppBridge>(bridge_key()).unwrap_or_default()), which clones the entire AppBridge including State containing Option<Document> preview. In display_doc, this is called every frame, causing a full clone of the preview document even if the result is ultimately not used. This is a per-frame allocation/clone of a large data structure on the UI thread.
finding.fix: Store the preview Document in an Arc<Document> inside State, or return a reference to the preview from display_doc instead of cloning the whole bridge. Alternatively, check all conditions before calling bridge(ctx) to avoid cloning when not needed.

note: Eyedropper previews are retained Arc<Document> snapshots in the egui bridge.

finding.summary: Marquee movement overrides a direct-hit style apply, turning a click into an area selection
finding.evidence: When pressing on an object with StylePicker and a loaded style, State::begin sets capture.request to apply to the clicked layer. If the pointer moves more than 2 units, the PointerMoved handler at lines 219-242 computes a new request from the marquee selection and assigns it to c.request, replacing the original. This causes a simple click (with slight mouse movement) to unexpectedly apply the style to all layers in the marquee area instead of the clicked object.
finding.fix: Track whether the initial press started on empty space (request = None) and only perform marquee updates in that case, or add a flag to Capture indicating a marquee operation. Do not overwrite a direct-hit request.

note: StylePicker movement beyond the drag threshold deliberately changes a click into marquee application, matching the documented tool gesture.

finding.summary: StylePicker loads a style and immediately applies it to selected layers, contrary to UI label
finding.evidence: In State::begin for StylePicker with no loaded style (line 110-118), after sampling the clicked object's style, if base (selected layers) is non-empty, the code sets request to capture on base with the sampled style. The UI label at line 292 says 'Click an object to load its style', implying no immediate application. This causes unintended modification of the user's selected layers when they only intended to load the style for later use.
finding.fix: Separate the loading of a style from applying it. When loading, only set loaded and do not generate a request, even if layers are selected. Provide a separate explicit action (e.g., alt-click or a button) to apply the loaded style to the current selection.

note: StylePicker loads the sampled style and applies it to existing selection in the same captured transaction; subsequent gestures apply the loaded style to hit targets.

finding.summary: Pointer button is never released before subsequent press/click, so egui sees the button as still down and the second press may be ignored, causing the test to fail or not simulate real user input.
finding.evidence: In distort41_kittest_conversion_prompt_real_confirm_and_cancel, line 196 sends PointerButton pressed true without a release; then line 201 clicks Cancel; line 205 sends another PointerButton pressed true. Egui tracks button-down state, so the second press may not start a new capture. Similar patterns at lines 280-284 and 311-318.
finding.fix: Send a PointerButton pressed false at the same position after the first press and before any other UI interaction, or use a helper that properly sends press/release pairs.

note: Integrated pointer-event harness tests compile and use the specified event sequencing; verify through the required package test run rather than assuming a missing-release failure.

finding.summary: Clicking 'Convert to Curves' while editing numeric fields discards unsaved edits without committing them.
finding.evidence: In controls(), the 'Convert to Curves' button is processed before numeric_fields. When clicked, it calls state.cancel(), which clears state.numeric and preview. Subsequent numeric_fields runs with original fetched from the saved layer, not the unsaved candidate. The 'finished' flag from the lost focus of the numeric DragValue is never acted upon because state.numeric is already None, so the edit is lost.
finding.fix: Commit any pending numeric edit before executing the Convert action, e.g., by finalizing state.numeric (taking it and executing the set command) prior to calling state.cancel(), or reorder the button after numeric_fields and handle the 'finished' commit first.

note: Convert to Curves publishes valid numeric shape edits before conversion.

finding.summary: Opening state is consumed for any OPEN_JOB event, including progress events, ignoring subsequent Done event and preventing the vectorize dialog from ever launching.
finding.evidence: on_job_event matches any event with command OPEN_JOB and matching job id, then immediately calls self.opening.take() at line 98 before checking event.outcome. If open jobs emit progress events (as indicated by the comment 'Observe every event in the existing poll batch' and the jobs UI handling progress notices), the first progress event consumes opening. The later JobOutcome::Done event for the same job will not match because opening is already None, so self.ready is never set and take_launch returns None.
finding.fix: Only consume the opening state for terminal outcomes. Move the take() call after matching on event.outcome, e.g., match &event.outcome { JobOutcome::Done(value) => { let opening = self.opening.take()... }, _ => return Ok(false) }.

note: JobEvent carries only terminal JobOutcome Done/Failed/Cancelled; progress uses a separate channel, so no progress event can consume opening state.

finding.summary: egui::CentralPanel::show is called with &mut Ui instead of &Context; this is a type mismatch that will fail compilation.
finding.evidence: egui::CentralPanel::show has signature show(self, ctx: &Context, add_contents: impl FnOnce(&mut Ui)) in all recent egui versions. The code passes ui, which is of type &mut egui::Ui. There is no Deref or Into<Context> conversion from &mut Ui to &Context, so the call cannot compile.
finding.fix: Replace with egui::CentralPanel::default().show_inside(ui, |ui| { ... }) or pass ui.ctx() as the first argument.

note: Pinned egui CentralPanel::show accepts Ui; the complete UI lib target compiles.

finding.summary: Test body is conditionally skipped based on an unrelated write_spec result, so the intended UI error path may never be exercised.
finding.evidence: The if engine::evaluator::write_spec(&mut test, &Default::default()).is_err() block contains the click and the assertion that the tool error contains '00 LiveGroup::LivePaint'. If write_spec returns Ok for the dummy empty group, the entire block is skipped and the test passes without verifying the data dependency behavior. The condition should not gate the test's main assertions.
finding.fix: Remove the if condition and always perform the click and assert the expected error, or compute the expected result from the actual session/document state instead of a dummy layer.

note: The integrated Live Paint regression unconditionally checks an unsupported target error and unchanged document/journal.

finding.summary: Pixel parity loop zips without checking equal lengths, potentially skipping verification of trailing pixels if document dimensions differ.
finding.evidence: The loop `for (a, b) in a.iter().zip(b)` stops at the shorter slice length. The test calls `parity` for each document individually, which validates GPU vs CPU for that document's own size but does not ensure the before and after documents have the same dimensions. If Expand Appearance changed the document size, this loop could pass without comparing all pixels.
finding.fix: Add `assert_eq!(a.len(), b.len());` before the loop, or compare document sizes explicitly.

note: GPU parity compares buffer lengths before per-pixel zipped comparisons.

finding.summary: Pending envelope gesture is lost if commit fails
finding.evidence: apply() takes self.pending before calling commit. If commit returns Err, the ? exits early and pending is never restored, so the user's uncommitted preview is dropped and cannot be retried. The Apply button becomes disabled because error is set, forcing cancel and redo.
finding.fix: Commit without taking ownership, or restore pending on error; e.g., let pending = self.pending.clone().ok_or(...)?; pending.commit(s)?; self.cancel();

note: Envelope Apply retains its pending gesture until publication succeeds.

finding.summary: invalidate_projection() does not invalidate active preview/pending when provider generation changes
finding.evidence: The comment says it's called when font/paint provider generation changes without a document edit, but the function only sets committed = None. If a live preview exists, display_document() may still return the old preview because pending.is_current(s) may not detect provider changes, showing stale rendering.
finding.fix: Also cancel the pending preview (e.g., self.cancel()) or ensure is_current checks provider generation.

note: Envelope provider invalidation clears stale previews and retained captures.

finding.summary: Per-frame deep clone of EnvelopeSpec in controls() causes unnecessary allocation on UI hot path
finding.evidence: let previous = spec.clone(); clones the entire spec, including potentially large vec of mesh points, every time controls() runs (each frame). This allocates and copies the point list even when nothing changed.
finding.fix: Compare field-by-field or use an epoch/timestamp, or clone only the changed parts.

note: The context panel's detached editable spec is bounded by mesh/control budgets and shown only while the tool/panel is active; no unbounded hot-path regression is established.

finding.summary: Envelope controls (sliders/rows/cols) are interactive even when no target is selected but changes are ignored
finding.evidence: ready is false when target is None. The kind combo is inside add_enabled_ui(ready), but the warp/mesh controls and buttons are outside. The update condition at line 190 checks ready && ..., so adjustments to sliders when ready=false do nothing, misleading the user.
finding.fix: Wrap the entire controls section in add_enabled_ui(ready) or disable individual widgets.

note: Controls are non-publishing until a valid captured target is ready; unselected controls are harmless option drafts, not ignored document commands.

finding.summary: Deep clone of Gesture on every mouse-move/hover update causes per-frame allocation of the entire graph, leading to UI lag on complex documents.
finding.evidence: In `update`, `let g = self.drag.as_ref().map(|d| d.gesture.clone()).map(Ok).unwrap_or_else(|| self.gesture(s))?;` clones the `Gesture` (which contains the graph) on every call. `update` is called from `canvas_input` at line 222 for every frame where the pointer is over the canvas (or captured), even if the document point hasn't changed. `Gesture::clone` likely deep clones the graph data (faces, edges, paths), which can be large.
finding.fix: Avoid cloning by borrowing the gesture: for drag, use `let g = self.drag.as_ref().map(|d| &d.gesture)`; for non-drag, return a reference from a new method or cache the graph separately. Also, only call `update` when the document point actually changed to avoid redundant recomputation.

note: Live Paint pointer motion borrows its retained captured graph instead of cloning it.

finding.summary: Adapter selector hard-requires an RTX 5090 Vulkan discrete GPU, so all tests in this file will panic on any machine without that exact GPU.
finding.evidence: In gpu(), create.native_adapter_selector is set to a closure that returns Err("RTX 5090 Vulkan discrete required") if no adapter matches name.contains("RTX 5090") && backend == Vulkan && device_type == DiscreteGpu. harness() calls gpu() for every test that uses the full harness, and none of those tests are marked #[ignore]. Running cargo test on a developer machine or CI without an RTX 5090 will cause wgpu_setup to fail and the test to panic.
finding.fix: Either make the GPU requirement conditional on an environment variable or feature, mark the affected tests #[ignore] and only run them on the dedicated acceptance machine, or provide a fallback/software adapter so the test suite can still execute without the specific GPU.

note: The task pins GPU acceptance to the real RTX 5090. These hardware gates deliberately fail when their required adapter is absent.

finding.summary: Invalid `egui::Event::ModifiersChanged` variant causes a compile error.
finding.evidence: `egui::Event` has no `ModifiersChanged` variant in standard egui versions; valid variants include `PointerMoved`, `PointerButton`, `Key`, etc. This line constructs `Event::ModifiersChanged(mods)`, so this module/test will not compile.
finding.fix: Remove the invalid event line. If modifier state needs to be set before the pointer event, set it through the harness input/context (e.g. `h.input_mut().modifiers = mods;`) rather than emitting a non-existent event.

note: ModifiersChanged exists in the pinned egui Event API; the integrated target compiles.

finding.summary: Inactive fill/stroke hit areas are incomplete; clicking visible non-overlapping regions (top strip of fill when stroke is active, bottom-left strip of stroke when fill is active) does not switch active paint.
finding.evidence: When stroke is active, the inactive fill hit is defined as Rect::from_min_max(rect.min, pos2(area.min.x + 14, rect.max.y)), covering only x=0..14, y=0..30; the top strip x=14..30, y=0..14 is visible but not interactive. Similarly, the inactive stroke hit covers only x=30..44, y=14..44, missing the bottom strip x=14..30, y=30..44. Users clicking on these colored areas get no response.
finding.fix: Define hit areas as the full rect for each paint and rely on interaction order, or add explicit rectangles for the protruding L-shaped regions so the entire visible area is clickable.

note: Both exposed strips of the inactive overlapping paint chip now participate in its hit area. Fill/stroke kittest coverage exercises switching.

finding.summary: tool_button allocates new Arc<[u8]> and URI on every call every frame, causing per-frame CPU allocations on hot UI path.
finding.evidence: In tool_button, lines 449-453 create a new Arc from icon bytes each frame; for mono icons it calls String::from_utf8_lossy(...).replace(...).into_bytes() which allocates at least one String and Vec. This function is called for every tool button in flyouts() and widget() during every GUI frame. The icon bytes are static and could be reused.
finding.fix: Cache the Arc<[u8]> using a OnceLock or store precomputed bytes, and reuse the same URI / egui::Image source each frame, e.g., use egui::include_image or ImageSource::Bytes with Arc::from_static.

note: Processed monochrome and color SVG bytes are retained in a OnceLock and shared by Arc, avoiding per-frame byte copies.

finding.summary: ruler_units returns wrong per_inch conversion for Millimeter and Inch design units (72 instead of 25.4 and 1.0).
finding.evidence: In ruler_units, when active document design_units is Millimeters, it returns (Unit::Millimeters, 72.), and for Inches it returns (Unit::Inches, 72.). The second tuple element is used as units per inch, so 72 is only correct for Points. For Millimeters the value should be 25.4 mm/inch, and for Inches it should be 1.0 inch/inch. This causes incorrect ruler scaling when the active document uses those design units and the ruler preference is Pixels.
finding.fix: Change line 153 to `Some(DesignUnits::Millimeters) => (Unit::Millimeters, 25.4),` and line 154 to `Some(DesignUnits::Inches) => (Unit::Inches, 1.0),`

note: The second return value is the point-size PPI used by Unit::to_px, not units per inch. 72 is correct. The production ruler now calls this bridge.

finding.summary: Expand… button enabled state uses appearance=true request, but the dialog operates with appearance=false, causing incorrect enable/disable behavior.
finding.evidence: Line 352 creates `request` with `appearance: true`. The resulting `reason` is used for both the 'Expand…' and 'Expand Appearance' buttons (lines 357-370). However, 'Expand…' opens a dialog that uses `appearance: false` in `rebuild` (line 94) and `commit_dialog` (line 122). Thus the button may be disabled when plain expand is allowed, or enabled when plain expand will fail.
finding.fix: Compute two separate disabled reasons: one using `appearance: false` for the 'Expand…' button, and one using `appearance: true` for the 'Expand Appearance' button and its execution.

note: Expand and Expand Appearance cache separate checked requests matching their actual appearance flags.

finding.summary: Draft continues editing the original layer after the active layer changes because the panel targets draft.edits[0] and State::begin does not reset/cancel for a different layer.
finding.evidence: panel fetches `id = st.active_layer`, but `current` is taken from `state.draft.as_ref().and_then(|d| d.edits.first()).cloned().unwrap_or(...)`. If a draft exists for layer A and the user selects layer B, `current` is A's edit. `state.begin(s, &[id], metadata)?` at line 236 returns early at line 155 because a draft exists, then `d.edits[0] = edit` mutates A. Input can similarly set `state.dragging` on B and update A's width at line 300. The resulting commit modifies the wrong layer.
finding.fix: Cancel the draft in `State::synchronize` when `session.active_layer` is not equal to the draft's target layer (or when the selected ids differ). Alternatively, make `begin` cancel/restart if the requested layer id is not already the draft target and have `panel`/`input` verify the draft matches the active layer before editing.

note: Frame drafts cancel on active-target changes and begin validates the requested targets before reusing a draft. Added target-switch regression.

finding.summary: A commit failure on pointer release leaves `State::dragging` true, so the resize gesture continues without the mouse button being pressed.
finding.evidence: In `apply`, `commit(s, d, metadata)?` returns early before `self.cancel()`. `input` calls `state.apply(s, metadata)?` on release at line 304 and propagates any error. If `commit` fails (e.g., `NativeOnly::store` rejects non-default options at line 28), `dragging` remains true and `draft` remains. On the next frame `input` sees `state.dragging == true`, `button_released` is false, and continues executing line 300 with the current pointer position. Reproducible by toggling Paragraph composer on and then dragging the frame width handle.
finding.fix: Ensure the drag state is cleared even if apply fails. For example, in `input` set `state.dragging = false` before/after `state.apply` (or on error), or modify `apply` to always clear `dragging`/draft on terminal commit errors.

note: Release ends the dragging flag before publication; a rejected commit retains a retryable draft without following the pointer. Added regression.

finding.summary: Every interactive frame edit clones the entire document and re-renders, causing per-frame full-document allocation and potential UI freezes on large documents.
finding.evidence: `input` calls `state.update(s)` on every pointer move while dragging (line 302), and `panel` calls it after every widget edit (line 240). `update` calls `preview` -> `prepare`, which unconditionally runs `(**source).clone()` at line 84, cloning all layers/caches. For large multi-layer/raster documents this is a hot-path full document clone plus text re-layout/render per frame.
finding.fix: Clone only the affected text layer(s) for preview, maintain a pre-rendered overlay/cache, or defer full document clone until commit. At least avoid cloning unrelated layers on every update.

note: Detached engine previews require a document snapshot; raster caches are shared. Preparation is bounded and the pointer performance gates measure the production path.

finding.summary: Bridge state stored in egui temporary data is cleared each frame, so the measure/area tool cannot be activated or maintain state across frames.
finding.evidence: bridge() reads with get_temp (line 360), but activate (line 369), set_scale (line 375), frame (line 392), and route (line 430) store with insert_temp. egui's temporary data is cleared at the end of each frame, so on the next frame get_temp returns None and Bridge::default() with mode=None, causing route to return false and the tool to remain inactive.
finding.fix: Use persistent egui data: replace insert_temp with insert and get_temp with get (i.e., ctx.data_mut(|d| d.insert(key(), b)) and ctx.data(|d| d.get(key()))).

note: egui temporary typed data persists across frames until replaced or garbage-collected; it is not cleared each frame. The measure lifecycle tests cover persistence.

finding.summary: In State::input error path, self.cancel() restores line but does not clear or recompute self.distance, leaving stale distance that may be displayed in the options panel.
finding.evidence: If update returns an error while a measure drag is active, input calls self.cancel() (line 122) which sets self.line = self.completed.clone() (possibly None) but does not touch self.distance. The options UI at line 272 shows state.distance if mode is Measure without checking state.line, so a distance can be displayed with no corresponding line or with a different completed line.
finding.fix: After self.cancel() in the error branch, set self.distance = None; or recompute it from self.line using the appropriate units (though units may be unavailable, so clearing is safer).

note: Measure cancellation clears the pending distance when restoring the completed line, preventing stale failed-preview measurements.

finding.summary: Per-pointer-move cloning of the entire base Gesture causes large allocations and UI lag with large meshes.
finding.evidence: In `motion`, `let mut next = c.base.clone();` is executed on every `PointerMoved` event. `c.base` is a `Gesture` containing `Commit` with all edits and mesh data for all selected layers. With the maximum allowed 50x50 mesh (2500 points with handles and colors), this clone is substantial and occurs on every mouse move, blocking the UI thread and violating the performance guidance on hot paths.
finding.fix: Avoid cloning the entire base on each move. Maintain a persistent working copy of the gesture and apply only delta updates to the moving point, or store the original mesh and compute the new state without deep clone. Alternatively, use copy-on-write techniques or smaller incremental updates.

note: Mesh motion updates the captured gesture directly with an absolute position rather than cloning its base gesture.

finding.summary: Per-pointer-move cloning of the full Commit for Preview actions doubles the allocation cost per move.
finding.evidence: In `events`, for each `PointerMoved` event, `actions.push(Action::Preview(request.clone()));` clones the entire `Commit` (which includes all layer edits and mesh data) and adds it to the action list. This happens in addition to the base clone in `motion`. The host then processes each Preview by calling `engine::preview_document`, which may further clone the document. This can cause severe lag when editing high-density meshes.
finding.fix: Avoid cloning the request on every move. Reuse a single `Commit` or use shared ownership (e.g., `Arc<Commit>`). Alternatively, throttle preview updates (e.g., one per frame) and only send a diff or the current state.

note: Mesh events emit one final preview request per event batch; release emits only its commit request.

finding.summary: Bridge state stored with egui temp data (get_temp/insert_temp) is cleared at the start of each frame, so b.owner is always None when frame runs and owner-change cancellation never executes.
finding.evidence: Line 13 uses `d.get_temp(key())`, line 16 uses `d.insert_temp(key(), b)`. egui's `*_temp` storage is cleared when a new frame begins. Consequently, at line 21 `b.owner` is always `None` (default Bridge) at the start of `frame`, so the branch at lines 21-23 never triggers. Any state requiring cancellation on tool/persona/module change is lost.
finding.fix: Use persistent `ctx.data`/`d.insert` instead of `get_temp`/`insert_temp`, or store `owner` and `State` in `PhotocraftApp` / persistent memory so it survives across frames.

note: egui temporary data persists across frames. The owner-change comparison is reachable and the lifecycle tests exercise it.
