finding.summary: Hardware-specific assert panics on any GPU other than one whose name contains 'RTX 5090', making the ignored test suite fail on all non-RTX 5090 machines.
finding.evidence: assert!(info.name.contains("RTX 5090"), "{info:?}"); is executed in harness() before any test body. Running `cargo test --ignored` on a machine with a different GPU (e.g., RTX 3080, AMD, Intel) will panic.
finding.fix: Remove or relax the exact GPU name check. Validate required capabilities (e.g., Vulkan backend, discrete GPU, Rgba32Float support) without pinning to a specific marketing name.

note: The owner explicitly requires real RTX 5090 gates; the ignored hardware acceptance intentionally asserts that adapter.

finding.summary: keys() always returns true when a vector path text draft is active, even if no key event was actually handled, blocking other key handlers.
finding.evidence: The function unconditionally returns true at line 122 after the loop, regardless of whether any event was matched and pushed to the `handled` vector. Unhandled events are left in `ctx.input`, but the boolean return value signals the caller that all keys were consumed, preventing global shortcuts and other handlers from processing them.
finding.fix: Return `!handled.is_empty()` instead of `true`, or otherwise indicate that keys were handled only if at least one event was actually processed.

note: Path Text keys reports consumption only when a key was actually handled, leaving unrelated shortcuts available.

finding.summary: Puppet Warp conversion prompt may target wrong layer because hover is not set before request_conversion is called from ensure_rig.
finding.evidence: In `ensure_rig`, when `PuppetGesture::begin` returns an error containing 'Convert', `self.request_conversion(s)` is called. However, `ensure_rig` is invoked at line 450 in `input_with` before any pointer event has been processed; at that moment `self.hover` is `None`. `request_conversion` then uses `self.hover.unwrap_or([0., 0.])`. If the artwork is not at the document origin, `conversion_targets` may fail to identify the correct layers, causing the conversion prompt to convert nothing or the wrong layers. This makes the tool unusable for off-origin artwork until the user moves the pointer over the shape and cancels the prompt to retrigger.
finding.fix: Ensure `hover` is set to the current pointer position before calling `ensure_rig`, or modify `ensure_rig` to obtain the current pointer position from the session/context and pass it to `request_conversion` instead of relying on `self.hover`.

note: Distort routing sets the current document-space hover before Puppet Warp conversion/rig capture.

finding.summary: After a successful puppet warp commit, a failure in recreating the rig causes inconsistent state rollback.
finding.evidence: In `up_inner`, after `run(s, "object.puppetWarp", ...)` succeeds (line 376-380), the document is modified. Then at line 386, `engine::PuppetGesture::begin` is called with `?`. If this call returns an error, `up_inner` returns `Err`. In `up_with` (line 350-359), `old_pins` was saved before `up_inner`; on error it executes `self.pins = old_pins;`. This reverts the pins to their pre-drag positions, but the document geometry has already been changed by the committed `puppetWarp` command. Consequently, the displayed pins no longer match the actual document geometry, leading to incorrect future interactions and potential data corruption.
finding.fix: After a successful commit, if recreating the rig fails, do not roll back the pins; instead clean up and report the error while preserving the committed document and pins state. Alternatively, commit and rig recreation should be atomic, or rollback handled only if the commit did not succeed.

note: A successful warp is retained when fresh-rig creation fails; rollback applies only to a still-valid uncommitted capture.

finding.summary: Saved PDF export options may contain artboard IDs from a previous document; they are not pruned to the current document, causing invalid artboard targets.
finding.evidence: open_dialog loads `vector.pdf.exportOptions` from prefs into `State.options` (lines 136-137). `State::open` then clones those options into the `Request` at line 25 without filtering `options.artboards` against the current document's artboards. The controls at lines 84-98 only display current artboards and provide no way to remove stale IDs while in Document scope. If the current document has different artboards, any previously saved IDs remain in `options.artboards`. When Export is clicked, `preflight(s, &r)` (line 42) is called with these stale IDs and can reject the document scope as invalid, blocking export from a newly opened dialog.
finding.fix: In `State::open`, after collecting `self.artboards`, retain only the `LayerId`s in `self.options.artboards` that are present in `self.artboards` (or clear the list if the document/artboard set changed).

note: Opening PDF export prunes saved artboard IDs against the active document.

finding.summary: Switching export scope from Document to Selection or Artboard permanently clears all artboard page selections, losing user input.
finding.evidence: When `kind != 0`, the `else` branch at line 96-98 executes `state.options.artboards.clear()`. If a user selects specific artboard pages under Document scope (lines 84-95), then temporarily switches to Selection or Artboard, every selected artboard is erased. Switching back to Document shows no pages selected, forcing the user to re-select them. This is a concrete state loss in the dialog.
finding.fix: Do not clear `state.options.artboards` when the scope is temporarily not Document. Keep the selections stored and only use them when exporting Document scope, or clear them only when the user explicitly changes the document/artboards set.

note: Scope changes preserve saved page selections; the export request clears them only for scopes that do not use document pages.

finding.summary: Direct-selection anchor sets are cloned every frame, causing per-frame heap allocation and copy on the UI thread.
finding.evidence: `frame()` invokes `selection(app)` each frame (line 71). Inside `selection`, when `app.ui.tool == DirectSelection` and the document matches, `d.anchors.clone()` (line 28) and each `a.anchors.clone()` (line 34) allocate and copy the full selected point list. This happens even when shortcuts are suppressed by `menu_nav::is_open(ctx)` or when no operation needs the owned clones, and scales with the number of selected anchors.
finding.fix: Pass `&d.anchors`/`&a.anchors` by reference to `state.shortcuts`/`state.menu` if the APIs allow, or compute and clone the anchor selection lazily only when a shortcut/menu/copy/paste action actually runs.

note: The keyboard frame materializes direct-selection anchors only when a pressed key event can dispatch a command. Menus capture selections on invocation.

finding.summary: Gesture is canceled before commit; if commit fails, completed path is lost.
finding.evidence: In up(), Outcome::Finished arm calls self.cancel() (line 125) before s.execute (line 126). If s.execute returns Err, the error propagates but self.gesture and preview are already None; the finished path cannot be recovered.
finding.fix: Execute the commit first, and only cancel self after a successful execute; or on error, restore the gesture.

note: Pen release publishes before discarding its completed gesture; failed publication leaves the draft available.

finding.summary: Gesture is canceled before commit; if commit fails, finished path is lost.
finding.evidence: In enter(), self.cancel() (line 135) is called before g.finish() and s.execute (line 138). If s.execute returns Err, the error propagates but self.gesture is already None, losing the finished path.
finding.fix: Commit first then cancel; or rollback on error.

note: Pen Enter finishes a cloned gesture and clears the retained draft only after successful publication.

finding.summary: May target active layer instead of selected layer when continuing a shape.
finding.evidence: destination() binds layer to st.active_layer and only checks that st.selected_layers.len() == 1, without verifying the selected layer is the active layer. If they differ, Target::Shape { layer } continues the active layer while the user selected a different layer.
finding.fix: Check that the selected layer is the active layer (e.g., st.selected_layers.len() == 1 && st.selected_layers[0] == layer) or use the selected layer for continuation.

note: Pen continuation chooses the actual single selected layer instead of an unrelated active-layer field.

finding.summary: Per-frame allocation and clone of point vector for each segment during overlay painting.
finding.evidence: paint_overlay builds a Vec<Pos2> of 33 points per segment and then clones it at line 275 to draw a black underlay before drawing the colored line. On complex paths with many segments, this causes avoidable per-frame allocations and clones on the UI hot path.
finding.fix: Avoid cloning by drawing the underlay and colored line using the same vector without clone, or reuse a scratch buffer.

note: Transient screen-space tessellation is required for the current zoom; its segments and node counts are bounded. The release pointer gate covers this path.

finding.summary: On capture.document.check error, state.capture is not cancelled, leaving a stale capture in state.
finding.evidence: In canvas(), when response.double_clicked_by(Primary) is true and capture exists, `capture.document.check(session, &state.scope)?;` propagates the error without calling `state.cancel()`. The stale PointerCapture remains in State, and subsequent pointer interactions may reuse it, causing incorrect gesture handling. In contrast, elsewhere in the same function when capture.target != hit, state.cancel() is called before returning the error.
finding.fix: Call `state.cancel()` before returning the error from `capture.document.check(...)?`, e.g., `if let Err(e) = capture.document.check(session, &state.scope) { state.cancel(); return Err(e); }`

note: Isolation clears a stale pointer capture when document validation fails.

finding.summary: Escape key is consumed by isolation exit even when dialogs are open, preventing the dialog from handling Escape.
finding.evidence: In frame(), `let escaped = escape(ctx, &mut b.isolation);` is called unconditionally. The `escape` function consumes the Escape key whenever isolation is active, without checking `app.ui.dialogs.is_empty()`. Meanwhile, `view_modes::shortcuts` on line 200 is gated with `vector && app.ui.dialogs.is_empty()`, showing that dialogs should suppress global shortcuts. Thus, if a dialog is open and isolation is active, pressing Escape exits isolation instead of closing the dialog.
finding.fix: Gate the escape call with `app.ui.dialogs.is_empty()` (or pass dialog state into escape and only consume Escape when no dialogs are open).

note: Isolation handles Escape only when no application dialog is open.

finding.summary: Failed PDF import clears previously loaded source and info even when the new file is invalid, causing loss of transient import state.
finding.evidence: set_named_source error path executes `self.source.clear(); self.info = None;` and returns Err. In offer(), if a user has a valid PDF already loaded in the dialog and tries to open an invalid PDF, this clears the previous source. dialog_open remains true, so the dialog now shows an empty invalid state.
finding.fix: On error, preserve the previous valid source/info; only clear when there was no previous source or explicitly reset separately.

note: An invalid replacement PDF reports its error while retaining the previously valid source and info. Added regression.

finding.summary: Changing PDF settings cancels pending preview but does not clear warning state, leaving stale warning buttons that may target layers from the previous import.
finding.evidence: In controls, `if changed { state.cancel(); }`. cancel (lines 89-98) clears request/scene/preview/drag/context but not warnings/warning_document/warning_targets. warning_controls (line 236) still iterates the old warnings. After an Open PDF, the active document still matches warning_document and layer ids exist, so buttons are enabled and can select layers from the old document even though the dialog settings have changed.
finding.fix: Clear warnings, warning_document, and warning_targets in cancel() or when settings change.

note: Changing PDF preview settings clears warning targets together with the staged scene.

finding.summary: PDF preview is regenerated from scratch on every pointer move during placement drag, potentially freezing the UI for large PDFs.
finding.evidence: In input, `Event::PointerMoved(pos) if state.drag.is_some() => state.motion(session, to_doc(pos))`. motion calls `pdf_import::preview(session, request, scene)?.0` and replaces self.preview. This is executed for each pointer move event; no throttling or caching. For a complex PDF, repeated full preview generation on the UI thread can block rendering.
finding.fix: Throttle preview updates (e.g., only on specific frames or after drag stops), cache expensive parts, or use a lightweight preview representation for dragging.

note: The source is parsed and native caches prepared once at stage. Motion translates the prepared scene into a detached preview; it does not decode the PDF again.

finding.summary: Hardware-specific tests are not ignored and will fail on machines without an RTX 5090
finding.evidence: The harness() function (line 12-26) uses a native_adapter_selector that returns an error if no RTX 5090 Vulkan discrete adapter is found. The tests selection_full_app_gpu_live_lasso_cancel_release_wand_add_rtx5090 (line 88) and selection_full_app_gpu_group_circle_then_node_lasso_delete_03_rtx5090 (line 217) are annotated with #[test] but not #[ignore], so they will run with cargo test and panic on any system lacking the required GPU, breaking the test suite.
finding.fix: Add #[ignore] to these two tests, or gate them behind a feature flag/environment variable that is only enabled on developer machines with RTX 5090.

note: These are explicit real-adapter app acceptance tests required by the task. Missing hardware is a failure under LC_REQUIRE_GPU=1.

finding.summary: Holding Alt after starting a Continue operation forces the path to close.
finding.evidence: When Alt is held on Down and an endpoint is hit, `Operation::Continue` is used (line 102-106). Later in update_preview, `closed = mods.alt || (matches!(g.capture.operation, Operation::Create { .. }) && near)` sets `closed` to true because `mods.alt` is still true during the drag. Then `engine::prepare` is called with `closed && g.samples.len() > 2`, closing the continued path even if the cursor is not near the start.
finding.fix: Only allow Alt to force closing for Create operations: e.g., `let closed = near || (mods.alt && matches!(g.capture.operation, Operation::Create { .. }));` or track Alt state from the original Down event separately.

note: Alt closes only a newly created Pencil path; continuing an existing open curve stays open.

finding.summary: Sculpt mode clones the entire sample vector on every pointer Move, causing O(n^2) allocations/copies.
finding.evidence: In `update_preview` sculpt branch, `let mut samples = g.samples.clone();` is executed for each Move event. `g.samples` grows with each move up to `fitting::MAX_SAMPLES`. This results in quadratic total copying over a stroke.
finding.fix: Avoid cloning when no reversal is needed; use iterators/reversed view or clone only when the direction actually changes.

note: Backward sculpt preparation temporarily reverses the retained samples, restores them even on error, and avoids copying the growing vector.

finding.summary: Every pointer Move calls engine::prepare with the full sample list, potentially causing O(n^2) fitting.
finding.evidence: Line 179: `self.preview = Some(engine::prepare(session, &capture, &g.samples, closed && g.samples.len() > 2)?);` is called on each Move. If `engine::prepare` refits from all samples, this is O(n) per move, O(n^2) per stroke, blocking the UI on long strokes.
finding.fix: Throttle preview updates or use an incremental fitting algorithm that only adjusts the last segments.

note: The complete bounded fit is needed to give the interactive preview exactly the same geometry as publication. The fitter and release-frame gates bound this work.

finding.summary: Missing selected layer aborts the search in find_endpoint/hit_curve, losing candidates and skipping remaining layers.
finding.evidence: At line 206 (and line 228), `let LayerContent::Shape(sh) = &st.doc.layer(id)?.content else { continue; };` uses `?` on Option in a function returning Option. If `doc.layer(id)` is None (e.g., stale selection after layer deletion), the function returns None immediately, discarding any previously found best match and not checking other selected layers.
finding.fix: Use `let Some(layer) = st.doc.layer(id) else { continue; };` and then inspect `layer.content` instead of using `?`.

note: Session::selected_layers filters IDs through the current document walk before these searches. A missing selected layer cannot abort the loop in this API.

finding.summary: O(n*m) nested loop over groups and swatches on every frame causes performance degradation with large swatch lists
finding.evidence: for group in ... { for w in book.swatches.iter().filter(|w| w.group == group.map(|g| g.id)) { ... } } scans all swatches for each group, leading to quadratic behavior.
finding.fix: Precompute a mapping from Option<group_id> to swatch references, or sort swatches by group and iterate in chunks.

note: Swatches are grouped once by group ID before drawing the group rows, removing repeated full-list scans.

finding.summary: edit_color converts any non-RGB color to RGB, losing original color mode (e.g., CMYK becomes RGB) when user edits it
finding.evidence: edit_color takes &mut Color, converts to rgba bytes, then on change sets *c = Color::rgba(bytes[0]/255., ...), which creates a new RGB color and discards the previous mode and other components.
finding.fix: Preserve the original color mode: update the color in its current mode, e.g., if original is Rgb, set RGBA; if CMYK, convert back to CMYK or edit in that space using appropriate UI.

note: The picker converts edited sRGB bytes back to the original CMYK, normalized Lab or grayscale mode. Added color-space/alpha regression.

finding.summary: state.error is not cleared on successful actions, causing stale error messages to persist after a subsequent successful operation
finding.evidence: After an error is set (e.g., at line 97 on Add Swatch failure), if a later action succeeds (e.g., clicking Add Swatch again with valid id at lines 83-98), the error remains because only successful preview (line 291) clears it. No other path sets state.error = None.
finding.fix: Clear state.error at the start of each panel call or after any successful action that previously failed.

note: Successful swatch publication clears the old error; failed publication records the new error.

finding.summary: Holding Shift while dragging a new Artboard exactly vertically/horizontally creates a zero-width/height rectangle because `f64::signum()` returns 0 for zero.
finding.evidence: In `drag_rect`, `dx = dx.signum() * side;` and `dy = dy.signum() * side;` where `side` is the max of abs deltas. When one delta is 0.0 (e.g., perfect vertical drag), its signum is 0, so that axis becomes 0. The resulting box has zero width or height and is either rejected by `math::validate_rect` (error) or creates a degenerate Artboard. Reachable via Tool::Artboard + Shift + straight vertical/horizontal drag.
finding.fix: When applying the square constraint, use a signed side that defaults to positive for a zero delta, e.g. `let sx = if dx >= 0.0 { 1.0 } else { -1.0 }; dx = sx * side;` and similarly for dy, or clamp the zero axis to `side` with a consistent sign.

note: Rust f64::signum returns 1 for positive zero and -1 for negative zero, not zero. Axis-aligned square drags retain a nonzero second extent.

finding.summary: Point Transform overlay calls `path_nodes` every frame, allocating a Vec of all knot points and traversing selected layers on each paint.
finding.evidence: `overlay` runs for the Point Transform tool and at line 687 iterates `path_nodes(doc, &ids)`. `path_nodes` recursively walks `LayerContent::Shape`/`Group` and collects all anchors into a fresh `Vec` (lines 118-136). For complex selections, this is a per-frame allocation and traversal on the UI thread, which can cause frame drops.
finding.fix: Cache the collected points in `State` (e.g., recompute only when selection, document revision, or preview changes) and reuse the cached Vec during overlay drawing.

note: The visible Point Transform overlay builds bounded screen geometry from selected native nodes. This is projection work, and the production pointer-frame gate measures it.

finding.summary: Race condition in test: unwrap on pending_preview may panic if the preview job completes before the assertion.
finding.evidence: After pointer() triggers a drag, the test immediately calls h.state().state.pending_preview().unwrap(). The job may finish within the same step (poll_jobs runs in harness step), causing pending_preview() to return None and the unwrap to panic, making the test flaky.
finding.fix: Replace unwrap with a check or use a helper that waits until a pending preview appears, e.g., loop with run_steps until pending_preview() is Some, then capture the ID.

note: pending_preview is the retained job ID; workers send results through a channel and cannot mutate the UI State. It clears only when the UI explicitly polls results.

finding.summary: Bridge state is stored in egui temporary data, which is cleared at the end of each frame, losing all cross-frame state.
finding.evidence: `bridge` reads via `d.get_temp(key())` (line 16) and `store` writes via `d.insert_temp(key(), b)` (line 19). egui's `insert_temp` is explicitly temporary per-frame and is cleared before the next frame. Therefore `State` (including `open`, `preview`, `generation`, `cache`) resets to `Default` every frame. The Repeat panel will appear for at most one frame after `open()` is called, and any user interaction or cached projection is lost, making the feature unusable.
finding.fix: Use `d.get_persisted` / `d.insert_persisted` if the types implement the required serde traits, or store `Bridge` in `PhotocraftApp` or another session-level structure instead of egui temporary data.

note: egui temporary typed state survives frames. Repeat lifecycle/input tests exercise retained drafts and captures.

finding.summary: Full document comparison inside timed performance loop skews frame time measurements.
finding.evidence: In colour39_full_app_2000_objects_release_pointer_frames, inside the loop (lines 161-168), each iteration calls `assert_eq!(h.state().session.active().unwrap().doc, before);`. The document contains 2000 layers, so comparing it is O(n) and adds overhead that is not part of the app's frame processing, making the measured frame time unreliable and potentially causing the performance gate to fail.
finding.fix: Remove the assertion from inside the timed loop; after the loop, verify the document hasn't changed once (e.g., after all pointer moves and before Apply).

note: The full document equality assertion now runs after the timed pointer-frame loop, leaving the measured samples free of comparison cost.

finding.summary: Per-frame cloning of each row's `from` vector causes unnecessary allocations and O(total source colors) work on every frame.
finding.evidence: In the row rendering loop, `for i in plan.rows[row].from.clone()` clones the entire vector for every row on every frame the dialog is shown. If the artwork has many source colours/groups, this is a hot-path allocation and CPU cost.
finding.fix: Iterate by reference instead: `for &i in &plan.rows[row].from` (adjust body to use `i` directly).

note: Recolor rows iterate borrowed source indices instead of cloning each vector every frame.

finding.summary: Hex input validation accepts a leading '+' sign as a valid hex string, allowing Apply with non-hexagonal input.
finding.evidence: `u32::from_str_radix` for unsigned integers accepts an optional leading `+`. Thus `"+12345"` has length 6 and parses successfully to `0x12345`, so `valid_hex` becomes true and Apply is enabled even though the field does not contain six hexadecimal digits (the same parse logic at line 111 will set the colour).
finding.fix: Replace the parse check with an explicit hex-digit validation, e.g. `v.len() == 6 && v.bytes().all(|b| b.is_ascii_hexdigit())` before parsing.

note: Hex validation checks ASCII hexadecimal digits explicitly, rejecting a leading plus sign in both parsing and Apply availability.

finding.summary: Panel reads effects from the first selected layer only, but actions (toggle, move, remove, edit) are applied to all selected layers via Gesture::update. If selected layers have different effect stacks, operations fail with 'effect index is absent' or produce unintended changes.
finding.evidence: Code at lines 115-116 reads effects only from ids.first(); loop at 124-153 uses those indices for actions; lines 157-176 apply indices to all layers through panel_edit without validating that all layers have the same stack length. Example: select two layers, one with 2 effects, one with 1; clicking 'Move effect up' on index 1 of the first layer calls Action::Move(1,0), which will succeed for the first but return Err for the second when effects.get_mut(1) is out of bounds, or vice versa.
finding.fix: Before entering the panel, validate that all selected layers have identical effect stacks (same length and effect kinds/order) or restrict editing to the first layer; otherwise display an error and disable editing controls.

note: The Path Effects panel identifies mixed selected stacks and suppresses index-based edits until the stacks match.

finding.summary: Move Distance/Angle mode passes the angle as a linear Y-offset without converting to Cartesian coordinates.
finding.evidence: In `Kind::Move`, when `move_mode == MoveMode::Distance`, the code calls `engine::move_by(number(&self.fields[0])?, number(&self.fields[1])?)`. The UI labels for Distance mode are 'Distance' and 'Angle', so the second field is an angle in degrees, but `move_by` expects dx, dy offsets. This produces incorrect transformation when the angle is non-zero.
finding.fix: Convert polar coordinates to Cartesian: `let dist = number(&self.fields[0])?; let angle = number(&self.fields[1])?.to_radians(); let dx = dist * angle.cos(); let dy = dist * angle.sin();` then call `engine::move_by(dx, dy)`.

note: Distance/Angle calls engine::move_by(distance, angle), which computes Cartesian offsets.

finding.summary: After successful 'Convert to Curves' action, `self.pending` is not cleared, causing the conversion dialog to reappear and allowing duplicate publishes.
finding.evidence: In the pending conversion window, action 1 does: `let mut c = request; c.conversion = ConversionChoice::Curves; if let Err(e) = self.publish(s, &c) { ... }`. There is no `else { self.pending = None; }`. If `publish` succeeds, `self.pending` remains `Some(request)`, so the window will be shown again next frame with the same request, potentially triggering duplicate transformations.
finding.fix: After a successful `publish` call, explicitly set `self.pending = None;` (or ensure `publish` clears it, but adding explicit clear is safer).

note: Convert to Curves clears pending after its successful command sequence; the conversion dialog does not publish twice.

finding.summary: In `Kind::Each`, the seed is parsed unconditionally, so an empty or invalid seed causes an error even when `random` is false and seed is not used.
finding.evidence: The `Each` struct includes a `seed` field, but the operation logic may ignore it when `random` is false. However, `request` always executes `self.seed.trim().parse().map_err(|_| "Seed must be an unsigned integer".to_string())?`. If the user leaves the seed field empty and does not enable Random, the operation fails with an error that is irrelevant to the selected behavior.
finding.fix: Only parse the seed when `self.random` is true; otherwise use a default value (e.g., `0`) or skip the field entirely.

note: Transform Each parses seed only when Random is enabled; deterministic transforms accept an unused empty seed.

finding.summary: Deserializing missing or null `warnings` from command response causes an error after a successful import/placement; placement state remains pending.
finding.evidence: In `place` (line 71) and `open` (line 77), `response.get("warnings").cloned().unwrap_or_default()` returns `Value::Null` when the response lacks `warnings` or has `warnings: null`. `serde_json::from_value::<Vec<VectorWarning>>(Value::Null)` fails with "invalid type: null, expected a sequence". In `place`, this error occurs before `self.cancel()`, so `self.request`, `self.scene`, and `self.preview` remain set even though the engine already executed the placement. The UI shows an error and remains in pending placement mode, allowing accidental duplicate placement.
finding.fix: Deserialize into `Option<Vec<VectorWarning>>` or provide a default empty JSON array, e.g. `let warnings: Vec<VectorWarning> = response.get("warnings").cloned().map(serde_json::from_value).transpose()?.unwrap_or_default();`

note: The integrated SVG command response always contains its warnings array, including an empty array. The checked response contract is shared with this caller.

finding.summary: O(n^2) anchor subtraction can freeze UI on large node selections
finding.evidence: In publish_nodes, Mode::Subtract uses `hit.anchors.contains(a)` inside a filter over `old.iter()`. Both hit.anchors and old are Vecs of anchors; if each contains thousands of elements, this performs millions of linear searches on the UI thread upon pointer release.
finding.fix: Collect hit.anchors into a HashSet before filtering, or sort both vectors and use set difference to achieve O(n log n) or O(n).

note: Anchor subtraction uses a HashSet for membership instead of a nested scan.

finding.summary: node_base cloned every frame during node-mode gesture causing per-frame allocation
finding.evidence: The stale check `|| (c.node_mode && c.node_base != node_base(direct))` calls node_base(direct) on every frame while a capture is active and node_mode is true. node_base clones all anchor Vecs from the direct selection, so with many selected anchors, this causes a full allocation and clone each frame on the UI hot path.
finding.fix: Cache the node_base fingerprint (e.g., length and hash) and only recompute the full vector when the anchor content changes, or store a generation counter with the direct selection.

note: Node-base comparisons borrow the captured sets instead of cloning them each frame.

finding.summary: Incorrect test assertion: expected rotated point coordinate x ≈ -60 is mathematically inconsistent with the given 45° rotation around click origin (20,20). The test will fail when the code behaves correctly.
finding.evidence: The test rotates a square from (20,20) to (100,100) by 45° with origin at (20,20) (Alt-click at (20,20)). The original knot[1] is at (100,20). After 45° rotation around (20,20), the new position should be (20 + 80*cos45°, 20 + 80*sin45°) ≈ (76.57, 76.57). The assertion requires p.x ≈ -60 and p.y ≈ 20, which corresponds to no standard rotation of this square. This assertion will fail when the rotation is implemented correctly.
finding.fix: Correct the expected coordinates to match the actual rotation transformation, e.g., assert p.x ≈ 76.568 and p.y ≈ 76.568 (or verify the intended rotation origin and angle and use the correct expected values).

note: The regression uses the documented transform coordinates and was corrected by its package before integration. The integrated transform suite checks the final fixture.

finding.summary: Per-frame clone of the full preview Document through egui temporary state.
finding.evidence: State stores `preview: Option<Document>` (line 14). `panel()` retrieves the full State with `ctx.data_mut(|d| d.get_temp::<State>(app_key()).unwrap_or_default())`, which clones State. If a preview Document is present, this clones the potentially large Document every frame. `frame()` (line 224) and `display_doc()` (line 235) perform the same clone. This can stall the UI thread and allocate large amounts of memory while a preview is active.
finding.fix: Store `preview: Option<Arc<Document>>` in State, or otherwise avoid cloning the Document when reading/writing temporary state.

note: Graphic Styles preview documents are shared Arc snapshots in the egui bridge rather than copied documents.

finding.summary: `unique` performs O(1025*N) work and is called every frame in `show_with_hooks`.
finding.evidence: `unique` loops over `1..=1025` and for each candidate scans all `store.graphic_styles`. It is called from line 134 whenever the name is empty or equals an existing style, and unconditionally from line 182 for the duplicate action. This runs each frame, causing UI frame-time to scale poorly with large style libraries.
finding.fix: Compute unique names lazily only when the corresponding action is activated, or use a HashSet of existing names to avoid repeated full scans.

note: Unique style naming builds one name set and probes it, avoiding repeated scans for every candidate suffix.

finding.summary: Rename style does not enforce unique style names.
finding.evidence: New style creation (lines 134-144) and duplication (lines 182-189) both use `unique` to avoid duplicate names, but `Operation::Rename { style, name }` at line 179 passes `state.name` directly without any uniqueness check. A user can rename a style to the name of another existing style, creating duplicate names and making the style list ambiguous.
finding.fix: Validate or uniquify the rename name before building `Operation::Rename`, for example by rejecting duplicates or using `unique` when a conflict is detected.

note: Native styles are identified by stable IDs; duplicate display names are permitted by the native style contract. Rename preserves references.

finding.summary: PointerGuard retains stale state after using the Pen tool, causing the first click with a different tool to be consumed and show a cancellation error.
finding.evidence: In PointerGuard::intercept, the Up event only clears target/tool for non-Pen tools: 'if matches!(ev, ToolEvent::Up { .. }) && app.ui.tool != Tool::Pen { self.target = None; self.tool = None; }' (line 97). After a Pen stroke ends, target and tool remain Some. When the user selects a different tool via select_tool (line 172), cancel() does not clear PointerGuard. On the next Down event with the new tool, stale becomes true at line 80 because self.tool (Some(Pen)) != app.ui.tool. The function then clears and returns true, swallowing the event and setting status to 'The gesture was cancelled; try again'.
finding.fix: Clear the PointerGuard when the tool changes, e.g., call app.pointer_guard.clear() inside select_tool after cancel() (or inside cancel()). Alternatively, adjust the Up handler to clear for Pen when the pen session actually ends.

note: Selecting another tool explicitly clears the persona pointer guard along with the outgoing tool capture.

finding.summary: Test clicks saved profile 'Fine' without reopening the combo box after selecting 'Uniform', causing get_by_label to fail because the popup is closed.
finding.evidence: At line 145 the combo box is opened, then line 147 clicks 'Uniform' which selects the item and closes the combo popup. Line 150 directly calls h.get_by_label("Fine").click(); with no preceding click on the combo box. In egui, ComboBox popups close after an item is selected, so 'Fine' is no longer present/visible in the accessibility tree, and the query will panic or fail.
finding.fix: After selecting 'Uniform' at line 147, reopen the combo box (similar to lines 115-116 or 145-146) before attempting to click 'Fine'. For example: h.get_by_role_and_label(egui::accesskit::Role::ComboBox, "Width profile").click(); h.run(); then h.get_by_label("Fine").click();

note: The package's corrected test reopens the profile combo before selecting Fine; integration runs that final test.

finding.summary: Missing file-save picker service silently cancels the export instead of reporting an error.
finding.evidence: `services.pick_save` is an `Option`. Calling `and_then(|pick| pick("drawing.svg"))` on it returns `None` both when the service is missing and when the user cancels the picker. The branch at line 112 then executes `state.cancel(); return Ok(None);`, so a missing picker service behaves exactly like a user cancellation: no file is written, no error is shown, and the dialog closes. In contrast, a missing write service is checked at line 117 and returns an error.
finding.fix: Match on `services.pick_save.as_mut()` explicitly: if the service is `None`, return `EngineError::Other("file save picker service unavailable".into())`; only treat the picker's own `None` return value as user cancellation.

note: SVG export returns an error when the save-picker service is unavailable; an actual user picker cancellation remains cancellation.

finding.summary: Quick click (press and release in same frame) ignores release, cancels placement instead of placing symbol.
finding.evidence: In canvas_input, if egui reports both primary_pressed and primary_released true in the same frame, the event is constructed as Event::Down because 'if pressed' comes before 'else if released'. The Down event starts the placement but the Up event never fires. On the next frame, neither down nor released is true, so event becomes Event::Cancel, which calls pointer with Cancel and cancels the placement. This makes a fast click fail to place.
finding.fix: Prioritize released over pressed, e.g., 'if released { Event::Up } else if pressed { Event::Down }', or detect both and send Down then Up in the same frame.

note: Same-frame symbol press/release dispatches Down followed by Up so a quick click places exactly once.

finding.summary: Placement/preview position uses view transform stored at pointer down instead of current transform, causing wrong coordinates if zoom/pan changes mid-drag.
finding.evidence: InputCapture stores xf.zoom and xf.flip in canvas_input at line 363. Later, in the 'at' calculation, the code uses c.zoom and c.flip instead of consulting the current ViewXform xf. If the user zooms or pans (e.g., with trackpad or wheel) while dragging, the document-space delta is computed with the old zoom/flip and ignores pan changes, so the placed/previewed symbol appears at an incorrect position.
finding.fix: Use the current xf (or recompute from screen position each event) to map the latest pointer position to document coordinates, rather than storing and reusing zoom/flip/origin.

note: The placement view transform is intentionally captured at pointer-down, consistent with the shared gesture coordinate contract and placement tests.

finding.summary: Error from Capture::new in Edit Master is silently ignored, leaving the user with no feedback when the button appears to do nothing.
finding.evidence: The Edit Master button handler uses '&& let (Ok(c), Some(id), Some(st)) = (Capture::new(session), state.selected, session.active())'. If Capture::new returns Err(e), the pattern fails and the click is a no-op. No state.error is set, unlike the Place Symbol and Create Symbol handlers which capture and display errors.
finding.fix: Match on Capture::new(session) explicitly, such as 'match Capture::new(session) { Ok(c) => ... , Err(e) => state.error = Some(e.to_string()) }'.

note: Edit Master now displays Capture::new failures through the symbol panel error state.

finding.summary: Full document clone on every cache invalidation (e.g., pan/zoom) causes large per-frame allocations and UI thread blocking.
finding.evidence: In prepare(), line 259: 'let mut base = if state.mode == Mode::Outline { None } else { Some(doc.clone()) };' clones the entire Document including all raster images. FrameCache::prepare() includes transform and clip in the cache key, so panning or zooming changes the key and triggers a new full document clone each frame.
finding.fix: Avoid deep-cloning the entire document. Use Arc<Document> or copy-on-write for the base document, or only clone the layers that are modified, and cache the base separately from transform-dependent data.

note: The view cache reuses prepared frames keyed by document snapshot, revision, view and clip. Detached projection ownership is required; repeated unchanged frames reuse it.

finding.summary: X-ray mode does not apply the X-ray fill effect to children of a group when the group itself is outlined.
finding.evidence: In native_xray(), for a LayerContent::Group, the function returns the cloned group with effects defaulted but does not process child layers. The opacity multiplication at line 117 is skipped for groups. Therefore if a user outlines a group in X-ray mode (via ctrl+click eye), prepare() calls geometry.xray_layer() for the group, and the group's descendants remain fully opaque instead of receiving the X-ray fill alpha. Symbol handling does recurse, but direct groups do not.
finding.fix: Recursively apply native_xray() to child layers of a group (similar to the fade function used for symbols) or reduce opacity of all leaf descendants within the group.

note: ViewState::outlined inherits outlined ancestors, and prepare walks each descendant independently. Group children receive their own X-ray projection/fade.

finding.summary: Hot-path `at()` performs 32 allocation+length computations per call, then clones the segment again for tangent.
finding.evidence: In the non-linear branch, each of the 32 binary-search iterations calls `geom::PathData::single(section(part, 0, 0., mid)).length()`, which allocates a new SubPath and numerically integrates length. Line 77 clones `part` again to convert to BezPath. For each spine sample point (often hundreds per frame) this causes many heap allocations and CPU-heavy length computations.
finding.fix: Precompute a length lookup table per segment in `Spine::new` (or cache length samples) and binary-search the cached table instead of repeatedly calling length; compute the tangent directly from `part.segment(0)` via the curve's derivative/tangent method instead of cloning and converting to BezPath.

note: Spine inverse lookup evaluates cubic subsegments and native arclength directly, without allocating PathData at each step or cloning for the tangent.

finding.summary: Zero tangent at curve endpoints returns an arbitrary angle instead of a fallback direction.
finding.evidence: `geom::bez::tangent(segment, t)` returns the derivative vector. For a cubic with coalesced control points (e.g., P0==P1 or P2==P3), the derivative at t=0 or t=1 can be (0,0). Then `atan2(0.0, 0.0)` yields 0.0, which is not a meaningful orientation and can misplace the first/last object on the spine.
finding.fix: Check the tangent length against a small epsilon; if it is near zero, use a one-sided derivative (e.g., tangent at t+epsilon or t-epsilon) or fall back to the chord direction between adjacent control points.

note: geom::bez::tangent already falls back to the first noncoincident endpoint control or chord when the derivative vanishes.

finding.summary: FreeTransform handles are drawn at the original bounds rather than the current distorted quad, so the active handle does not follow the pointer during a distort drag.
finding.evidence: In paint, the outline `q` is taken from the active Distort drag quad (`self.drag` -> `Operation::Distort { quad, .. }`) when present, but the handle loop at line 588 always draws `handles(b)` from the original bounds. During a distort drag, the user sees the quad move while the handles stay at the starting positions.
finding.fix: When a Distort drag is active, derive the handle positions from the current quad (e.g., compute corners/midpoints from `q`) instead of using `handles(b)`.

note: Free Distort handles use the current quad corners and edge midpoints, matching the displayed distorted boundary.

finding.summary: Reshape paint only draws knots for layers whose ID is exactly in the selected list, but mouse-down allows selecting knots on descendant layers of selected groups; this leaves selected descendant knots invisible.
finding.evidence: `down` for Kind::Reshape uses an ancestry check: `ids.iter().any(|id| *id == l.id || doc.path_of(l.id).zip(doc.path_of(*id)).is_some_and(|(p, root)| p.starts_with(&root)))`. `paint` only checks `ids.contains(&l.id)`, line 602. If a group is selected and a child shape knot is clicked, the child node is stored in `selected_nodes` but never drawn. The `contains` check is also inside the innermost knot loop, making paint O(total knots * selected IDs) each frame.
finding.fix: Compute the same selected/ancestor condition once per layer outside the knot loops, and use that boolean for drawing.

note: Reshape overlays include descendants of selected groups, matching the native mouse-down selection scope.

finding.summary: The Enter shortcut opens a new dialog even when a pending commit or envelope request is active, leaving both states alive and potentially orphaning the pending transform.
finding.evidence: The Enter handling at line 512 runs before the `self.dialog.is_some() || self.pending.is_some() || self.envelope_request.is_some()` early return at line 535. `open_dialog` sets `self.dialog` but does not clear `self.pending` or `self.envelope_request`. After release sets `self.pending` for a Distort with conversion targets, pressing Enter will set `dialog` while `pending` remains, producing two active states.
finding.fix: Guard Enter with `!self.active()` (or specifically ensure `pending`/`envelope_request` are handled before opening a new dialog), and/or have `open_dialog` clear `pending` and `envelope_request`.

note: Enter opens a transform dialog only when no pending transform or envelope request owns the state.

finding.summary: Operator precedence makes only the vertical shear fallback be halved, producing an asymmetric fallback lever when the reference point lies on the center line.
finding.evidence: `let fallback = if horizontal { b[3] } else { b[2] } / 2.;` parses as `if horizontal { b[3] } else { b[2] / 2. }`. Thus horizontal shear uses full height as fallback while vertical shear uses half width. If the intended fallback is half of the relevant extent in both cases, horizontal shear from the center will use a lever twice as large as expected.
finding.fix: Parenthesize the if expression: `let fallback = (if horizontal { b[3] } else { b[2] }) / 2.;` or write both branches explicitly.

note: The fallback expression explicitly parenthesizes the conditional before division, giving both axes the same half-extent lever.

finding.summary: Panic on empty closed subpath: qa[0] indexed without checking that normal(a) is non-empty.
finding.evidence: In prepare(), when both a and b are closed, starts == (None,None), and a.anchors.len() != b.anchors.len(), the code takes the else branch and calls normal(&a) which returns an empty Vec if a.anchors.is_empty(). The next line uses qa[0] unconditionally. Empty subpaths are handled elsewhere (e.g., depth, grow, collapse), so user input containing an empty closed contour can reach this panic.
finding.fix: Use qa.first().copied().unwrap_or(geom::Vec2::ZERO) or add a guard: if qa.is_empty() { return Ok((a,b)); } before indexing.

note: blend::validate_path rejects empty subpaths before prepare can index normalized anchors.

finding.summary: Component operation is applied only to the first subpath of each component; all subsequent subpaths get PathOp::Join, losing the component's boolean operation.
finding.evidence: In with_starts(), for each matched pair within a component, the pushed PathOp is `if index == 0 { op } else { PathOp::Join }`. If a component contains multiple subpaths that share the same effective op (e.g., a subtract or intersect component with holes), only the first subpath retains op, while later subpaths are set to Join, changing the path's boolean semantics when interpolated.
finding.fix: Use the component's op for all subpaths in the component, e.g., push `(x, y, op)` instead of the conditional, or verify the intended op semantics and ensure all subpaths preserve it.

note: PathOp::Join intentionally groups later contours into the first contour's compound component; the operation belongs only on the component's first contour.

finding.summary: damage() fails to compare document resolution_dpi, so DPI changes do not trigger repaint and the UI shows stale rendering.
finding.evidence: The early full-invalidation check at lines 104-110 compares old and new id, size, mode, depth, icc_profile, and global_light, but omits resolution_dpi. In project()'s text branch (line 38 and line 50) doc.resolution_dpi is used for layout and rendering. If only resolution_dpi changes, layer contents and dependency keys remain equal, so the loop skips all layers, changed stays Rect::EMPTY, and the function returns Some(empty) instead of None/full damage, leaving the old rendering on screen.
finding.fix: Add `|| old.resolution_dpi != new.resolution_dpi` to the condition that returns None for full repaint.

note: damage already compares resolution_dpi and returns full invalidation on a change.

finding.summary: Shape rendering path lacks any pixel-count or scale-bounds validation, allowing a large user zoom scale to request a huge raster surface and cause memory exhaustion or panic.
finding.evidence: In project()'s Shape arm, `vector::render_shape_view(s, doc.pixel_format(), cpu::scaled_rect(doc.bounds(), scale)?, clip, scale)` is called with a scale derived from user zoom. The text path explicitly checks coordinate limits (lines 47-48) and `cpu::MAX_VIEW_PIXELS` (line 59), but the shape path performs no such checks. A sufficiently large finite scale (e.g., 1e6) causes `scaled_rect` to return a rect with enormous width/height, and `render_shape_view` will likely attempt to allocate a surface of that size, leading to OOM/panic.
finding.fix: Before calling `render_shape_view`, validate that `scale` is finite, positive, and within safe bounds, and check that the scaled rect area does not exceed `cpu::MAX_VIEW_PIXELS`. Return `Err(cpu::ViewError(...))` if exceeded.

note: Native scaled shape projection validates scale 1..64, finite coordinates and visible raster area before rendering; rejection regressions cover these limits.

finding.summary: Draft is discarded even when the commit engine command fails, causing loss of unsaved edits.
finding.evidence: In `commit`, `let result = s.execute("type.path.commit", params).map(|_| ()); self.cancel(); result`. If `s.execute` returns an `Err` (e.g., stale revision, engine error), `self.cancel()` is still called, clearing `self.draft`, `self.preview`, `self.overlay`, and `self.synced`. The user's typed changes are lost and cannot be retried.
finding.fix: Only cancel after a successful execute, or keep the draft on error so the user can retry. For example: `let result = s.execute(...).map(|_| ()); if result.is_ok() { self.cancel(); } result`

note: Path Text keeps its draft/preview after a failed engine publication and clears them only after success.

finding.summary: matches! attempts to move a non-Copy LayerContent out of a shared reference, causing a compile-time error.
finding.evidence: detached.layers.last().unwrap() returns &Layer, and .content is LayerContent. Since LayerContent has a Group variant containing a Vec (or similar non-Copy data), LayerContent is not Copy. The matches! macro consumes the expression by value, so this attempts to move out of a shared reference and fails to compile with E0507.
finding.fix: Match by reference instead, e.g.: assert!(matches!(&detached.layers.last().unwrap().content, LayerContent::Group(_)));

note: matches! on this place expression inspects the enum discriminant without moving its payload. The pinned Rust compiler accepts the test.

finding.summary: Off-by-one in dab budget check rejects exactly MAX_DABS dabs
finding.evidence: After pushing a new sample, code checks `if next.dabs.len() >= MAX_DABS` and returns an error when the length equals MAX_DABS. This prevents reaching the documented maximum; users cannot use exactly MAX_DABS dabs. The sample budget check uses `>=` before push, allowing exactly MAX_SAMPLES samples, showing inconsistency.
finding.fix: Change condition to `if next.dabs.len() > MAX_DABS` to allow exactly MAX_DABS dabs.

note: Exactly MAX_DABS is accepted. Additional work is preflighted before mutation and rejected atomically; added exact-limit regression.

finding.summary: Simplification silently discards extra subpaths returned by simplify
finding.evidence: The code calls `photocraft_pathops::simplify(&single, tolerance)` which returns a `Path` that can contain multiple subpaths. It then does `fitted.subpaths.into_iter().next()` and assigns only the first subpath to `*sp`, discarding any additional subpaths. If simplify splits a contour into multiple parts (plausible for complex geometry), those parts are lost, resulting in data loss.
finding.fix: Check that `fitted.subpaths` has exactly one element, or merge/handle all resulting subpaths by inserting them into `out.subpaths` appropriately.

note: Liquify simplification now requires exactly one output contour rather than silently dropping additional contours.

finding.summary: Zip assumes equal number of subpaths in output and base, causing missing attributes/simplification
finding.evidence: `for (sp, old) in out.subpaths.iter_mut().zip(&self.base.subpaths)` is used at lines 116-118 and 122-131. If `out.subpaths.len() != base.subpaths.len()`, the zip silently iterates only over the shorter length. Extra output subpaths do not receive the `op` attribute from base, and if simplify is active, they are skipped entirely, leaving them unsimplified and possibly causing later validation to fail.
finding.fix: Explicitly check that `out.subpaths.len() == base.subpaths.len()` at the start of `path()`, or handle mismatched counts by mapping subpaths differently (e.g., by original index if available).

note: The liquify kernel retains the input subpath vector and edits its anchors in place. It does not add/remove contours before the checked simplification stage.

finding.summary: Cloning Dabber on every push leads to O(n²) allocation on hot path
finding.evidence: `let mut next = self.dabber.clone();` clones the entire Dabber each time a sample is pushed. Dabber likely contains vectors of dabs and samples, so each push copies all previously accumulated data, causing total O(n²) work over a stroke. With MAX_SAMPLES=4096, this is about 8 million element copies per stroke, and repeated strokes can degrade UI responsiveness.
finding.fix: Avoid cloning by pushing to the internal Dabber directly and rolling back on error, or by computing dabs incrementally without full clone.

note: Dabber preflights the appended work without cloning its retained samples/dabs; rejection leaves the prefix unchanged. Added atomicity regression.

finding.summary: Zero-length track causes division by zero for floating point, producing NaN and corrupting geometry.
finding.evidence: pos = t.cum[i] / t.len(); if t.len() is 0.0 (e.g., a track with a single vertex or duplicate points), this evaluates to 0.0/0.0 = NaN. The NaN pos is then passed to widths(stroke, *s) in lines 58-59, leading to NaN coordinates for left/right samples and an invalid Path.
finding.fix: Guard against zero-length tracks before processing, for example `if t.len() <= f64::EPSILON { return Err(Error::Degenerate); }` or skip the track.

note: Track::new removes duplicate vertices and rejects fewer than two distinct vertices, guaranteeing positive track length before calligraphic projection.

finding.summary: Clicking 'Cancel Repeat Preview' while a preview is dirty commits the change instead of cancelling.
finding.evidence: `finished |= ui.input(|i| i.key_pressed(Key::Enter) || (i.pointer.primary_released() && state.dirty));` makes `finished` true on any pointer release when `state.dirty` is set. The commit block at lines 221-227 runs before the Cancel button at lines 235-237, so releasing the pointer over the Cancel button triggers `commit`, clearing `state.dirty` and `state.panel`, and then `state.cancel()` on the button has no effect. The document is modified against the user's explicit cancel action.
finding.fix: Move the Cancel button handling before the commit block, or restrict `finished` to focus/drag-stopped events and Enter, not every pointer primary release.

note: Repeat Cancel is evaluated before automatic field publication and wins; arbitrary pointer release no longer commits a dirty panel draft.

finding.summary: Canvas handle drags are cancelled after one frame if no widget has keyboard focus.
finding.evidence: The cancel condition `!i.focused` is true whenever egui has no focused widget. Starting a drag on a repeat handle does not request focus (the paint code uses `Sense::hover()` at line 384), so on the frame after `state.drag` is set, `state.captured()` is true and `!i.focused` is true, causing `state.cancel()` and `return`. The drag never receives subsequent motion events.
finding.fix: Do not treat lack of focus as cancellation. Instead cancel only on Escape, PointerGone, WindowFocused(false), or when `synchronize` detects invalid capture/selection. If focus loss cancellation is desired, track focus on the canvas widget specifically.

note: InputState::focused is window focus, not keyboard widget focus. Canvas drags are preserved while the window is focused.

finding.summary: `target_bounds` clones every selected layer on every frame, causing per-frame allocations in the canvas input/paint hot path.
finding.evidence: `let layers = ids.iter().map(|id| st.doc.layer(*id).cloned()...).collect::<Result<Vec<_>>>()?;` clones entire layer structures. `canvas` calls `input` (line 326) then `paint` (line 378), both call `target_bounds`, so at least two full clones of selected layers per frame. For complex vector layers this can cause UI lag.
finding.fix: Compute bounds without cloning, e.g., by borrowing layers or extracting only the needed bounds data; or cache bounds and invalidate on document/revision changes.

note: The single selected repeat/layer bounds path now borrows the source layer/children. Multiple selections copy only when a new repeat is explicitly requested.

finding.summary: Panic when rows or cols is zero (e.g. 1-pixel-wide/high image or 1x1 mesh).
finding.evidence: `((su.floor() as i64).clamp(0, cols as i64 - 1), ...)` computes `cols as i64 - 1` = -1 when `cols == 0`; `i64::clamp` panics if `min > max`. A 1×1 or 1×N image yields `cols == 0` and/or `rows == 0`.
finding.fix: Use saturating arithmetic to avoid negative bounds: `(su.floor() as i64).clamp(0, cols.saturating_sub(1) as i64)` and `(sv.floor() as i64).clamp(0, rows.saturating_sub(1) as i64)`. This collapses the degenerate dimension.

note: EnvelopeSpec validation requires nonzero rows/columns and exact grid size before the private grid evaluator is called. Pixel dimensions do not set grid dimensions.

finding.summary: Dragging a newly added width point inserts duplicate points on every pointer move
finding.evidence: In move_drag, for added points (when the user clicks on the center line to add an inherited width point), d.origin is the gesture before the point insertion, and d.added remains true throughout the drag. Each call to move_drag clones d.origin and calls set_point with None (line 198). The initial insertion from down is not reflected in d.origin, so each pointer movement triggers another insertion at the same t, producing multiple duplicate width points in the profile.
finding.fix: After the initial insertion in down, store the resulting index in the Drag struct (e.g., update d.selection.index and set d.added=false immediately), or use the current self.gesture as the base for updates, or pass Some(inserted_index) to set_point in move_drag.

note: The width capture updates the retained newly inserted point by its selected index. Its add/drag regression checks one point across multiple moves.

finding.summary: UI can stop repainting while a preview result is pending in the channel, leaving stale preview or no preview until the user interacts.
finding.evidence: In show(), the repaint condition only checks self.preview_job and self.apply_job. However, self.preview_rx may be Some when a preview job has completed but the result has not yet been received (e.g., Started::Done or job removed before channel message is ready). In poll(), preview_job is set to None when the job is no longer active, but preview_rx remains Some until try_recv succeeds. If the message arrives after that frame and no repaint is requested, the channel result will never be read until an external event causes a new frame.
finding.fix: Add self.preview_rx.is_some() to the repaint condition: if state.preview_job.is_some() || state.apply_job.is_some() || state.preview_rx.is_some() { ctx.request_repaint_after(...); }

note: Trace requests repaint while a preview receiver is pending, including the gap after the worker finishes and before UI result polling.

finding.summary: Unvalidated rect can cause negative area, leading to huge allocation and panic.
finding.evidence: In render_rgba, the check `if r.size().area() > 1_048_576` does not reject negative area. If `r.x1 < r.x0` or `r.y1 < r.y0`, `r.size().area()` is negative. Casting a negative number to usize (`r.size().area() as usize`) wraps to a very large value, and `vec![[0.; 4]; ...]` attempts to allocate an enormous buffer, causing a panic (capacity overflow or OOM).
finding.fix: Validate that the area is non-negative and within budget before casting, e.g., `let area = r.size().area(); if area <= 0 || area > 1_048_576 { return Err(Error::Budget); }`

note: PixelRect::size uses width/height clamped to zero for inverted extents; its area cannot become negative. Large positive areas are rejected before allocation.

finding.summary: Unbounded recursion in max_document_id can cause stack overflow on deeply nested layer trees.
finding.evidence: The function `layers` recursively calls itself via `l.children().map_or(0, layers)`. `project_document` calls `max_document_id(source)` at line 320 before any depth validation. A malicious file with a deeply nested group hierarchy (e.g., depth 10,000) will reach this code and overflow the stack, crashing the application.
finding.fix: Add a depth limit or convert the traversal to an iterative stack (e.g., a Vec of slices to visit) while computing the maximum ID.

note: Maximum document ID scanning is iterative and includes symbol definitions, avoiding unbounded recursion.

finding.summary: Unbounded recursion in prepare_caches::render can cause stack overflow on deep documents.
finding.evidence: The nested function `render` recursively calls itself for every child via `render(children, format, bounds, patterns)?` without checking depth. `prepare_caches` is a public function and may be called on a document that has not been depth-limited (unlike the `project_document` pipeline which eventually limits depth to 16, but only after `max_document_id` has already run). A sufficiently deep document will cause a stack overflow.
finding.fix: Add a depth limit parameter to `render` and return an error if the limit is exceeded, or convert the traversal to an iterative approach.

note: Blend cache preparation checks document depth before walking and bounds recursive rendering. Added excessive-depth rejection regression.

finding.summary: Error computation ignores NaN distances, allowing inadequate curve fit when mapping has interior singularities
finding.evidence: The fold (1..32).map(|i| { ... map(c.eval(t)).distance(fitted.eval(t)) }).fold(0., f64::max) uses f64::max which ignores NaN. If any sampled mapping point is non-finite (e.g., due to division by zero inside the closure), the distance becomes NaN and is silently discarded, so the maximum error can be underestimated. The condition error <= tol * 0.5 may then pass even though the fitted curve does not accurately represent the mapping, leading to incorrect path output.
finding.fix: Before folding, explicitly check each sampled distance for finiteness; if any distance is non-finite, return Err(Error::Invalid). For example, collect into a variable and use a loop with a check, or map to Option and use try_fold.

note: Mapped-curve error measurement rejects nonfinite distances explicitly instead of allowing max reduction to hide NaN.

finding.summary: Initial mapped point is not validated for finiteness, so open single-knot paths can bypass validation and result in invalid coordinates
finding.evidence: For an open subpath with n == 1, segs becomes 0, so the loop `for i in 0..segs` is skipped and no call to `fit` occurs. The initial point `point` is created from `f(first.anchor)` without checking `number(point.x, -MAX_COORDINATE, MAX_COORDINATE)` or similar. If `f` returns NaN or Inf, `doc_point` may propagate it (or even panic if it clamps), and `validate_path` may not catch numeric invalidity. This results in a path with non-finite coordinates being returned.
finding.fix: After computing `point`, validate it with the same `number` check used in `fit`; if invalid, return `Err(Error::Invalid)`. Alternatively, ensure `validate_path` rejects non-finite coordinates.

note: Final validate_path checks every mapped anchor and handle, including a single-knot output.

finding.summary: Bridge to an endpoint via endpoint-to-curve does not mark that endpoint as used, allowing the same endpoint to be bridged multiple times.
finding.evidence: For each endpoint a, ops::nearest on another shape can return q that is itself an endpoint of an open subpath. The candidate is pushed with b=None (line 41). Processing only inserts a into used (lines 55-58), not q's endpoint index. A later candidate whose a is that other endpoint will pass the used.contains check and create a second bridge incident to it, producing e.g. A-B and B-C with B connected twice, violating the one-bridge-per-endpoint invariant implied by used.
finding.fix: When q corresponds to an existing endpoint from ends, set b to Some(index) instead of None, or additionally mark that endpoint as used. This can be done by comparing q to each ends[k].3 (or using the subpath/knot indices returned by ops::nearest).

note: The candidate loop inserts endpoint a into used before handling endpoint-to-curve bridges, so each endpoint is reserved once.

finding.summary: Endpoints that already lie on another subpath of the same shape are not detected, so they are treated as dangling and a spurious bridge is added.
finding.evidence: The endpoint-to-curve loop continues when i == j (line 33). For a shape with multiple subpaths, an endpoint of one subpath that lies exactly on another subpath of the same shape is already connected (not dangling). Because nearest is never called on the same shape's other subpaths, no d<=1e-7 zero candidate is generated for it, so it can be bridged to an unrelated curve within gap distance.
finding.fix: For the same shape, query nearest on all subpaths except the one containing the endpoint, and if distance <= 1e-7 mark the endpoint as used (push a zero candidate) just like for other shapes.

note: Gap detection checks other subpaths of the same source while excluding only the endpoint's own subpath, preventing bridges from attached endpoints.

finding.summary: Proportional art brush ignores stroke.base.width in cross-scale, causing art thickness not to scale with stroke width.
finding.evidence: Line 144 defines cross = stroke.base.width * a.width. In bend line 127, this cross is divided by stroke.base.width via (l+r)/stroke.base.width, so it must be a length. For Proportional, line 147 overrides cross with l / w * a.width, omitting the stroke.base.width factor. With base_width != 1.0, output cross displacement is wrong by that factor.
finding.fix: Use (l / w) * f64::from(stroke.base.width) * a.width (or l / w * cross) for ArtScale::Proportional.

note: ArtScale::Proportional intentionally uses the along-axis scale for both dimensions; Stretch and BetweenGuides use stroke width for cross scaling.

finding.summary: Dense sampling of art segments never includes u=1.0, so the final endpoint of open art subpaths is omitted.
finding.evidence: params starts as (0..steps).map(|j| j as f64 / steps as f64), which yields [0, 1/steps, ..., (steps-1)/steps]; split insertion only adds u in (0,1). For each segment only its start is emitted; the next segment's start supplies the previous endpoint, but the last segment's endpoint is never added. Open art brush strokes therefore end before the intended final vertex.
finding.fix: Change range to (0..=steps) and collect steps+1 params, or explicitly push 1.0 before mapping.

note: Art-brush validation requires closed contours with at least three knots. Open art is rejected before bend; a closed contour's final endpoint repeats its first.

finding.summary: PatternBrush with zero scale (or zero stroke width) makes tw + gap == 0, causing raw = inf and n to saturate to usize::MAX; then n + out.paths.len() can overflow.
finding.evidence: tw = side.bounds.width() * k, gap = tw * pb.spacing. If pb.scale == 0 (or stroke.base.width == 0), k = 0, so tw = gap = 0. With avail > 0, raw = (avail + gap) / (tw + gap) = inf. raw.round().max(1.) as usize saturates to usize::MAX. At line 295, n + out.paths.len() overflows (panic in debug) once out.paths is non-empty; even when out.paths is empty it returns Error::Budget instead of producing an empty pattern.
finding.fix: Guard tw + gap <= 1e-9 and skip/return or clamp n to a safe limit before the addition.

note: Brush/appearance validation rejects zero/nonfinite scale and nonpositive stroke width before pattern placement.

finding.summary: Scatter with zero or negative spacing does not break on open tracks and pushes duplicate positions until Budget error.
finding.evidence: step = b.width() * size * spacing. If step <= 0 (e.g. scatter spacing range includes 0 and size > 0), for an open track pos is 0 or negative, so pos > t.len() + 1e-9 never fires and t.closed is false. Each loop iteration sets s = Some(pos) and calls out.push; it only stops when Output::push returns Error::Budget. This can generate up to MAX_PIECES duplicate zero-size/degenerate paths.
finding.fix: After computing step, if step <= 1e-9 (or after signed step check) break or return a clear error before entering the placement loop.

note: Scatter validation requires finite positive spacing before this private placement loop.

finding.summary: Edges from the last source are dropped and remaining source edges are misattributed when using shape_builder (any open path) because source keys are 1-based but the filter treats them as 0-based indices.
finding.evidence: Line 187 assigns `inputs.push(ops::Shape::new(shape.path.clone(), slot as u64 + 1))`, so keys for n sources are 1..=n. Line 234 filters `e.key < sources.len() as u64`, which excludes key n (the last source). Additionally, line 235 uses `e.key` as an index into `inputs` and `sources`, but since `e.key` is 1-based, indexing `inputs[key]` retrieves the next input, misattributing the edge's source for keys 1..n-1. The native branch (all closed) uses 0-based keys and works correctly, making the inconsistency clear.
finding.fix: Use 0-based keys consistently: assign `slot as u64` (not +1), and adjust filter to `e.key < sources.len()`; or if keeping 1-based, change filter to `e.key >= 1 && e.key <= sources.len() as u64` and index with `(e.key - 1) as usize`.

note: Planar::try_shape_builder explicitly rekeys input shapes to zero-based slots. Region and edge source indices correctly use those slots; added multi-source regression.

finding.summary: LivePaintSpec::set_face and set_edge mutate the spec before full validation, leaving an over-budget or duplicate spec on error.
finding.evidence: In `set_face`, if the signature is new, `self.faces.push(...)` is executed (line 76), then `self.validate()` (line 78) is called. If validation fails (e.g., budget exceeded), the method returns Err, but the pushed record remains, so the spec now has `faces.len() > MAX_REGIONS*2` and is in an invalid state. Similar in `set_edge` (line 84). Callers may assume atomic failure.
finding.fix: Validate the proposed state before mutating, e.g., clone the spec, apply change, validate, then replace; or at minimum check budget and duplicate before push, then roll back on unexpected validation errors.

note: Live Paint face/edge edits validate a cloned candidate before publication, leaving the original spec unchanged on errors. Added atomicity regression.

finding.summary: touched performs O(points * faces * segments) intersection tests without a broad-phase check, which can block the UI during paint gestures.
finding.evidence: For every pair of consecutive points, it iterates over all faces (line 285) and for each face iterates all its bezier segments and intersects with the line (line 287-288). With MAX_POINTS=4096 and MAX_REGIONS=2048, worst-case is ~8 million face iterations per gesture, each with multiple segment intersections. This method is likely called on pointer move, causing frame drops.
finding.fix: Add a quick bounding-box rejection: before segment intersection, check if the face's `bounds` intersects the line's bounding box; or use a spatial index (e.g., quad tree) to query faces near the segment.

note: Touched-face testing skips already found faces and rejects disjoint face/gesture bounding boxes before intersecting boundary segments.

finding.summary: fill() clears gradient midpoints when stop counts differ, so t=0 or t=1 does not reproduce the input gradient.
finding.evidence: In the `sa.len()!=sb.len()` branch, `midpoints.clear()` is called after resampling stops. If t=0, the output starts as `a.clone()` but loses `a`'s custom midpoints; colors at sample positions are from `color(sample(...), sample(...), 0)` (so `a`'s colors), but the new gradient uses default midpoint 0.5 between the resampled stops, producing different interpolated colors than the original `a`.
finding.fix: Special-case t==0.0/t==1.0 to return `a.clone()`/`b.clone()`, or preserve/recalculate midpoints so the piecewise interpolation matches.

note: Fill interpolation returns exact input clones at t=0 and t=1, including unequal gradient stop counts and midpoints. Added endpoint regression.

finding.summary: appearance() item type flips at t=0.5 when corresponding appearance items differ.
finding.evidence: `near` switches from `a` to `b` at t=0.5 and `out` contains only `near`'s item at each index. If `a` has Fill and `b` has Stroke at index 0, t=0.49 returns a Fill while t=0.5 returns a Stroke; no crossfade between types.
finding.fix: When x/y are different variants, add both near and far items to `out.items` and opacity-crossfade their visible/opacity, or otherwise make the transition continuous.

note: Discrete appearance item types intentionally switch at the midpoint; continuous interpolation applies only to compatible paint/geometry fields.

finding.summary: distance() ignores extra gradient colors because it zips two color vectors.
finding.evidence: `colors(a).iter().zip(colors(b))` only compares up to min length. A gradient with stops [red, blue] and another with [red, blue, green] compare equal because the third stop is ignored.
finding.fix: Compare all stops, e.g. flatten both color lists index-wise with a penalty for length mismatch, or iterate over max length with default/transparent.

note: Perceptual distance includes extra gradient colors instead of truncating to the shorter vector. Added additional-color regression.

finding.summary: distance() returns 0 between a Group and a non-Group layer, and ignores extra group children.
finding.evidence: `colors(group)` is empty because `stack` yields `Appearance::default()` for `LayerContent::Group`, and recursive comparison only runs when both contents are `Group`. A group versus a shape produces an empty zip and delta remains 0. When both are groups, `children.iter().zip(...)` at line 256 ignores unmatched children.
finding.fix: Collect colors from all leaf descendants regardless of layer content type and compare full sets; do not rely solely on zip of children.

note: Group/non-Group pairs are rejected. Unmatched group children collapse using their own retained paint, so they contribute no paint change to the spacing metric.

finding.summary: Flat-axis expansion in source_bounds can produce bounds outside MAX_COORDINATE, causing valid input near the coordinate limit to be rejected.
finding.evidence: A path with all anchor/control points at x = 1_000_000 (valid under validate_path) has zero width. source_bounds expands r.x0 to 999999.5 and r.x1 to 1000000.5 (lines 95-98). Map::with_tolerance then checks valid_point(Point::new(bounds.x1, bounds.y1)) and fails because 1000000.5 > MAX_COORDINATE, returning Error::Invalid for input that should be accepted.
finding.fix: Clamp the expanded frame to the valid coordinate range, e.g. use half_width = (MAX_COORDINATE - x.abs()).min(0.5) when expanding, or allow internal bounds to slightly exceed MAX_COORDINATE while still enforcing the limit on actual point input/output.

note: Flat source bounds expand inward at the coordinate limit, keeping valid source geometry within the allowed frame.

finding.summary: Inverted fill paints the path interior instead of the exterior because coverage is not inverted.
finding.evidence: For `shape.path.inverted` and fill items, line 238 sets bounds to `canvas`, but the coverage used in `render_rgba` is still `area.clone()` from line 213 (the non-inverted fill rasterizer). The render path at line 279 multiplies source alpha by this coverage directly. No inversion step exists. Thus an inverted fill renders the shape interior rather than the surrounding canvas.
finding.fix: When `shape.path.inverted` is true for a fill, use a coverage that is `1 - area` (or use a rasterizer that already handles inversion), or modify `fill_rasterizer` to return inverted coverage and adjust bounds accordingly.

note: Compiled fill/mesh coverage inverts for inverted paths before compositing. Added interior/exterior regression.

finding.summary: Per-tile per-item allocation of coverage buffers causes excessive memory churn and CPU overhead on large images.
finding.evidence: `render` loops over tiles (line 314-315) and calls `render_rgba` for each tile. Inside `render_rgba`, for every item, `let mut cov = item.coverage.render(rect);` allocates a new `Vec` of `rect.width()*rect.height()` floats. With up to 128 items and a 4K image (256x256 tiles = 256 tiles), this results in 32768 allocations of ~65536 floats each, totaling over 2 billion float operations during rendering.
finding.fix: Restructure rendering to precompute coverage per item and tile once, reuse buffers, or use a tile cache that renders all items for a tile in one pass without per-item allocation.

note: Coverage buffers are bounded per item and tile and required for ordered alpha compositing. Real raster and pointer performance gates measure this implementation.

finding.summary: Smooth handles can exceed MAX_COORDINATE, causing validate to reject valid input points.
finding.evidence: For points within [-MAX_COORDINATE, MAX_COORDINATE], the handle offset (next - prev)/6 can be up to (MAX - (-MAX))/6 = MAX/3.
